The intercostal neurovascular bundle was protected, and the parietal pleura was bluntly separated before each osteotomy to preserve pleural integrity. In the FC group, each rib was transected at two sites to create a four-rib flail segment; in the MRF group, a single transection was made per rib. Paradoxical chest wall motion was visually confirmed in the FC group before layered closure. Invasive arterial pressure, heart rate, pulse oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and end‑tidal carbon dioxide tension (ETCO₂) were monitored throughout. Chest CT was performed on Day 7.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All surgeries were successful, with no mortality. Paradoxical chest wall motion was confirmed in all FC animals after emergence. The SpO₂/FiO₂ ratio declined postoperatively in both groups, with a significantly greater decrease in the FC group than in the MRF group (221.0±1.4 vs. 260.2±1.9, P<0.001). Heart rate and mean arterial pressure increased in both groups and were significantly higher in the FC group (P<0.001). CT confirmed the intended fracture patterns and flail-segment displacement, with no evidence of pleural breach, pulmonary injury, pneumothorax, or hemothorax.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A standardized porcine flail chest model was established that preserves pleural, pulmonary, and neurovascular integrity, allowing the isolated study of rib fracture pathophysiology. This model will facilitate future research on fixation materials and surgical techniques.

abstract.label: STUDY TYPE
abstract.text: Basic Science/ Animal Study.

articles.title: Contemporary management of traumatic abdominal wall hernias: What you need to know.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.text: Traumatic abdominal wall hernia (TAWH) is an uncommon but clinically important consequence of both blunt and penetrating abdominal trauma. It is defined by disruption of the abdominal wall musculature and fascia with herniation of intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal contents through the defect. Although penetrating abdominal wall defects are usually apparent and can often be primarily closed during operative exploration, blunt TAWH is significantly more heterogeneous and challenging. The skin may remain intact while the muscle, fascia, neurovascular supply, and bony attachments are disrupted. The reported incidence of TAWH varies according to imaging strategy and trauma population, but frank herniation remains rare, occurring in <1% of blunt trauma patients in most contemporary series. The major management challenge is deciding whether the patient requires immediate trauma laparotomy or laparoscopy, acute abdominal wall repair, staged management with same-admission repair, or delayed hernia repair/abdominal wall reconstruction. Evidence remains primarily dominated by retrospective single-center series, multicenter registry studies, and systematic reviews with heterogeneous definitions and follow-up. Although traditional dogma had taught that these repairs should always be performed in a delayed fashion, recent multicenter data, systematic reviews, and surgeon experience suggest that timing of repair, type of repair, and mesh use must be individualized; bowel injury, contamination, defect location, and patient physiology are more important than a universal early-versus-delayed algorithm. This article summarizes the practical issues the trauma and acute care surgeon needs to know: diagnosis, classification, associated injuries, indications for exploration, repair timing, operative strategy, management of lateral and posterior defects, mesh use in contaminated fields, and associated outcomes.

articles.title: PERCUTANEOUS MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY: A NEW TOOL IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA.
articles.journal: Port J Card Thorac Vasc Surg
articles.journal_full: Portuguese journal of cardiac thoracic and vascular surgery

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) remains challenging due to nonspecific symptoms and signs that lead to a high mortality rate. Common causes include cardiac emboli and thrombosis of a mesenteric plaque.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To present a clinical case of acute mesenteric ischemia that underwent successful endovascular revascularization.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: 82-year-old female patient with a history of atrioventricular block, hypertension, and dementia. She was admitted to the emergency department for acute abdominal pain with onset 3 days before. Diagnosis of ischemic colitis secondary to acute superior mesenteric artery occlusion was confirmed by angioCT scan. Endovascular treatment was performed: percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy through left brachial access using the Rotarex® system (Straub Medical). She improved from her previous symptoms and was discharged at day 6, with no need of exploratory laparotomy.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION
abstract.text: AMI is a vascular emergency that requires rapid identification and treatment. There are two courses of action for mesenteric revascularization: open or endovascular. Some authors have demonstrated an advantage in the endovascular approach, with reduced morbidity and mortality, especially in an often aging and frail group of patients. The Rotarex® (Straub Medical) system fragments the thrombus and aspirates it at the same time, thus avoiding embolic phenomena at distance. Despite being a new technology, it has shown to be a very promising tool for AMI treatment due to its fast restoration of blood flow with minimal invasiveness.

articles.title: Bone microarchitecture, density, and strength assessment in automotive trauma patients using HR-pQCT: a pilot study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Automotive trauma patients enrolled in the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) typically undergo computed tomography (CT) imaging as part of emergency care. HR-pQCT is a noninvasive imaging technique that enables assessment of bone microarchitecture at the peripheral sites. CT and HR-pQCT can be used to estimate volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) and strength via finite element analysis (FEA). However, HR-pQCT's superior resolution (approximately 10 times higher than conventional clinical CT scanners) captures in vivo trabecular and cortical microarchitecture, enabling high fidelity FEA. This study examines HR-pQCT-derived bone microarchitecture and strength measurements in relation to fracture patterns, bone-related comorbidities, and CT-derived vBMD in CIREN trauma patients, while providing foundational evidence to support HR-pQCT use following motor vehicle crashes (MVC) and pedestrian crashes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Nine automotive trauma patients (ages 17-76; 78% female) enrolled at Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center from the National Highway Safety Administration's CIREN study participated in the HR-pQCT pilot study. HR-pQCT scans were acquired within 1-12 months following the patient's MVC (n = 7) or pedestrian crash (n = 2). Scans were acquired at four sites: 1) distal tibia, 2) diaphyseal tibia, 3) distal radius, and 4) diaphyseal radius. HR-pQCT normative percentiles were determined using Indiana University's calculator. Descriptive statistics were used to present HR-pQCT musculoskeletal outcomes based on bone-related comorbidities, BMI, and fracture incidence. Pearson correlations were performed between HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia and radius total vBMD and CT-derived total vBMD at the spine and femoral compartments.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At the distal tibia, participants without tibia and fibula fractures tended to show greater mean cortical thickness (1.63 ± 0.38 versus 1.15 ± 0.05 mm), cortical area (146.24 ± 46.07 versus 103.70 ± 1.70 mm2), cortical vBMD (943.83 ± 79.18 versus 861.05 ± 26.52 mg HA/cm3), and bone strength (10.25 ± 3.72 versus 7.00 ± 0.70 kN). Additionally, HR-pQCT-derived distal tibia total vBMD demonstrated a strong positive correlation with CT-derived femoral head total vBMD (r = 0.766; p = 0.045). Normative percentiles showed that participants with bone-related comorbidities had lower bone microarchitectural and strength percentiles than the group without comorbidities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study demonstrates the viability of HR-pQCT for characterizing bone microarchitecture, strength, and density in automotive trauma patients and identifying differences that might relate to fracture and bone-related comorbidities. These preliminary findings support incorporating HR-pQCT imaging into automotive crash research due to its ability to provide detailed cortical and trabecular microarchitectural measurements that are not available from clinical CT.

articles.title: Emergency medical services (EMS) professionals: Unpacking anxiety, burnout, depression, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and social support perceptions.

abstract.text: This study examined associations among burnout, mental health symptoms, and suicidal risk in emergency medical services (EMS) professionals. A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 315 EMS professionals (53.5% men, 45.4% women). Participants completed the Suicide Behaviors Questionnaire-Revised, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, and Maslach Burnout Inventory, along with demographic and work-related items. Burnout, anxiety, and depression were positively associated with suicidal risk. Higher scores on Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale subscales and Maslach Burnout Inventory domains corresponded with higher Suicide Behaviors Questionnaire-Revised scores, and suicidal risk differed across gender categories, with elevated scores among participants selecting a gender option outside the male/female binary. Findings underscore the interrelated nature of burnout and psychological distress in EMS professionals and support the need for accessible, evidence-based mental health interventions that address both individual symptoms and occupational stressors in EMS settings. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Preliminary Reliability and Validity of Asynchronous Speech Screening to Support Clinical Triage for Children With Cleft Palate and Velopharyngeal Dysfunction.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Children with cleft and craniofacial conditions require ongoing monitoring and evaluation to manage persistent speech and resonance disorders. Regular assessment allows clinicians to detect emerging problems, evaluate intervention efficacy, and adjust treatment plans accordingly. However, socioeconomic and logistical barriers place many children at risk for sporadic or absent follow-up, leading to undiagnosed or underaddressed velopharyngeal dysfunction. This pilot study examined the reliability and use of asynchronous speech and resonance screenings to identify children who need comprehensive imaging assessment versus those suitable for continued monitoring and local speech therapy.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Twenty children with repaired cleft palate and/or noncleft velopharyngeal dysfunction completed in-clinic speech evaluations, during which standardized audio-only and audio-video samples were simultaneously recorded using telephone and web-conferencing platforms. During the evaluation, speech samples were rated in real time using the Cleft Audit Protocol for Speech-Americleft Modification. Each of the 40 recording files, including 20 audio-only and 20 audio-video recordings, were blinded, randomized, and independently reviewed by two asynchronous raters, yielding 80 asynchronous rating events. Interrater agreement and reliability were evaluated using percentage agreement and unweighted kappa coefficients across modalities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Across parameters and modalities, asynchronous ratings closely approximated in-person ratings. Reliability was very good for intelligibility and acceptability (κ = .81-.83), good for resonance and cleft speech characteristics (κ = .63-.75), and moderate for audible nasal emission and weak pressure consonants (κ = .45-.57). Asynchronous raters demonstrated high agreement with in-person ratings for therapy recommendations (80%-85%; κ = .57-.69) and clinical triage decisions (70%-90%; κ = .41-.79).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Preliminary findings support the feasibility and reliability of asynchronous speech and resonance screening to inform clinical triage decisions. Audio-only and audio-video recordings yielded generally comparable ratings and triage recommendations, with video offering potential added value for select speech features. Future development of asynchronous monitoring platforms has promise for reducing unnecessary clinic visits, streamlining interventions, and ensuring timely follow-up for those in need of higher level care.

articles.title: Rule-Out yield of the European society of cardiology 0/1-Hour troponin protocol in frail and non-frail octogenarians.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the rule-out yield of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) algorithm for 30-day major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in emergency department (ED) patients aged ≥ 80 years, and explore whether frailty modifies performance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center cohort study included patients aged ≥ 80 undergoing 0/1-h hs-cTnI sampling for suspected acute coronary syndrome. Frailty was defined using the Clinical Frailty Scale (≥ 5). The prespecified primary outcome was the 30-day MACE miss rate in the rule-out stratum against a 1% threshold.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,136 screened encounters, 800 were analyzed (median age 83 years; 56.9% female); 312 (39.0%) were frail. Blinded re-abstraction of 80 records yielded kappa 0.82 (0.71-0.93) for frailty and agreement ≥ 0.71 across variables. The algorithm classified 120 patients (15.0%) as rule-out (prespecified target, 236); two had 30-day MACE (miss rate 1.7%; wide 95% Wilson CI, 0.5%-5.9%), an imprecise estimate whose upper bound exceeds the 1% threshold. A post hoc bounding analysis counting all 11 rule-out patients with incomplete nonfatal ascertainment as events raised the upper bound to 10.8% (6.4%-17.7%). Sensitivity was 99.0% and negative predictive value 98.3%. In prespecified exploratory analysis, no statistically significant independent association was observed between frailty and 30-day MACE (average marginal effect + 1.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.05 to + 7.20; p = 0.744).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The ESC algorithm ruled out only 15% of octogenarians, potentially reflecting baseline age- and renal-related troponin elevations. Limited rule-out sample size, wide confidence intervals, and incomplete follow-up prevent a definitive safety conclusion.

articles.title: Altered cholangiocyte subsets with neural pathway enrichment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

abstract.text: Hepatocytes have been extensively studied in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet the role of cholangiocytes remains underexplored. We utilized a comprehensive approach that integrates high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cellular interaction evaluation, machine learning techniques, immune cell infiltration analysis, and Mendelian randomization to investigate both single-cell sequencing data and bulk sequencing datasets. Single-cell analysis identified significant alterations in cholangiocyte subpopulations in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) patients, including an increase in cholangiocytes with elevated SEMA3 pathway expression. The hdWGCNA analysis identified the green module, which is enriched with genes associated with neural pathways pertinent to MASH. Seven machine learning models assessed the diagnostic feasibility of key genes in the green module for MASLD spectrum. Immune infiltration analysis highlighted complex interactions between cholangiocytes enriched for neural-related pathways and immune cells, particularly neutrophils and monocytes. Patient stratification identified two distinct subtypes within the MASLD spectrum, with subtype 2 exhibiting enhanced activity in neural-related pathways. Mendelian randomization analysis identified PLEKHA5 as a candidate causal gene for MASLD, suggesting a potential role in neural mechanisms (SEL1L3 showed a suggestive association, P = 0.0413). Collectively, this hypothesis-generating bioinformatics study elucidates distinct characteristics of cholangiocyte subpopulations in MASH, revealing neural pathway alterations that may contribute to disease pathogenesis and providing a foundation for future investigation into cholangiocyte-related mechanisms in MASLD.

articles.title: Comparison of low volume versus high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in people receiving haemodialysis: a randomized non-inferiority trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Colonoscopy in chronic kidney disease patients undergoing haemodialysis is crucial. Some concerns have been raised about the use of oral bowel cleansing agents for colonoscopy. We compared the efficacy, safety and tolerability of a low volume versus a high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in such patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multicentre, parallel-arm, randomized, phase IV trial with 15% non-inferiority margin was conducted. Eligible subjects were allocated to either the low volume (2 L) or high-volume (4 L) bowel preparation group in 1:1 ratio. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with adequate bowel cleansing. Secondary outcomes were polyp/adenoma detection rate (PDR/ADR), cecal intubation rate, patient tolerability/compliance and adverse events.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixty-nine patients were randomized in four centres, 35 to low and 34 to high-volume groups. No difference in caecal intubation rate, in patients with adequate preparation, was observed (96.7% vs 100%, p = 1). As per-protocol, adequate bowel preparation was achieved in the 69.7 and 63.0% of low and high-volume groups, respectively (p = 0.58). The mean Boston Bowel Preparation Scale was similar in the two groups (5.6 ± 2.4vs 5.4 ± 2.4, p = 0.51). The PDR was 39.4% in low volume and 37.0% in high volume (p = 1). No differences in adverse events were observed. No emergency dialysis sessions were required. Serum creatinine levels remained stable before and after preparation in both groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Optimal cleansing was difficult to obtain in haemodialysis patients. Both low and high-volume preparations were equally effective and safe. The small sample size is a limit underpowering our research. Larger studies are, therefore, required. Trial registration number The trial was approved by the Central ethic committee (protocol approval no. 0089971/23/11/2020) and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04709770.

articles.title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

articles.title: Overtriage of a physician-staffed prehospital emergency resource in Austria : An exploratory retrospective analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Appropriate emergency medical dispatch aims to balance rapid deployment of physician-staffed emergency medical services against unnecessary utilization of limited prehospital resources. Data on physician dispatch appropriateness in Austrian emergency medical services remain scarce. This study evaluated overtriage of a physician-staffed emergency medical response vehicle in Lower Austria.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective study included all primary dispatches of a physician-staffed emergency medical response vehicle between January and December 2022. Dispatches were retrospectively classified as appropriately triaged or overtriaged based on predefined criteria. Secondary objectives were overtriage across the 10 most frequent dispatch codes and the association between priority level and dispatch appropriateness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 3454 primary dispatches were analyzed and 2629 dispatches were classified as overtriage (76.1%; 95% confidence interval, CI 74.7-77.5%). Of these, 38.4% represented dispatches without patient contact and 37.7% were classified as low acuity overtriage, while only 23.9% (95% CI 22.5-25.3%) were retrospectively classified as appropriately triaged. The 10 most frequent dispatch codes accounted for 41.8% of all dispatches and demonstrated a combined overtriage rate of 77.1% (95% CI 74.8-79.2%). Priority level was not associated with physician dispatch appropriateness (ρ = -0.002, p = 0.92).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this study, over three quarters of physician-staffed emergency medical service dispatches did not meet the predefined retrospective criteria for physician involvement, although about half of these overtriaged cases were cancelled before physician-patient contact. Among cases with patient contact, 61% did not meet the predefined criteria for physician-level care. These findings highlight substantial potential to refine emergency physician-dispatch criteria.

articles.title: [The role of urology in pelvic trauma : Diagnosis and management of associated genitourinary injuries].

abstract.text: Pelvic fractures may be accompanied by injuries of the lower urinary tract which, although uncommon, are associated with considerable morbidity and long-term functional impairment. Optimal management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate treatment, and early integration of urological expertise into interdisciplinary trauma care. This review summarizes current evidence on the diagnosis and management of bladder and posterior urethral injuries associated with pelvic fractures, emphasizing the role of urology throughout clinical decision-making. Recommendations from the European Association of Urology (EAU), the American Urological Association (AUA), and the World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) are discussed in the context of key clinical studies. Beyond selecting appropriate diagnostic imaging and treatment strategies, the urological expertise plays an important role in interdisciplinary decision-making, particularly when urological management must be coordinated with pelvic ring stabilization, as well as in reconstructive management and structured long-term follow-up. Early urological involvement is therefore an integral component of interdisciplinary management aimed at minimizing complications and preserving long-term functional outcomes, including urinary continence, voiding and sexual function, and quality of life.

articles.title: The new trochanteric nail TFN-A has a higher complication rate in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures than the predecessor model PFN-A.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42-9.94; p = 0.004). No relevant differences were found regarding demographic data or the quality of reduction and internal fixation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The TFN-A had a significantly higher rate of complications leading to major revision than the former PFN-A. This may have been missed when considering only the reoperation rate for all causes due to a camouflage effect by minor complications.

articles.title: FOLFOX-Associated Ventricular Fibrillation Arrest in a Patient With Colon Cancer.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity is uncommon but may cause life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 43-year-old man with stage IIIB colon cancer developed chest discomfort and out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest approximately 72 hours after his first folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil (5-FU), and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) cycle. Electrocardiography showed anterior ST-segment elevations, but coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive left and right coronary arteries. Echocardiography showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 30%, which improved to approximately 50% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging without myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement. FOLFOX was discontinued, guideline-directed medical therapy was initiated, and an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for secondary prevention.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights a rare, severe presentation of fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity after the first treatment cycle despite no prior cardiac history.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Ventricular fibrillation may occur early during FOLFOX therapy. Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management are essential.

articles.title: Silent Hypoxemia in High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema: A Case Report.

abstract.text: We report a case of a trekker who ascended to Tilicho Lake (4919 m) from Kathmandu (1400 m) in 3 days. On day 3, he descended to Shree Kharka (4045 m). The following day, he trekked to Yak Kharka (4025 m) where, although he had no symptoms, he measured his own oxygen saturation (SpO2) at 72% in ambient air. Overnight, his SpO2 ranged from 75-80% on oxygen 2L/min via nasal cannula. The next day his SpO2 dropped to 47% while still on oxygen. He descended on horseback to Manang (3500 m), where his SpO2 was 70% on room air. He was diagnosed with high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). He was treated with oxygen, 4L by nasal cannula, and nifedipine. The following day, he flew to Kathmandu, where he made a full recovery. Trekkers may develop life-threatening HAPE without obvious symptoms or signs. Slow ascent can decrease the likelihood of developing HAPE, but trekkers do not always follow the recommended ascent rate. Early detection, by history and physical examination and with point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), if available, is critical in resource-limited regions such as ours. The keys to managing HAPE are early recognition and management, including descending to a lower altitude as soon as possible.

articles.title: Voluntary levamisole intoxication: a rare case of reversible neurological toxicity without cocaine co-ingestion.
Treatment patterns, healthcare utilization, and healthcare costs in patients with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes: a retrospective real-world study in Tianjin, China.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Data on healthcare among people with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in mainland China are limited. This real-world study evaluated treatment patterns, healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and healthcare costs among people with newly diagnosed T1D in Tianjin, China.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from a medical records database. The objective was to evaluate clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, HCRU, and healthcare costs in people with newly diagnosed T1D between January 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In total, 1396 people with newly diagnosed T1D were included (mean ± standard deviation age 30.6 ± 22.2 years; 38.8% aged <18 years [mean age 9 years]). At diagnosis, 70.3% required hospitalization or emergency care and 43.3% had diabetic ketoacidosis, with a higher prevalence in children and adolescents (65.7%). The three most common initial insulin regimens were insulin pump (30.4%), basal-bolus insulin (24.3%), and bolus insulin only (20.9%). During follow-up, the mean total all-cause HCRU was 14.32 clinical visits per person per year (PPPY) and the mean length of all-cause hospitalization was 14.14 days PPPY. Mean total all-cause healthcare costs were 28256.13 Chinese Yuan Renminbi (CNY) PPPY.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: People with T1D in Tianjin, China presented with severe conditions at diagnosis and had substantial ongoing HCRU and healthcare costs; actual costs may have been underestimated due to database limitations. These findings highlight the considerable clinical complexity and healthcare expenditure observed in individuals with T1D in China and emphasize the urgent need for effective strategies to improve T1D management and address the healthcare system burden.

articles.title: Subspecialty headache clinic visit reduced healthcare utilization in patients with migraine: Single institution retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to evaluate whether care in a subspecialty headache center, compared with a general neurology clinic, was associated with lower 90-day unplanned healthcare utilization (HCU) in patients with migraine and to identify patient-level factors associated with higher unplanned HCU.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Migraine is a common, disabling condition that frequently prompts emergency department (ED) evaluation and treatment. It ranks among the leading global causes of years lived with disability and imposes a substantial financial burden. People with migraine are most often managed in general neurology clinics rather than in specialty centers. Subspecialty headache centers can offer more advanced and guideline-based care, but their impact on post-visit HCU is not well defined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective cohort study of adults with a migraine diagnosis cared for at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center from 2018 to 2023. Unplanned HCU was defined as any ED visit, urgent care encounter, or hospital admission within 90 days after the index outpatient general neurology or subspecialty headache center visit (first qualifying migraine-coded encounter in the study period). Associations between clinic type and unplanned HCU were evaluated with adjustment for age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, Area Deprivation Index, and comorbidities, and, in a subset with available data, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System 16-item Profile (PROMIS-16) domains.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 38,472 patients included, 16,209 (42.1%) were evaluated in the subspecialty headache center. Total 90-day unplanned HCU was 12.6% in the subspecialty headache center vs. 15.4% in general neurology clinics (p < 0.001). Subspecialty headache center evaluation was associated with 15% lower odds of unplanned HCU (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79-0.90, p < 0.001). The association remained after accounting for patient characteristics (aOR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92) and PROMIS-16 domains (aOR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.59-0.76). Higher unplanned HCU was also associated with younger age at diagnosis, Medicaid and Medicare insurance/coverage, non-White races, comorbidities like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, and worse pain interference and physical function scores.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Evaluation in a subspecialty headache center was associated with approximately 15% lower odds of 90-day unplanned HCU. Subspecialized migraine care may represent a high-value care model.

articles.title: Adaptability of Medical Surge Preparedness Practices to Large-Scale Combat Operations.

abstract.text: Since its inception, the National Disaster Medical System (NDMS) has been activated in the context of acute-onset and time-limited disasters; however, its original intended purpose was for providing care for casualties from a large-scale combat operation (LSCO). Consequently, determining the utility of specific medical surge practices for an LSCO is necessary to optimally prepare the NDMS for such an event. Lessons learned from prior medical surge events can inform LSCO preparations despite the contextual differences between the 2 scenarios. This case study builds on earlier analyses by the US Department of Defense's NDMS Pilot program to develop a set of evidence-based leading practices for improving medical surge response that can be used by healthcare facilities providing acute care during LSCO-related patient surges.

articles.title: Essentials of Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship: Clinical Updates From the Past Decade.

abstract.text: Ten years ago, a comprehensive series of articles was published in Pediatric Emergency Care detailing the state of pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellowship education. We intend to provide an update to the clinical elements of fellowship training, with a companion article to follow that will address the nonclinical domains. This article will summarize the core components of fellowship as mandated by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) and review significant changes and challenges to fellowship education that have occurred over the past decade. In light of upcoming modifications to fellowship education, including an increased focus on competency-based medical education and the addition of a 2-year, clinically oriented fellowship option, it is vital for stakeholders to be familiar with the core elements of PEM fellowship training as the curriculum is adapted to meet the needs of trainees and their patients.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Vestibular Symptoms on the Vestibular Ocular Motor Screening for Return-to-play After Sport-related Concussion: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal_full: Journal of neurologic physical therapy : JNPT

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
abstract.text: The vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) contributes to gaze stabilization after head movement, but its independent prognostic value for return-to-play (RTP) after sport-related concussion (SRC) is unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined associations between early vestibular-ocular motor screening (VOMS) assessment and RTP duration following SRC.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, PEDro, and Cochrane Library to March 2025 identified studies assessing within 14 days of SRC and reporting RTP outcomes. Two reviewers extracted data and assessed the risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for studies reporting prolonged recovery (≥28-30 days).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twelve studies (N = 3297 athletes) met inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis of four studies (n = 968) found a positive VOMS screen was associated with increased odds of prolonged recovery (odds ratio 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.82-3.13; P < 0.00001; I 2 =0%). Among nine studies of isolated VOR gain, eight reported significant univariate associations with longer RTP, but only two retained significance after multivariable adjustment. VOMS reliably identifies athletes at risk for protracted recovery, but isolated VOR measures show inconsistent independent predictive value after adjustment.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Objective VOR gain quantification (eg, vHIT, caloric) is needed to clarify whether physiological VOR dysfunction independently affects recovery. Clinicians should interpret VOR findings within a multimodal assessment.

articles.title: Exploring the difference between self-harm and suicidal ideation among older people who present to emergency departments: national cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Older people have higher rates of death by suicide, and both self-harm and suicidal ideation are major risk factors for suicide. There is limited data relating to this group internationally.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to identify the clinical and sociodemographic variables associated with psychiatric admissions for older people who present with self-harm and suicidal ideation to emergency departments in Ireland.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This is a cohort study of older people in Ireland, utilising data collected by the National Clinical Programme for Self-Harm and Suicide-Related Ideation (NCPSHI). It is a national data-set including anonymised data from all participating emergency departments in Ireland, comprising 72 810 presentations over 5 years (2018-2020). We examined the characteristics of people aged over 60 presenting with self-harm and suicidal ideation (n = 4866). The variables associated with suicidal ideation and behaviours were explored using multivariable analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nationally, 7% of the patients presenting were aged over 60 years. One-quarter (26.8%) of older people presenting with self-harm required psychiatric admission (16.3% all-ages). On multivariable analysis, the relationship between self-harm and psychiatric admission was not statistically significant (reference group was those with suicidal ideation), after controlling for gender, year of presentation, substance use and need for medical admission odds ratio 0.977 (CI0.936-1.020).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our results outline the characteristics of older people presenting to Irish emergency departments with self-harm and suicidal ideation, which are associated with psychiatric admission. Further research is needed to understand the factors driving these presentations and to tailor our services to meet the needs of older people.

articles.title: Transient neurobehavioral dysfunction secondary to oxygen induced convulsion is not related to cerebral blood flow reduction.

abstract.text: This study aimed to investigate changes in blood flow following hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) exposure and their association with neurobehavioral dysfunction after oxygen-induced convulsions. Eighteen male C57 mice were randomly assigned to an oxygen toxicity (OT) group, a 40-m group, and a 15-m group (n = 6 per group). After the chamber was flushed with pure oxygen, mice were pressurized at a rate of 100 kPa/min. Mice in the OT group were exposed to 100% oxygen at 500 kPa until convulsions occurred; mice in the 40-m group were exposed to 100% oxygen at 500 kPa for 10 min without developing convulsions; and mice in the 15-m group were exposed to 100% oxygen at 250 kPa for 30 min without developing convulsions. After exposure, mice were decompressed at a rate of 100 kPa/min. Neurobehavioral function was assessed using the Y-maze test before exposure and at different time points after exposure. Cerebral blood flow (CBF) and femoral blood flow (FBF) were also measured, and the associations between changes in blood flow and neurobehavioral alterations were further evaluated. Results showed oxygen-induced convulsions significantly impaired spatial memory, whereas hyperbaric hyperoxia exerted differential effects on spatial memory, locomotor activity, and exploratory activity. These neurobehavioral alterations were transient and largely recovered within several hours after exposure. CBF decreased significantly immediately after HBO exposure, with a more pronounced reduction in mice exposed to 500 kPa, and subsequently recovered toward baseline levels. FBF also decreased after exposure although the changes were less pronounced. No significant association was observed between post-exposure CBF reduction and neurobehavioral dysfunction. In conclusion, oxygen-induced convulsions cause transient spatial memory impairment, whereas neurobehavioral dysfunction following HBO exposure is not directly associated with the reduction in CBF.

articles.title: Incidence of severe mountain bike-related injuries and mortality: A 15-year statewide analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mountain biking has grown in popularity and has seen widespread trail development but carries risk for severe trauma. No studies have analysed severe injuries in the context of contemporary mountain biking to understand trends and modifiable risk factors.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To describe the incidence and longitudinal characteristics of severe injuries related to mountain biking in Tasmania, Australia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis of all patients admitted to Tasmanian public hospitals with severe mountain bike (MTB)-related injuries from 1st January 2010-31 st December 2024.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Incidence of severe MTB-related injuries (including mortality) as defined by hospital admission to an intensive care unit or neurosurgery high dependency unit; for emergency surgery (in <4 h); or transfer intra- or interstate for definitive treatment. Secondary outcomes were annual injury trends in mechanism of injury, body regions, injury profiles, and incident location.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: For the total period there were 85 severe injuries (including 4 mortalities) from 6643 MTB-related emergency department (ED) presentations. Annual severe MTB-related cases increased over the 15 years from 0.8 cases/year before 2015, to 8.1 cases/year in later years. Severe injury cases accounted for only 1.3% of all MTB-related ED presentations. Most severely injured riders were male (97%); the mean age was 36 years (SD 16.9) for the total period, but this increased from 18.5 years (SD 5.8) pre-2015-36.9 years (SD 16.8) post-2015. Executing a jump was the dominant mechanism of injury (44%), followed by fall over handlebars (14%), obstacle collision (11%) and adverse trail conditions (9%). The most injured body regions were abdomen (31%), neck (23%) and thorax/chest (20%). The most common types of injuries were fracture/dislocation (44%), abdominal organ injury (24%) and thoracic organ injury (15%). Spinal cord injury occurred in 6% of cases and traumatic brain injury in 7%. Over 50% of severe injury incidents occurred on purpose-built MTB trails.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Severe MTB-related injuries increased proportionally to all MTB-related injuries suggesting the increase was largely driven by rider exposure. Targeted injury prevention strategies, safe trail design, and understanding risk factors are needed to ensure safe progression of this popular sport.

articles.title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pilon fractures frequently involve small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments that are susceptible to shear displacement and may not be reliably controlled by conventional periarticular plates. Rim plating is a fragment-specific, low-profile juxta-articular buttress technique that has demonstrated favorable biomechanical and clinical results in selected tibial plateau fracture patterns. This review examines the rationale for extending this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies describing rim-based constructs in tibial plateau fractures, with emphasis on hyperextension and posterolateral patterns, as well as computed tomography (CT)-based studies of pilon fracture morphology and fragment capture by precontoured plates. Relevant studies were identified through PubMed and reference screening and synthesized qualitatively to inform a technical proposal for adjunct rim plating in selected pilon fractures.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The reviewed tibial plateau literature consistently identified peripheral regions that may remain unsupported by conventional periarticular plates, particularly in hyperextension and posterolateral fracture patterns, where adjunct rim plating has been associated with maintained reduction and favorable clinical outcomes. In the distal tibia, CT-based studies suggest that commonly used anatomically precontoured plates may not reliably capture the anterolateral (Tillaux-Chaput) fragment when fragment height is less than 15 mm. In this setting, an adjunct rim plate may serve as a peripheral buttress to improve support of the articular margin, distribute subchondral stress, and prevent displacement of the articular block.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Rim plating may be best conceptualized as a joint-line buttress strategy for improving peripheral containment of shear-dominant marginal fragments. Extrapolation of this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns is mechanically plausible and supported indirectly by CT-based fragment-capture data. This technique may be useful in carefully selected anterior or anterolateral distal tibial rim fractures that are not adequately controlled by standard periarticular plating.

articles.title: A Structured Approach to Integrating Holistic Review Into Rank Order List Construction.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Residency programs are increasingly seeking to incorporate holistic review into the selection of applicants to interview, but its integration into the creation of the rank order list (ROL) remains less known.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We sought to develop a formula that reflects holistic review of an applicant by incorporating key application elements identified by the residency program and that aligns with the final submitted ROL.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: For the 2023-2024 application cycle, the leadership team from a single emergency medicine residency training program identified key attributes that characterized a successful resident. We then created a formula that weighted the identified elements to reflect our standard approach to applicant assessment. After submission of our ROL to the National Resident Matching Program, we compared the formula's performance to that of the final submitted ROL using linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 143 of 160 interviewed applicants placed on the final ROL and were analyzed. Seventeen applicants that were unranked or missing a Standardized Letter of Evaluation were excluded. The regression analysis showed that the rank formula closely approximated the final position on the ROL (β = -14.38, 95% CI 15.94 to -12.83; R 2 = 0.69; p < 0.0001). A higher rank score was strongly associated with a lower ROL number, which indicated a more favorable placement.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Using a ROL formula may consistently sort applicants post-interview and allow a leadership team to see when an applicant has moved outside their projected range, ensuring standardized placement on the ROL based on predefined attributes. We demonstrated a model that may assist in the comprehensive ranking of our residency applicants by incorporating elements of holistic review.

articles.title: Threading the Needle: Competing Contributors to Burnout in Emergency Medicine Residents.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency Medicine (EM) residents experience the highest rate of burnout of any specialty. Although there have been many proposed interventions, burnout remains highly prevalent. The purpose of this qualitative study was to explore how EM residents recognize, approach, and recover from burnout in order to inform future efforts to mitigate the burnout epidemic in trainees.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We interviewed 15 PGY 2-4 residents at four American EM residencies in 2023. We applied a grounded theory approach and a constructivist/interpretivist paradigm to explore participants' experiences through interactive dialogue and co-created interpretation. We invited participants to complete an online survey to collect demographics, information about their burnout experiences, and to schedule a virtual 60-min semi-structured interview, which we then transcribed, coded, and analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Analysis revealed three key tensions in the way EM residents experience burnout susceptibility versus recovery: coping by social connection versus withdrawal, perceiving burnout causes as societal versus individual, and seeing solutions to burnout as individual versus societal. Residents described withdrawing from others when experiencing burnout, yet believed that interpersonal connection could alleviate their symptoms. Viewing burnout primarily as the result of societal/organizational factors was protective. Solutions to burnout that felt most empowering to residents were individual. Perceiving burnout as the result of individual choices or seeing the solutions to burnout as requiring societal change worsened trainee distress.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Resilience to burnout requires residents to connect when they feel like withdrawing, and to take individual initiative when facing systemic obstacles. The difficulty of holding these intersecting views may explain the persistence of burnout and may prompt future studies to explore how residents who demonstrate these behaviors do so in times of stress.

articles.title: A narrative review of CBRN health sector preparedness in Lebanon.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: As chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) events become increasingly recognised within international and national emergency preparedness efforts, this study aims to provide the first system-level overview of Lebanon's preparedness capacities for CBRN-related health emergencies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature was conducted using a structured search strategy, with findings thematically synthesised to assess governance and operational CBRN preparedness capacities across eight health system domains in Lebanon.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The review identified important advances in Lebanon's preparedness for CBRN health emergencies, including engagement with international preparedness frameworks, development of governance structures, and implementation of coordination, training, and simulation initiatives. However, preparedness remains uneven and constrained by fragmented coordination, legislative gaps, limited surveillance and operational integration, shortages in material and human resources, and dependence on external support. Economic instability and workforce migration further challenge sustainability, while preparedness capacities and readiness levels vary across emergency response and healthcare institutions. Overall, strategic planning and governance capacities appeared stronger than operational response and surveillance functions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: While major efforts towards CBRN preparedness in Lebanon have been initiated, key aspects remain under-developed. Given Lebanon's continued exposure to recurrent crises and regional instability, strengthening CBRN preparedness should be considered a critical component of broader health system resilience and national disaster risk reduction efforts.

articles.title: Characteristics and outcomes of haemorrhage, traumatic brain injury and combined injuries from a South African Trauma Cohort Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To describe and compare injury severity, clinical management and mortality among haemorrhage, traumatic brain injury (TBI) and combined haemorrhage+TBI cohorts in a South African trauma population.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Secondary analysis of data from the Epidemiology and Outcomes of Prolonged Trauma Care (EpiC) multicentre observational cohort study, April 2021 to December 2024.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Six government health facilities and affiliated government ambulances across the Western Cape, South Africa.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: 18 840 adult patients with blunt and/or penetrating traumatic injuries enrolled in the EpiC registry were eligible for this secondary analysis. Patients <18 years of age and prisoners are excluded from EpiC. Burn injuries, non-haemorrhage and non-TBI injuries were excluded from this analysis. Patients were assigned to one of three mutually exclusive cohorts (haemorrhage, TBI or haemorrhage+TBI) using anatomic and physiologic criteria.

abstract.label: PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was crude, all-cause prehospital or in-hospital mortality. Mantel-Haenszel risk ratios (RRs) for mortality were adjusted for injury severity, injury force type and mode of prehospital transportation. Secondary outcomes included critical interventions, hospital admission, length of stay and time from injury to death.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 7614 patients met inclusion: 5146 (67.6%) haemorrhage, 1556 (20.4%) TBI and 912 (12.0%) haemorrhage+TBI. The majority were male (85.1%) with a median age of 31 years. Patients with haemorrhage+TBI received more intensive care, including airway interventions (38%), transfusions (41%) and intensive care unit admissions (36%). Crude mortality was highest in haemorrhage+TBI (31.3%), followed by TBI (7.7%) and haemorrhage (5.4%). After injury-pattern specific severity adjustment, mortality risk remained significantly higher in haemorrhage+TBI than in TBI (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.60 to 2.19) and haemorrhage (RR 3.38, 95% CI 2.96 to 3.85). Estimates were similar after additional adjustment for injury force and prehospital transportation (RR 1.84 and 2.98).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this South African population, haemorrhage+TBI was the least prevalent but most high-risk cohort with greater morbidity and mortality compared with haemorrhage or TBI alone, even after adjusting for injury severity. These findings may inform system level planning and resource allocation particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Adoption of Outpatient Management of Acute Low-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess longitudinal outcomes of a multicomponent intervention designed to address key barriers to the outpatient management of low-risk pulmonary embolism (PE), and to define the most appropriate target population and metric for evaluating adoption.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We implemented a multicomponent intervention in the emergency department (ED) of a quaternary academic medical center. Outcomes were evaluated using the RE-AIM framework, comparing a 3-year preimplementation period (2016-2019) with active implementation (year I), postimplementation (year II), and maintenance (year III) periods. The primary outcome (adoption) was the proportion of low-PESI (≤85) patients discharged from the ED. Following implementation, the charts of all hospitalized low-PESI patients were reviewed to determine reasons for admission.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,810 patients with acute PE, 705 (39.0%) had low-PESI scores. Adoption rose from 5.1% preimplementation to 16.1% (odds ratio [OR] 3.43, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.77 to 6.63), 24.0% (OR 5.98, 95% CI 3.04 to 11.78), and 33.3% (OR 9.24, 95% CI 5.04 to 16.92) in years I to III. There were no recurrent venous thromboembolism or deaths within 30 days of any ED discharge. Bleeding complications were rare (0%-4.3%) and none required hospitalization. Hospitalization decreased primarily among low-PESI patients without Hestia criteria, whereas admission of low-PESI Hestia-positive patients remained relatively constant. Excluding Hestia-positive cases, adoption increased from 9.0% preimplementation to 75% in the maintenance phase.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this single-center implementation study, a multicomponent intervention guided by RE-AIM resulted in a sustained increase in outpatient management of low-risk PE. Both the PESI score and Hestia criteria could be incorporated into the definition of the target population and future quality metrics.

articles.title: Clinical and patient-reported predictors of days alive and out of hospital in decompensated cirrhosis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Days alive and out of hospital (DAOH) is a patient-centered outcome, but has not been studied in decompensated cirrhosis (DCC). We aimed to quantify DAOH and to identify clinical and patient-reported factors associated with DAOH.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using an ongoing prospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with DCC, DAOH was calculated by subtracting days hospitalized, transplanted, or deceased from 90 days post-discharge from index hospitalization. Univariable and multivariable negative binomial hurdle models were used to identify clinical and patient-reported variables associated with DAOH, where DAOH was treated both as a categorical (any readmission, transplant, death vs. all 90-DAOH) and continuous (proportion of event days) outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 363 adults (median age 54 y; MELD 3.0 score 23), 40% experienced all 90-DAOH while 90-day readmission, death, and transplant occurred in 49%, 21%, 11%, respectively. Mean DAOH was 68.3 (SD: 29.0). In multivariable models, transplant evaluation status (listed vs. not listed/evaluated: OR 7.55, p=0.004) was associated with experiencing an event within 90 days. In comparison, when considering the number of event days, higher PROMIS Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities scores were independently associated with a lower proportion of event days (rate ratio, RR 0.91 per 3-point increase, p=0.030) in addition to MELD 3.0 >25 (vs. <15, RR 2.75, p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: DAOH is a holistic, patient-centered outcome for decompensated cirrhosis that integrates readmission, transplantation, and mortality into a single measure of post-discharge burden. By using DAOH and moving beyond readmissions, we show that lower MELD 3.0 and higher patient-reported social well-being were independently associated with more days at home after hospitalization.

articles.title: Sports-Related Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest due to External Causes, Including Commotio Cordis, at Schools in Japan.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: To describe the characteristics and outcomes of sports-related out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) due to external causes, including commotio cordis, during school-supervised sports activities in Japan's elementary schools, junior high schools, high schools, and technical colleges.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: OHCA data (2008-2022) were obtained from the Stop and Prevent cardIac aRrest, Injury, and Trauma in Schools (SPIRITS)-a nationwide database of OHCAs occurring under school supervision across Japan. We identified sports-related OHCAs with external causes and summarized patients' characteristics, bystander interventions, available response intervals, and survival outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 30 sports-related OHCA cases due to external causes. The most frequently played sports were soccer/futsal (n = 8), baseball (n = 8), and swimming (n = 4). The leading etiology was commotio cordis (n = 15), followed by drowning (n = 8). Among the 15 cases meeting our operational definition of commotio cordis, automated external defibrillator (AED) pads were applied in 14 (93%), shocks were delivered in 13 (87%), and 12 (80%) achieved a favorable neurological outcome. Among other external causes (n = 15), ventricular fibrillation occurred in 4/15 (27%), AED pads were applied in 7/15 (47%), shocks were rare (1/15, 7%), and 1/15 (7%) achieved favorable neurological outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Nationwide case-level reconstruction revealed distinct mechanism-to-response pathways. Although these descriptive data cannot establish the causal effects of the public access defibrillation programs or other interventions on outcomes, they highlight potentially actionable, mechanism-specific opportunities for emergency response and prevention.

articles.title: UEFA consensus guidelines on anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in women's football - Part Two: rehabilitation, return to play, and players' perceptions.

abstract.text: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries remain a major challenge to player health and performance in women's football. They are associated with lengthy rehabilitation, a high risk of re-injury, and potential long-term knee issues that can impact both career longevity and quality of life. Building on Part One of the UEFA consensus, which addressed risk factors and prevention, Part Two addresses the continuum of care after ACL injury, from rehabilitation to return to play (RTP) and beyond. A multidisciplinary panel of 26 experts in sports medicine, physiotherapy, orthopaedics, and performance science developed evidence-informed statements using a modified RAND-UCLA Appropriateness Method. Through three Delphi rounds, 180 statements were assessed and refined, resulting in consensus on 170 (94%). The panel supported a player-centred, criterion-based approach where progression relies on clinical and functional milestones rather than fixed timelines. Key recommendations emphasise restoring quadriceps strength as a central milestone, integrating neuromuscular and psychological readiness assessments, and adopting phased RTP protocols that gradually re-expose players to the physical and cognitive demands of the game. Psychological and social factors (fear of re-injury, motivation, communication, and support networks) are recognised as vital influences on recovery. These guidelines offer practical, evidence-based advice for medical and performance staff working in women's football. By combining scientific research with expert consensus, they support a holistic, collaborative approach to ACL rehabilitation aimed at protecting player health, lowering re-injury risk, and enabling a confident, sustained return to performance.

articles.title: Hospitalized primary headache in children after emergency department evaluation: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, management, and final diagnoses of children hospitalized for headache following emergency department (ED) evaluation, and to explore factors associated with treatment refractoriness.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 4-17 years presenting to a tertiary pediatric ED with headache as the primary complaint who required hospitalization between January 2019 and June 2024. Patients whose headache was clearly attributed to trauma, fever, or a previously identified systemic or neurological disorder were excluded. Final headache diagnoses were established during hospitalization by the pediatric neurology team, using ICHD-3 criteria when applicable. Data included demographics, clinical presentation, diagnostic testing, treatments, and discharge diagnoses. Descriptive analyses were performed, with exploratory comparisons between patients requiring ≤ 2 versus > 2 sequential pharmacologic interventions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 3,646 ED visits for headache, 162 (4.4%) resulted in hospitalization; 30 children (18.5% of admissions) had a final diagnosis of primary headache and constituted the study cohort. Mean age was 12.7 years, and 70.0% were female. Although frontal location and pressure-type pain were the most common presentation features, 76.7% of patients were ultimately diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine. Acute neurological abnormalities were documented in 10.0% of patients. Cranial CT was performed in 63.3% and brain MRI in 23.3%, with no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache identified. Intravenous metamizole (dipyrone) was the most frequently used first-line acute therapy, and 70.0% of patients required a second sequential pharmacologic intervention. Among patients diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine, 21.7% met criteria for status migrainosus. No clinical variables were significantly associated with treatment refractoriness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hospitalization for primary headache after pediatric ED evaluation was uncommon but identified a clinically severe subgroup, predominantly with migraine-spectrum disorders and frequently requiring escalation of acute treatment. Despite frequent neuroimaging, no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache was identified. These findings suggest that more selective imaging strategies may be appropriate in children with a reassuring clinical presentation, although prospective studies are needed to better define predictors of hospitalization, treatment refractoriness, and optimal acute management.

articles.title: Return-to-play with a solitary kidney after renal tumour.
Degrees of certainty: beyond threshold thinking in sport and exercise science.
Socioeconomic status and loss to follow-up after orthopedic trauma surgery.
articles.journal_full: Canadian journal of surgery. Journal canadien de chirurgie

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Follow-up after surgery is important, to monitor patient recovery and to identify potential complications. Our primary objective was to determine the association between patient socioeconomic status and loss to follow-up after orthopedic trauma surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 18 to 75 years who underwent orthopedic trauma surgery at a trauma centre in Ontario between January 2022 and December 2023. Patient socioeconomic status was determined by linking postal code with Material and Social Deprivation Index and presented as quintiles. We measured clinic follow-up attendance for 6 months after index surgery. We used logistic regression modelling to estimate the association between material deprivation quintiles and loss to follow-up, accounting for baseline patients and perioperative factors.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study cohort included 1764 patients. Approximately 1 in 4 patients missed at least 1 follow-up appointment in the 6 months after surgery. Odds of missed follow-up with no return were 83% higher in patients in the most deprived quintile, compared with patients who were least deprived (odds ratio 1.83, 95% confidence interval 1.09 to 3.08). Younger age and higher American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status score were associated with increased odds of loss to follow-up. Geographic distance to hospital was not independently associated with loss to follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Loss to follow-up is common after orthopedic trauma surgery, and the risk is higher in patients who are most socioeconomically disadvantaged. Innovative solutions should address the needs of specific patient groups to optimize patient access to appropriate, timely follow-up after orthopedic trauma surgery.

articles.title: Where should hip spica casting be performed for femoral shaft fractures in children aged 2-5 years: Emergency department or operating room? A retrospective comparative cohort study.

abstract.text: IntroductionThis study compared emergency department hip spica casting under procedural sedation with operating room casting under general anesthesia and fluoroscopic guidance for femoral shaft fractures in children aged 2-5 years.MethodsThis retrospective comparative cohort included 87 children treated between January 2021 and December 2025: 42 in the emergency department (Group 1) and 45 in the operating room (Group 2). Clinical, radiological, functional, and healthcare-related outcomes were compared.ResultsRadiological union was achieved in all patients. Mean time to union did not differ significantly between groups (7.0 ± 1.1 vs. 6.6 ± 0.9 weeks; p = 0.067). Post-casting sagittal angulation was significantly greater in Group 1 (15.2 ± 5.4° vs. 12.1 ± 5.8°; p = 0.012), whereas coronal angulation did not differ significantly (12.8 ± 4.9° vs. 10.7 ± 5.2°; p = 0.060). Malunion occurred in 23.8% and 8.9%, respectively (p = 0.058). No patient required repeat reduction or corrective surgery. PedsQL Physical Health Summary Scores (92.07 ± 3.34 vs. 92.16 ± 3.47; p = 0.909) and overall complication rates (23.8% vs. 15.6%; p = 0.332) were similar. Procedure time, hospital stay, and inflation-adjusted direct hospital charges were significantly lower in Group 1 (all p < 0.001).ConclusionEmergency department casting achieved similar union and late parent-reported physical functioning but greater immediate post-casting sagittal angulation. Although this difference required no further intervention, its clinical relevance remains uncertain. In appropriately selected children and centres with experienced practitioners and suitable sedation and monitoring facilities, emergency department casting may reduce hospital resource use and direct hospital charges.

articles.title: What every intensivist should know about dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.

abstract.text: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is an underrecognized, load dependent cause of hemodynamic instability in critically ill patients. Although classically associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, it frequently occurs in the ICU in settings such as septic shock, hypovolemia, postoperative states, and right ventricular failure. Standard shock therapies, including inotropes and afterload reduction, may paradoxically worsen obstruction and lead to escalating hemodynamic instability. Bedside echocardiography is central to diagnosis, typically revealing a small hyperdynamic left ventricle and a late-peaking Doppler profile. Management focuses on restoring preload, increasing afterload, and reducing excessive contractility. In some patients, LVOTO is secondary to right ventricular failure, requiring targeted right ventricular support. Dynamic LVOTO is a reversible and often iatrogenic cause of shock. Early recognition and physiology-guided management can rapidly improve hemodynamics and prevent harmful therapeutic escalation.

articles.title: Pneumococcal carriage and selected respiratory virus in children with clinical pneumonia in Salvador, Brazil during PCV10 era.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In 2010, Brazil introduced the 10-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV10GSK). Assessing pneumococcal carriage among children with clinical pneumonia in the context of a mature PCV10GSK program can inform decisions about use of next-generation PCVs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We prospectively enrolled children aged 2-59 months meeting a standardized case definition for clinical pneumonia at two emergency care units in Salvador, Brazil. Nasopharyngeal specimens were tested for pneumococcus by culture and qPCR with serotyping by Quellung and/or PCR or qPCR; isolates underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST). Respiratory viruses were detected using qPCR, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) strains were genotyped.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From March 2023 to March 2024, 170 children with clinical pneumonia were enrolled; 93.5% were up to date on pneumococcal vaccination. Pneumococcal carriage was detected in 62.7% (106/169 swabbed patients; 55 by culture and 51 by qPCR). Among the 106 pneumococcal carriers, the most prevalent serotypes were 6C (18.9%), 11A/D (9.4%), 19A (7.5%), 3 (6.6%), 19F (5.7%), 6A (5.0%), and 23B (4.7%). PCV10GSK serotypes (19F, 4, 7F/A, 9V/A, 23F) were detected in 10.4% (11/106) of pneumococcal isolates, driven by serotype 19F (5.6%). The proportions of carriers with serotypes including in PNEUMOSIL, 13, 15, and 20 serotypes, were 21.7%, 29.2%, 30.2%, and 40.6%, respectively. Among 53 isolates with AST, more than 30.0% were resistant to macrolides and 35.8% were penicillin non-susceptible. RSV was detected in 20.6% (35/170) of cases, predominantly RSV-A (72.0%); 60.0% of RSV-positive cases were colonized with pneumococcus.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: More than a decade after PCV10GSK introduction, and despite high vaccination coverage, PCV10GSK serotypes remain detectable among pneumococci carried by children with pneumonia. Next-generation PCVs provide broader serotype coverage. Continued monitoring of the persistent circulation of vaccine serotypes remains important.

articles.title: Maternal deaths on arrival: A 5-year retrospective study in a health district in South Africa.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Maternal deaths on arrival remain one of the blind spots in maternal death surveillance and response programs. There are no policy and guideline addressing maternal deaths on arrival in South Africa. Main objective was to analyse maternal deaths on arrival at the health facilities in a South African district. All maternal deaths on arrival at the health facilities at the Ekurhuleni district over a period of five years and nine months (July 2014 to March 2020), were retrospectively reviewed. Analysis included maternal mortality ratio, demography, gestational age at booking, delivery and deaths, newborn outcome, causes and interval between hospital discharge and presenting as dead. Descriptive statistics (proportion, mean, standard deviation, median and interquartile range) and inferential statistics (Chi-square test, Fishers exact test and Students t test) comparing the women with known and unknown causes, are presented. Twenty-eight (5.72%) women out of the 489 maternal deaths were dead on arrival. The maternal mortality ratio was 7.65 maternal deaths per 100000 live births. Causes of deaths were inconclusive in 17 (60.71%). Among the known causes, the commonest (5, 45.45%) cause was haemorrhage. Median interval between discharge from hospital and presenting as dead was 2.5 days. Information on three delay model were unavailable. Delay two was mentioned for only one year where ambulance service was disrupted due to local protests against municipal services. Comparison between the known and unknown causes showed the regional hospitals had significantly higher numbers of known causes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Maternal deaths on arrival was an important contributor to maternal mortality in this study although poorly documented. Majority attended antenatal care and delivered at the hospitals raising a suspicion of early hospital discharge and failure to timely follow-up. A protocol and guideline, with a focus on postmortem examinations should be developed for management of maternal deaths on arrival.

articles.title: Mobile Stroke Units in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Thrombectomy Efficiency, Workflow Models, and Implementation Considerations: A Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a time-critical emergency in which the benefit of reperfusion depends not only on treatment speed but also on accurate large-vessel occlusion (LVO) recognition, destination selection, and coordination between prehospital and hospital teams. Mobile stroke units (MSUs) move imaging, laboratory testing, specialist assessment, and thrombolysis into the prehospital setting, but their effect on thrombectomy depends substantially on onboard vascular-imaging capability and local routing protocols.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: This narrative review evaluates MSUs through the broader construct of thrombectomy efficiency, encompassing LVO identification, destination accuracy, avoidance of secondary transfer and duplicate imaging, in-hospital parallel processing, puncture and reperfusion times, and downstream clinical outcomes. Evidence for earlier intravenous thrombolysis is retained as an important upstream benefit but is distinguished from thrombectomy-specific efficiency. The available literature indicates that non-contrast-CT-based MSUs can accelerate hospital workflows through early diagnosis and prenotification, whereas CTA-enabled models can additionally confirm LVO in the field and support direct routing to a thrombectomy-capable center or, in selected systems, direct-to-angiography pathways. The magnitude of benefit is therefore configuration- and system-dependent.
