Economic evaluations likewise show that value is highly sensitive to annual patient volume, catchment population, staffing model, operating hours, analytic time horizon, and baseline patient disability.

abstract.label: KEY MESSAGES
abstract.text: MSUs should not be treated as a uniform intervention. Their thrombectomy value is determined by how effectively prehospital imaging and specialist assessment are linked to destination decisions, interfacility-transfer avoidance, and receiving-center activation. CTA-enabled pathways provide the clearest mechanism for thrombectomy-specific time savings, while non-contrast-CT-based models may still improve in-hospital efficiency. Implementation is most defensible when local geography, case volume, workforce, dispatch integration, downstream thrombectomy capacity, and cost-effectiveness are considered together.

articles.title: Online Sports Betting Legalization and Behavioral Health Care Use.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: The number of states with legal online sports betting has grown from 1 to 31 since 2018, expanding access to gambling. Despite the known behavioral health burdens associated with gambling, little is understood about legalization's impact on mental health and substance use treatment use.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the association between online sports betting legalization and treatment use for mental health conditions and substance use disorders (SUD).

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This was a quasi-experimental staggered difference-in-differences study using claims data from January 2016 to December 2023. The setting was a large, national convenience sample of people with employer-sponsored health insurance. Included in the analysis were men and women aged 18 to 64 years living in states that legalized online sports betting during 2018-2022 or had not by the end of the study period.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: State legalization of online sports betting.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Outcomes were measured at the state-year level, weighted by number of enrollees as follows: proportions of enrollees with 1 or more prescription fills for antidepressant, antianxiety, or SUD medications and proportions of enrollees with 1 or more outpatient, emergency department, or inpatient visits with a diagnosis for depression, anxiety, or SUD.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 61 951 305 enrollee-years, 31 914 852 (52%) were women, and the mean (SD) age was 41.9 (13.5) years. Online sports betting legalization was associated with increases in the probability of antidepressant use (men: 0.57 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.26-0.89 percentage points; women: 1.08 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.23-1.94 percentage points) and antianxiety use (men: 0.32 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.14-0.50 percentage points; women: 0.64 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.16-1.12 percentage points), but there was no detectable change in SUD medication use. Legalization was also associated with increases in the probability of an outpatient diagnosis for depression (men: 0.34 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.20-0.49 percentage points; women: 0.57 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.25-0.89 percentage points) and anxiety (men: 0.67 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.32-1.01 percentage points; women: 1.15 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.50-1.81 percentage points) but not SUD. Legalization was not associated with behavioral health diagnoses in the emergency department and inpatient settings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Results of this quasi-experimental difference-in-differences study suggest that online sports betting legalization was associated with an increase in outpatient and prescription mental health care use among people with employer-sponsored health insurance. These findings underscore the importance of prevention and treatment of potential adverse health consequences of legalized online sports betting.

articles.title: Cultural Adaptation, Validity, and Reliability of the Moral Distress Scale for Prehospital Emergency Health Services Employees: The Case of Türkiye.

abstract.text: Prehospital emergency healthcare professionals, who frequently face situations requiring rapid decision-making, interventions with limited resources, and ethical dilemmas related to patient care, are at high risk of experiencing moral distress. This study aimed to conduct the Turkish cultural adaptation, validity, and reliability testing of the Moral Distress Scale in order to evaluate the moral distress experienced by prehospital emergency healthcare workers. Within the scope of the study, the 20-item, five-factor Moral Distress Scale was translated and culturally adapted into Turkish. The construct validity of the scale was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis. Data were collected from 215 prehospital emergency healthcare professionals. Factor loadings ranged from 0.442 to 0.801, and item-total correlations were above 0.30. In the exploratory factor analysis, items 4 and 5 from the "Providing Care" subdimension were loaded onto the "Conflict" subdimension, while item 6 was loaded onto the "Communication" subdimension. The confirmatory factor analysis results confirmed the five-factor, the 20-item structure of the scale, and the model fit indices were found to be acceptable (χ2/df = 2.27, p ≤ 0.001; RMSEA = 0.07; GFI = 0.86; CFI = 0.89; IFI = 0.89; PNFI = 0.70; SRMR = 0.06). The scale demonstrated high internal consistency (α = 0.90). Our results indicate that the Turkish version of the Moral Distress Scale is a reliable and valid instrument for assessing moral distress experienced by prehospital emergency healthcare professionals in their work settings.

articles.title: Musculoskeletal ultrasound in traumatic emergencies: what radiologists need to know.

abstract.text: While conventional radiography (CR) and computed tomography (CT) remain diagnostic staples in emergency settings, ultrasound (US) is a critical tool offering a rapid, dynamic, and noninvasive alternative for acute musculoskeletal (MSK) pathologies assessment. Prompt identification of conditions such as unstable fractures, soft tissue or muscular hematomas, joint effusions, and tendon ruptures is essential to prevent or mitigate long-term patient morbidity. This review summarizes the role of US in the emergency department, providing a practical overview of targeted scanning techniques and key sonographic signs. Additionally, common diagnostic pitfalls and effective escalation pathways are discussed to streamline clinical decision-making and optimize timely patient management.

articles.title: The Current State of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Graft Selection, Lateral Augmentation, Rehabilitation, and Return-to-Play.

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) reliably restores anteroposterior stability; however, the rate of return to prior level of play and incidence of recurrent ACL injury have improved little over the past two decades. The purpose of this review is to describe the current state of ACLR with respect to graft selection, lateral extra-articular augmentation, rehabilitation and return to play, including the role of psychological readiness, and the specific rehabilitation protocol utilized by the senior author.

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: Graft utilization has shifted substantially. Quadriceps tendon autograft accounted for less than 5% of primary reconstructions prior to 2014 and approximately 20% by 2023. Contemporary registry data demonstrate smaller differences in revision risk between autograft types than previously reported. Randomized and comparative data support lateral extra-articular tenodesis in selected high-risk knees, with the largest effect reported in the revision setting. Return-to-play practice has shifted from fixed timelines toward criteria-based clearance. However, a subset of athletes do not pass a full clearance battery, and some athletes who do pass and observe recommended timeframes still sustain reinjury. Limb symmetry index may overestimate functional recovery, while test batteries and thresholds vary considerably between institutions. Psychological readiness is independently associated with both return to sport and second ACL injury. Graft selection should be matched to the patient profile, and lateral augmentation should be reserved for high-risk knees. Return to play should be determined by a combination of time from surgery, functional criteria, and psychological readiness. Future study should focus on validating return-to-play criteria against reinjury endpoints and on standardizing how these criteria are defined and reported.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut.

articles.title: Comparison of two immobilization techniques for radiological outcomes in fifth metacarpal neck fractures: a prospective controlled study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Although fifth metacarpal neck fractures are commonly managed conservatively, there is no consensus regarding the optimal immobilization strategy. The aim of this study was to compare the radiographic outcomes of the Jahss Position Splint (JPS) and the conventional Ulnar Gutter Splint (UGS) in the treatment of fifth metacarpal neck fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 78 adult male patients treated for isolated closed fifth metacarpal neck fractures between January 2023 and June 2024 were prospectively evaluated. Patients were allocated to either the JPS group (n = 42) or the UGS group (n = 36). Patients were assigned to JPS or UGS according to the predefined odd/even-calendar-day duty schedule of two surgeons, each of whom routinely applied one of the techniques. All patients underwent closed reduction using the Jahss maneuver followed by three weeks of immobilization. Radiographic outcomes included initial fracture angulation (IFA), post-reduction angulation (PRA), final follow-up angulation at 12 weeks (FFA), metacarpal shortening, and malunion rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: No significant differences were observed between the groups regarding age or IFA (p > 0.05). Correction during reduction and splint application was greater with JPS than with UGS (15.2 ± 9.6° vs. 8.9 ± 11.0°; p = 0.009), whereas subsequent loss of reduction during immobilisation did not differ significantly between the groups (2.8 ± 8.4° vs. 1.0 ± 9.8°; p = 0.388).The JPS group demonstrated significantly lower PRA (p < 0.001) and FFA (p = 0.003) compared with the UGS group. Metacarpal shortening was significantly less in the JPS group (p = 0.036). The malunion rate was 5% in the JPS group and 28% in the UGS group (p = 0.009).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: JPS was associated with greater immediate angular correction and more favourable final radiographic outcomes than UGS but did not reduce subsequent loss of reduction during immobilisation. Because functional and patient-reported outcomes were not assessed, the clinical relevance of these radiographic differences remains uncertain.

articles.title: Surgical management of orbital wall fractures in juveniles: a European multicenter study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Isolated orbital floor fractures in juveniles are a challenge, as children and adolescents may experience diplopia and limited ocular motility, even with little to no periorbital edema or visible signs of injury to the eye. The aim of the present study is to assess the demographic and clinical variables, and the outcomes of pediatric patients affected by isolated orbital wall fractures at several European oral and maxillofacial surgery centers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Pediatric patients (less than 18 years) with hospitalized and surgically treated for unilateral isolated orbital blow out fractures of the orbital floor and/or the medial wall were included. The following data were recorded for each patient: gender, age, etiology of trauma, site of orbital wall fracture(s), timing of intervention, surgical approach, orbital reconstruction material/implant, post-operative complications RESULTS: A total of 51 pediatric patients (45 boys, 6 girls) with a mean age of 12.1 years were included. Most patients (43 children, 84.3%) presented with an isolated orbital floor fracture. Clinically, the most frequently observed sign was diplopia / double vision (43 patients, 84.3%). More than two thirds (68.6%) of cases were surgically treated within the first two days from injury. In 6 patients (11.8%) one or more persistent postoperative disturbances were found six months postoperatively, including diplopia in 3 subjects (5.9%), infraorbital nerve paresthesia in 2 patients (3.9%), and enophthalmos in 2 patients (3.9%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The rarity of pure orbital wall fractures in pediatric patients makes it difficult to establish uniform evidence-based guidelines for their management. These injuries must also be recognized promptly, as surgical intervention may be required at a very early stage. A reasoned and individualized choice of the optimal surgical approach appears to be the most appropriate strategy for this specific type of facial fracture in the pediatric population.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Validation of PECARN as a clinical decision rule for CT imaging of children with blunt abdominal trauma: a single centre retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Blunt traumatic injuries are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children. Contrast enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the best imaging tool for screening patients at risk of blunt abdominal injury. Concerns existed on potential overuse and the radiation risks. We aim at evaluating paediatric use of trauma CT scan.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Children with traumatic injuries who attended a tertiary trauma centre from January 2000 to December 2024 were included to evaluate the use of trauma CT scan and patterns of paediatric abdominal trauma. We excluded those with penetrating or isolated head injury. The Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) algorithm was applied retrospectively with the aim of validating the use of PECARN.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Total of 1138 paediatic trauma admissions were identified during the study period and 70% (n 802) had blunt trauma. 483 patients were included after excluding patients with isolated head injury and missing data. 90 days trauma related mortality was 0.7% with one patient died within 24 hours of admission. Overall Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 3.52±5.95 which appeared to increase with age (rho 0.289, p <0.01).111 patients received CT scan, among which 35 are whole body CT. Significant findings were detected in 30% of these scans, 25 required intervention. Patients with higher trauma index and lower GCS, trauma call activation, older aged at presentation were more likely to receive a scan (p<0.001). No pathology was missed in the no CT group. PECARN validation was performed on 200 patients, There were no missed scans and pathologies in PECARN negative patients. Sensitivity was 100%, specificity was 96.5%, negative predictive value was 100%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A significant portion of children had negative trauma CT scan and did not need intervention. Use of clinical decision rule is warranted in identifying children at lower risk to minimize unnecessary imaging.

articles.title: Management and outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures: a 10-year experience from an Australian Level 1 Trauma Centre.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures are associated with high morbidity and mortality despite advances in resuscitation, development in trauma systems and multispecialty haemorrhage control. This study aimed to describe the management strategies and clinical outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures over a 10-year period at an Australian Level I Trauma Centre.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective observational cohort study was performed of patients aged ≥ 16 years with moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures (Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) ≥ 3) treated between January 2015 and December 2024. Data were obtained from the institutional prospectively collected trauma registry.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 313 patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 47.0 years and 69.3% were male. Motor vehicle (35.1%) and motorcycle collisions (24.9%) accounted for 60.1% of injuries. Median ISS was 26 (IQR 19-34), with 70.6% sustaining pelvic AIS 4-5 injuries. 20.1% of patients underwent at least one haemorrhage-control intervention, including angioembolisation (14.4%), preperitoneal pelvic packing (5.8%) and external fixation (5.8%). Angioembolisation utilisation increased from 6.7% in 2015 to 40.0% in 2024. In-hospital mortality was 7.7%, with traumatic brain injury accounting for 62.5% of deaths and haemorrhagic shock for only one death.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures remained characterised by high-energy mechanisms and severe multisystem injury over the study period, while management evolved with increasing utilisation of angioembolisation. In-hospital mortality was numerically lower compared with historical cohorts, with most deaths attributable to associated traumatic brain injury rather than pelvic haemorrhage.

articles.title: [Crisis, disaster and war: the role of urology in resilient healthcare structures].

abstract.text: Europe's changed security environment requires the German healthcare system to prepare for crises, disasters, and war. Planning must address not only a sudden influx of casualties but also failures of energy supply, information technology, communications, supply chains, and staffing. This does not justify unrestricted expansion of the urologist's professional remit. In mass casualty incidents, urological contributions should follow a graded competency model: trauma bay and team tasks, surgical assistance, defined core urological procedures, and advanced capabilities restricted to selected experts. Resilience depends on prioritized care, network-based capacity management, analogue fallback procedures, critical stockpiles, and regular exercises. Surgical training for rare open emergency procedures can be supplemented by simulation-based training and interdisciplinary courses. The authors propose a modular, assessable qualification pathway combining stepwise training in routine clinical care, simulation, rotations, and competency assessment. Its purpose is to reinforce interdisciplinary teams while safeguarding routine and emergency urological care.

articles.title: [Acute heart failure-management during the first 120 min : Approach for early stabilization and decongestion].

abstract.text: Acute heart failure (AHF) is among the most common causes of emergency department, intermediate care, and intensive care unit admission and remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in contemporary therapy. The first 120 min of management are particularly critical, as this period determines not only respiratory and hemodynamic stabilization, but also trigger identification, decongestion strategy, and the foundation for subsequent prognostic improvement. This CME article provides a practical, phenotype-based approach to the early management of AHF. The proposed strategy is centered on the rapid classification of patients according to congestion ("wet" vs. "dry") and perfusion ("warm" vs. "cold") status. Stabilization and diagnostic work-up must occur simultaneously. Early assessment should focus on identifying acute coronary syndrome, clinically relevant arrhythmias, hypertensive crisis, pulmonary embolism, structural heart disease, and infectious triggers. In addition to clinical examination, electrocardiography, blood gas analysis, and biomarkers, point-of-care ultrasound with lung ultrasound and focused echocardiography play a pivotal role in the first-line evaluation. From a therapeutic perspective, early noninvasive ventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema, prompt vasodilation in hypertensive presentations, and effective decongestion with intravenous loop diuretics constitute the core interventions. In cases of insufficient response, escalation strategies such as sequential nephron blockade or selective use of vasoactive agents should be considered. Structured reassessment at short intervals is essential to detect persistent congestion, evolving hypoperfusion, inadequate therapeutic response, or overlooked differential diagnoses. The article emphasizes that successful acute management must already establish the transition toward guideline-directed long-term therapy during the first hours of hospitalization, including early initiation of evidence-based heart failure medication once hemodynamic stabilization has been achieved.

articles.title: Early cystography after traumatic bladder repair: Diagnostic intervention or marker of an accelerated catheter removal pathway?
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

articles.title: Influencing factors analysis and prediction model development for ROSC in adult non-traumatic OHCA: a retrospective study based on pre-hospital emergency settings.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac arrest is a major global public health problem. This study aimed to explore factors influencing return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and develop a prediction model for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively collected electronic medical records of adult non-traumatic OHCA patients at Tianjin Emergency Medical Center from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC up to emergency department arrival and handover to receiving-hospital staff. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression with clinician ID as random intercept adjusted clustering bias; predictors with p < 0.05 formed the nomogram. Patients were randomly split 7:3 for training and internal testing. Discrimination was assessed by ROC-AUC (acceptable threshold >0.7). We performed 1000 bootstrap resampling to correct C-index against overfitting. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) further evaluated predictive consistency and net clinical benefit.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 9,386 included cases, 678 (7.2%) achieved ROSC. Mixed-effects regression identified independent ROSC predictors: public location (aOR = 1.285, 95% CI:1.038-1.592), 06:00-12:00 onset (aOR = 1.308, 95% CI:1.018-1.682), prolonged emergency response time (aOR = 0.971, 95% CI:0.945-0.999), extended onset-to-ambulance intervals (5-10 min: aOR = 0.758;10-30 min: aOR = 0.578;>30 min:aOR = 0.498 vs ≤5 min), no OHCA occurred at emergency call (aOR = 1.540, 95% CI:1.048-2.262), male attending physicians (aOR = 1.255, 95% CI:1.077-1.464), longer physician practice years (aOR = 1.043, 95%CI: 1.022-1.065), intermediate physician title (aOR = 1.236, 95% CI:1.047-1.459), shockable initial rhythm (aOR = 2.850, 95% CI:2.390-3.397), endotracheal intubation (aOR = 2.294, 95% CI:1.936-2.718), epinephrine >5 mg (aOR = 0.765,95% CI:0.626-0.935). The nomogram AUC reached 0.775 (95% CI:0.756-0.794) in the training set and 0.775 (95% CI:0.745-0.805) in the test set; 1000 bootstrap internal validation gave an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.7679 with minimal optimism of 0.0071, showing negligible overfitting, good calibration and favorable net clinical benefit via DCA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study identified multiple factors significantly associated with ROSC in OHCA patients; the constructed model showed good predictive value.

articles.title: Patterns of re-presentations to Tasmanian emergency departments for suicidal behaviour.
articles.journal_full: The Australian and New Zealand journal of psychiatry

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine sociodemographic and episode-of-care characteristics among individuals presenting with suicidal behaviour who re-present to emergency departments in Tasmania, Australia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Emergency department presentations related to suicidal behaviour from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2023 were identified across four public hospitals in Tasmania. The primary outcome of interest was the number, rate and risk of re-presentations, defined as a subsequent visit within 7 days, 28 days or at any time during the study period. Analyses also assessed the total presentation frequency per individual across these timeframes. Concordance in episode-of-care characteristics, including arrival mode, was compared between the index and first re-presentation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 12,659 presentations related to suicidal behaviour were recorded among 7,426 Tasmanian individuals, of which 5,409 had a single presentation, and 2,017 had one or more re-presentations. Re-presentation within 7 days, 28 days and across the study period was associated with younger age, higher triage urgency and specific departure modalities. The highest concordance between index and repeat presentations was observed for arrival by ambulance (51.63%), afternoon arrival (40.33%), triage category 3 (66%) and leaving at own risk after clinician assessment (65.05%). Individuals with multiple re-presentations were more likely to be female and from lower socioeconomic areas.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Re-presentations to the emergency department for suicidal behaviour were more common among younger individuals, those triaged as more urgent and those who left the emergency department without seeing a health professional. Higher re-presentation rates were also observed among females and individuals from disadvantaged socioeconomic areas. These findings highlight key sociodemographic and care-related factors that can inform targeted interventions, improved service planning and enhanced mental health resource allocation to reduce repeat emergency department presentations.

articles.title: Post-discharge alcohol-related emergency department use among older adults following involuntary inpatient treatment for alcohol use disorder.
articles.journal_full: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists

abstract.text: ObjectiveThe New South Wales Involuntary Drug and Alcohol Treatment (IDAT) program provides last-resort involuntary inpatient treatment for severe substance dependence. This study described older adults with severe alcohol use disorder (AUD) admitted to IDAT and their alcohol-related emergency department (ED) use after discharge.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥60 years with primary AUD admitted to an IDAT unit during 2016-2022. Demographic, social and clinical variables were summarised. Alcohol-related ED presentations before admission and after discharge were compared; time to first post-discharge presentation was examined using Kaplan-Meier analysis.ResultsOf 374 admissions, 37 older adults met inclusion criteria. Medical and psychiatric comorbidity, living alone and residence outside major cities were common. Among 36 participants included in post-discharge analyses, alcohol-related ED presentations were lower in the 6 months after discharge than in the 6 months before admission (median 1 vs 3, P < 0.001). Within 6 months, 22 participants (61%) re-presented, of whom 18 (82%) first re-presented within 3 months.ConclusionsOlder adults admitted to IDAT for severe AUD formed a clinically and socially complex cohort. Alcohol-related ED re-presentations were concentrated within 3 months of discharge, highlighting a high-risk transition period requiring structured continuity of care.

articles.title: Pediatric Disaster Preparedness at Rural and Critical Access Hospitals: A Mixed-Methods Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Over 80% of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits in the United States occur outside of children's hospitals. Although previous studies have described gaps in pediatric readiness, few studies have focused on pediatric disaster preparedness at rural and critical access hospitals (CAHs). During periods of pediatric surge, CAHs may be forced to manage pediatric patients with delayed transfer times. This mixed-methods study, conducted by the Region V for Kids (RV4K) Pediatric Disaster Center of Excellence, elicited strengths and barriers to pediatric disaster preparedness in rural and CAHs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a qualitative study of clinicians from CAHs in the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Region 5. After completing a demographic survey, respondents were invited to participate in focus groups about pediatric disaster preparedness, followed by an open-response questionnaire about how RV4K can support rural and CAHs. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Focus group transcripts and questionnaire responses were analyzed using a constant comparative approach to identify themes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 41 survey respondents, 19 participated in focus groups. Most study participants worked at EDs seeing <1800 children per year, and less than half had pediatric inpatient capabilities. Few hospital disaster plans considered children. Four focus group themes emerged: strengths of staff and community, staffing limitations, and desire for targeted pediatric education resources and pediatric disaster plan development.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our study engaged directly with staff at rural and CAHs to gain insights about pediatric preparedness that will be used to develop resources specifically tailored to CAHs' unique clinical needs.

articles.title: Does End-of-Therapy-Anchored Follow-Up Bias Comparisons of Antibiotic Duration in Acute Otitis Media?
Pediatric Infectious Encephalitis in Spain: Etiology, Outcomes and Acyclovir Use in Emergency Departments.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric infectious encephalitis remains a significant cause of neurologic morbidity. Prompt antiviral treatment is recommended in patients with suspected herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology and outcomes of infectious encephalitis and to evaluate acyclovir use in children with suspected encephalitis presenting to the pediatric emergency department (PED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 10 Spanish PEDs (2017-2023), including children ≤18 years who underwent cerebrospinal fluid polymerase chain reaction testing as part of the evaluation of a possible central nervous system infection. Patients meeting the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) criteria for infectious encephalitis were analyzed, and acyclovir prescription rates were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We registered 446 episodes; 118 patients (26.5%) met the IEC criteria, and 88 (74.6%) had microbiologic confirmation. The most common pathogens were enterovirus (43.2%), influenza virus (18.2%) and HSV (9.0%). Thirty-seven patients (31.4%) had an adverse outcome, including 75% of those with HSV infection. Acyclovir was administered to 56.9% and 53.1% of patients with and without an altered mental status, respectively. All patients meeting IEC criteria presented with altered mental status and ≥1 minor criterion at evaluation in the PED.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Enteroviruses were the leading cause of pediatric infectious encephalitis, whereas HSV infection was associated with the highest risk of adverse outcomes. Acyclovir use in the PED was suboptimal and poorly aligned with clinical criteria. Our findings suggest that empirical acyclovir should be considered in patients with altered mental status and at least one minor criterion, whereas it may be unnecessary in the absence of these features.

articles.title: Predicting Self-Harm Events After Emergency Department Visits Associated With Mental or Substance Use Disorder Diagnoses.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Using a machine learning model, the authors aimed to predict self-harm events within 90 days of an emergency department (ED) visit associated with a mental or substance use disorder diagnosis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Electronic health record and claims data of patients ages ≥11 years from seven integrated health systems were used to identify ED visits and diagnoses. Data on 1,254 predictors were extracted for the 60 months before an ED visit, and self-harm was measured in the 90 days after this visit. Logistic regression models were used to estimate self-harm events, with performance estimated by using out-of-sample cross-validation predictions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In a sample of 1,554,828 ED visits for 803,413 patients, self-harm occurred for 19,603 (1.3%) visits. The best-fitting model yielded an area under the curve of 0.85, indicating good overall performance that was consistent across various subgroups. Patients with ED visits estimated to be at the 95th percentile in predicted risk for self-harm had a 10.8% rate of self-harm events, compared with 2.4% for visits estimated at the 50th percentile. Patients with visits estimated to be in the highest risk stratum had an observed risk for self-harm of 27.2%, approximately 136 times greater than the observed risk in the lowest risk stratum.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The model performed well in predicting self-harm events in the 90 days after an ED visit for individuals with behavioral health diagnoses. Such machine learning models could be useful in identifying ED patients who may need safety planning and close follow-up after discharge.

articles.title: In situ Simulation as a Training Tool in a Tertiary Pediatric Emergency Department in Italy: Enhancing Preparedness Where it Matters.
articles.journal_full: Advances in medical education and practice

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In situ simulation differs from in-centre simulation as it is conducted in the actual clinical environment rather than a simulation laboratory, thereby enhancing contextual realism and enabling identification of system-level vulnerabilities within clinical workflows.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of in situ simulation on self-perceived competence, clinical performance, team dynamics, and system readiness in a tertiary pediatric emergency department in Italy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective single-center observational study was conducted in a tertiary pediatric emergency department in Italy. A total of 55 healthcare professionals participated in 11 high-fidelity in situ simulation sessions. Participants completed pre- and post-intervention self-assessment questionnaires using a Likert-scale instrument developed for the study. Clinical performance was evaluated using a structured ABCDE-based checklist. No formal qualitative interviews were conducted. Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-tests with a significance threshold of p<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant improvements were observed across all assessed domains, particularly in ABCDE assessment, ventilation, and defibrillator use (p<0.001). Junior residents and participants without recent EPALS certification demonstrated the greatest improvement. In situ simulation also identified latent safety threats related to equipment availability and clinical workflow.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In situ simulation improves perceived clinical competence and team performance while providing actionable insights into system-level safety vulnerabilities. Future research should incorporate objective performance metrics and validated assessment tools.

articles.title: Predicting Pulmonary Complications Using Two Clinical Decision Tools in an Emergency Department Sample of Chest Trauma Patients.

abstract.text: The Research to Practice column is designed to improve the research critique skills and translation of research findings into emergency care clinical practice. In this issue, we discuss the findings of Chen, et al. (2024) whose project examined the validity of two systematic chest trauma decision tools used in tandem to predict the highest risk of developing pulmonary complications or a need for surgical stabilization those patients with rib fractures. The findings supported that RibScore and SCARF score were individually sensitive in predicting pulmonary complications, but when combined, their predictive accuracy was even greater. Both scores were easy to calculate and integrate into a chest trauma assessment.

articles.title: Comparison of Acute Physiology, Age and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale in predicting clinical outcomes and mortality in organophosphorus poisoning.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Organophosphorus poisoning is a major health hazard in developing countries. We conducted a study to compare the Acute Physiology, Age and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) scoring system and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale in predicting the complications, ventilator requirement and mortality in patients of Acute Organophosphorus Poisoning.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: A prospective observational study was done on 100 patients above 18 years of age, presenting with alleged history of consumption of organophosphorus compounds. The patients were evaluated for the required details to calculate the APACHE II score and Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale and were followed up till discharge or mortality to identify the complications, ventilator requirement and mortality. This data was tabulated using Excel and analyzed using SPSS software to look for correlation between the scores and the outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean age of our patients was 33.64 ± 12.99 years. The APACHE II cutoff score for complications, ventilator requirement and mortality was ≥ 7 (sensitivity 94.3%, specificity 96.9%, Area under Receiver Operator Characteristic (ROC) 0.99, p < 0.01), ≥9 (sensitivity 86.7%, specificity 82.4%, Area under ROC 0.91, p < 0.01) and ≥16 (sensitivity 85.7, specificity 96.8%, Area under ROC 0.98, p < 0.01) respectively. Similarly, the Peradeniya Organophosphorus Poisoning Scale cutoff was for complications, ventilator requirement and mortality was ≥ 3 (sensitivity 80%, specificity 92.3%, Area under ROC 0.90, p < 0.01), ≥3 (sensitivity 80%, specificity 75.3%, Area under ROC 0.85, p < 0.01) and ≥7 (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 97.8%, Area under ROC 0.99, p < 0.01) respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both APACHE II and POPS demonstrated good predictive performance for adverse outcomes in acute organophosphorus poisoning. Both scores showed excellent discrimination for mortality, with no statistically significant difference between their AUCs.

articles.title: Psychometric evaluation of the Persian version of the shared decision‑making questionnaire in patients undergoing emergency surgery.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Accurate assessment of shared decision-making (SDM) is essential in emergency surgery, yet no culturally adapted and validated instrument is available in Iran. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and assess the psychometric properties of the Persian SDM-Q-9 among patients undergoing emergency surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This methodological cross-sectional study followed a forward-backward translation procedure to adapt the SDM-Q-9 into Persian. Face and content validity were established prior to construct validation. Data were collected from 575 patients undergoing emergency surgery and randomly split into two independent subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 287) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 288). Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha, McDonald's omega, and composite reliability (CR). Convergent validity was examined using average variance extracted (AVE).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The data were suitable for factor analysis (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.923; Bartlett's test of sphericity: χ² = 3433.445, df = 36, p < 0.001). EFA using Maximum Likelihood (ML) extraction with Promax rotation supported a single-factor structure explaining 58.60% of the total variance, with all factor loadings exceeding 0.70. CFA of the independent validation subsample initially showed inadequate fit for the one-factor model. After reviewing modification indices and item content, three theoretically justified residual correlations were retained. The resulting model showed good fit (χ²/df = 2.78, Comparative Fit Index [CFI] = 0.962, Tucker-Lewis Index [TLI] = 0.944, Root Mean Square Error of Approximation [RMSEA] = 0.059, and Standardized Root Mean Square Residual [SRMR] = 0.052). Factor loadings ranged from 0.67 to 0.84, supporting a predominantly unidimensional structure. The scale demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.921, McDonald's omega = 0.926, and CR = 0.924). Convergent validity was supported by an AVE of 0.576.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The Persian SDM-Q-9 demonstrated satisfactory validity and strong reliability for assessing patient-perceived shared decision-making in emergency surgical settings in Iran. Its predominantly unidimensional structure supports its use, although the localized residual associations identified in CFA warrant replication in independent, multicenter samples.

articles.title: Impact of Methamphetamine Use on Injury Characteristics and Postoperative Outcomes in Upper Extremity Fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Methamphetamine use in orthopedic trauma carries an indeterminate risk, with prior studies suggesting increased rates of deep vein thrombosis and elevated mortality. Upper extremity fractures (UEFs) have distinct mechanisms of injury and operative risk. This study evaluates outcomes following operative management of UEFs in patients with and without documented methamphetamine use.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective chart review was conducted of adults undergoing surgical fixation of UEFs (distal radius/ulna to clavicle; phalangeal, metacarpal, and carpal fractures were excluded) from January 2022 to March 2025. Outcomes included urinary tract infection, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, pneumonia, emergency department (ED) visits, readmission, surgical site infection, hardware removal, and mortality. A post hoc subgroup analysis of isolated UEFs was performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 426 patients meeting study criteria: 40 with methamphetamine use, and 386 without. Methamphetamine users were more likely to experience polytrauma (27.5% vs 10.9%, P = .003), higher-energy injuries (75.0% vs 53.6%, P = .003), interpersonal violence, such as altercations (22.5% vs 5.7%, P < .001), and ED visits within 30 days (20.0% vs 9.1%, P = .047). No other estimable postoperative outcome differed significantly. For isolated UEFs, methamphetamine users had shorter follow-up (85.9 vs 116.3 days, P = .022).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Methamphetamine use was associated with higher-energy injury mechanisms and increased health care use, namely ED visits. No other estimable perioperative complication differed significantly, and no deaths occurred. Operative management should not be withheld solely because of methamphetamine use; targeted case management may reduce postoperative use.

articles.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

articles.title: AI-augmented cardiopulmonary point-of-care ultrasound: a narrative review for pulmonary and critical care clinicians.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is an increasingly utilised tool in pulmonary and critical care medicine, yet its effectiveness remains limited by operator dependency and the required cognitive demands of real-time image acquisition and interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to augment POCUS by supporting image acquisition, interpretation and quantitative analysis. Given the rapid evolution of this field, clinicians must understand both the capabilities and limitations of AI-enabled POCUS. However, prior reviews have largely catalogued applications without focusing on how these tools integrate into bedside workflows. This narrative review examines AI in cardiopulmonary POCUS through a workflow-based lens relevant to pulmonologists and intensivists. We discuss the role of AI as a bedside coach, interpreter and quantifier, highlighting applications in lung and focused cardiac ultrasound, including pneumothorax detection, B-line analysis, left ventricular function assessment, and identification of other cardiopulmonary pathologies. Across domains, AI demonstrates strong performance in controlled settings, although variability persists in real-world environments due to differences in image quality, patient factors and dataset limitations. Future directions include interactive, clinician-in-the-loop systems, protocol-driven integration, and multimodal data synthesis. A clear understanding of these developments will be essential for clinicians as AI becomes increasingly embedded within bedside patient care.

articles.title: Arthroscopic Bankart Repair Is Associated With Lower 90-Day Emergency Department Use Than Open Repair, With Smoking, Medicaid Insurance, and Depression as Additional Independent Predictors.
articles.journal_full: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To characterize the timing, frequency, and predictors of 90-day emergency department (ED) visits after Bankart repair using a national administrative database.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients undergoing primary arthroscopic or open Bankart repair were identified from the 2010 to 2023 Q1 PearlDiver M170 database. Patients with infection or neoplasm within 90 days preoperatively or less than 90 days of database follow-up were excluded. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of ED visits within 90 days postoperatively. Among ED users, weekly visit timing was compared with a baseline rate (range of rates from postoperative weeks 53-57), and primary diagnoses at 1, 2, and 3 months were categorized.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 149,024 patients (age 33.4 years, 66.1% men, 95.5% arthroscopic), 11,760 (7.9%) visited the ED, with 25.8% of visits occurring during the first 2 postoperative weeks. Independent predictors of ED use included (in decreasing odds ratio order) recent smoking (odds ratio 2.99), Medicaid insurance (2.03), depression (1.70), prior opioid use (1.56), social determinants of health (1.55), diabetes (1.45), Medicare insurance (1.36), open surgical approach (1.34), female sex (1.33), body mass index ≥ 30 (1.24), Midwest region (1.21), and age (1.01. per year decrease) (P < .001 for all). Shoulder-related visits accounted for 33.2% of ED encounters in month 1, declining to 17.6% and 13.0% by months 2 and 3, with shoulder pain as the leading subcategory at every postoperative month.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: After Bankart repair, nearly 8% of patients presented to the ED within 90 days, with the highest incidence occurring during the first 2 postoperative weeks. The strongest independent predictors of ED visits included smoking (odds ratio 2.99), Medicaid insurance (2.03), depression (1.70), prior opioid use within 6 months (1.56), social determinants of health (1.55), diabetes (1.45), Medicare insurance (1.36), open surgical approach (1.34), and female sex (1.33). Shoulder pain was the most common shoulder-related reason for ED presentation across all 3 postoperative months.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Integrated physical, cognitive and psychological rehabilitation following multiple ACL reconstructions in a professional handball player: a case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries with repeated surgical interventions and postoperative complications pose a major challenge in sports rehabilitation. Beyond neuromuscular deficits, psychological and cognitive readiness often remain impaired, increasing reinjury risk and threatening athletic careers. This case highlights an integrated rehabilitation strategy addressing physical, psychological, and cognitive domains in a professional athlete with a complex surgical history.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 31-year-old white Serbian male professional handball player with a history of two ACL reconstructions, meniscal repairs, a postoperative knee infection, and multiple arthroscopic interventions presented with persistent knee instability, pain, and psychological distress. Following repeated failed return-to-play attempts, he underwent a ten-week intervention combining therapeutic exercises, sports psychology sessions, and neurocognitive dual-task training. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included gait analysis, postural control, strength testing, ACL-specific functional tests, and psychological evaluations. Post-intervention assessments showed improvements in gait mechanics, postural stability, neuromuscular strength, and reduced functional asymmetries, alongside lower cognitive anxiety and greater motivation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case suggests that an interdisciplinary, multimodal rehabilitation approach, integrating physical, psychological, and cognitive strategies, may help address both physical deficits and psychological barriers in athletes with multiple ACL surgeries and complex postoperative courses. Such integration may support function, confidence, and readiness in high-performance athletes facing career-threatening injuries.

articles.title: Virtual Wards for Acute Care Patients: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Increasing capacity pressures and overcrowding in hospitals and emergency departments (EDs) have led to a global surge in the adoption of technology-enabled hospital-at-home programs, also known as virtual wards (VWs). These models provide hospital-level care in patients' homes supported by remote monitoring, aiming to shorten or avoid hospital admission. While substantial evidence supports the feasibility of VWs for chronic care, evidence for use in patients with acute conditions remains limited. This scoping review aimed to map existing evidence on VWs for acute medical patients within acute care settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In February 2025, multiple databases were searched to identify studies evaluating VWs for adult acute care populations. Outcomes included clinical and safety variables, length of stay, functional outcomes, cost and resource use, barriers and facilitators to implementation, user experiences, and qualitative analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-two studies were included (RCTs n = 3, case-controls n = 9, cohort n = 7, qualitative n = 3), with substantial heterogeneity in VW models and telemonitoring approaches. The most common indication was infection (e.g. pneumonia, urinary tract). Results of this narrative synthesis suggest care delivered in VWs may be similar to hospital care for rates of ED visits, readmission, short-term mortality, and adverse events. Length of stay in the hospital tended to be shorter. Functional outcomes may be better in VWs. Cost analyses were limited and showed mixed results. Surveys and qualitative analyses indicated high acceptability and generally positive experiences among patients, carers, and healthcare staff.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Evidence from the predominantly non-randomized studies included in this review suggests that VWs may be a feasible alternative for selected acute care patients, with outcomes broadly similar to standard hospital care. Substantial heterogeneity in study designs, alongside the descriptive nature of this synthesis, limits the evaluation of evidence strength and comparability. Robust randomized trials and comprehensive cost-effectiveness analyses are needed.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary perspectives on managing functional/dissociative seizures in the emergency department: A survey of medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) commonly present to emergency departments (ED), but the practices of the multidisciplinary emergency care workforce have not been described.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians at two EDs of an Australian metropolitan tertiary health service, between August-December 2025. Closed items were analysed descriptively; open-ended responses were analysed using conventional qualitative content analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 930 clinicians invited, 101 participated (55 medical, 36 nursing, 10 allied health); 93 (92%) had witnessed a FDS in their ED work, yet 88 (87%) reported little to no training and 73 (72%) had little to no understanding of FDS. Management approaches employed included reassurance (49%), a safe low-stimulus environment (28%) and watchful waiting (29%), with deliberately conservative pharmacology amongst more experienced medical staff. Challenges included treatment disagreement (30%), patient or family expectations (30%) and stigma (21%). Three priorities emerged: a departmental pathway (32%), patient-specific management plans (18%), and multidisciplinary training (18%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Multidisciplinary emergency care clinicians manage FDS based on clinical experience rather than formal training. The three priorities identified by ED clinicians for practice development require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations in Radiology and Medical Imaging Education: Educational Effectiveness, Validity, and Implementation-A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To synthesize evidence on objective structured clinical examinations (OSCEs) in radiology and medical imaging education, focusing on educational outcomes, validity evidence, reliability, scoring, feasibility, and implementation consequences.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: PubMed/MEDLINE, ERIC, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to July 20, 2026. Eligibility was limited to radiology, radiography, nuclear medicine, sonography, and medical student imaging curricula; clinician bedside POCUS courses outside radiology or medical imaging education were excluded. Educational-effect studies were appraised with MERSQI. Measurement evidence was appraised across seven validity and implementation domains. Meta-analysis was considered only for sufficiently comparable independent studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-three reports met the narrowed scope: 22 measurement/implementation reports and 21 educational-effect reports. Educational studies comprised six randomized studies, nine nonrandomized comparisons, one pre-post study, and five post-course or implementation studies. Seven reports favored the intervention, one met a noninferiority criterion, one was mixed, six were uncertain, and six were not estimable as comparative effects. MERSQI scores ranged from 10.5 to 14.0. Feasibility was documented in all measurement reports, but internal-structure or reliability evidence was absent in ten, and consequence evidence was strong in only one.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Imaging-focused OSCEs are feasible and useful for local assessment in radiology and medical imaging education, but evidence remains heterogeneous and incompletely supported by reliability, response-process, and consequence data.

articles.title: Low-Intensity Social Care for Dementia Caregivers: A Randomized Trial.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Resource needs increase strain among dementia caregivers. We tested the impact of CommunityRx-Dementia, a low-intensity resource referral intervention that provides education about common resource needs, a personalized list of nearby resources, and navigation support via a navigator and online resource finder.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-blind RCT comparing usual care (control) versus usual care plus CommunityRx-Dementia (intervention). We enrolled (12/2020-2/2024) English-speaking dementia caregivers agreeing to receive text messages who lived in a 62 ZIP code geography around an urban academic medical center. We assessed caregiver self-efficacy (primary, 12 months), loneliness, need for help and self-reported hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits (other pre-specified outcomes). Pre-planned, main analyses included participants with ≥ 1 baseline health-related social risk (HRSRs); post hoc analyses included caregivers without baseline HRSRs.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Caregivers with HRSRs (n = 133) were predominantly female (84%) and Black (79%); 52% had household income < $50 K/year; 94% texted a navigator and 31% requested additional resource information. Caregiver self-efficacy (range 1-5, intervention = 3.5; control = 3.5, odds ratio [OR]: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.30, 2.09) and rates of loneliness (intervention = 41%; control = 50%; OR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.24, 1.59), needing help (23% = intervention, 34% = control; OR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.30, 2.11) and hospitalization (intervention = 0.1, control = 0.2; IRR: 0.42, 95% CI: 0.14, 1.30) were similar at 12 months, but ED utilization was lower in the intervention group (0.3 vs. 0.7, IRR: 0.41, 95% CI: 0.19, 0.90). Caregivers without HRSRs (n = 210) were mainly female (75%) and Black (82%); 25% had household income < $50 K/year; 95% texted a navigator and 39% requested additional resource information. Self-efficacy, loneliness, hospitalizations, and ED utilization were similar between arms at 12 months, but odds of needing help were 0.31 (95% CI: 0.12, 0.83) for the intervention group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A low-intensity social care intervention aimed at dementia caregivers did not improve self-efficacy at 12 months but reduced emergency care utilization among those with HRSRs.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov, Registered 10/29/19, Identifier: NCT04146545.

articles.title: Paramedic perspectives on organ donation after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Rhabdo-RRT score: development and external validation of an emergency department tool for predicting renal replacement therapy in rhabdomyolysis.
Counterfeit and unregulated GLP-1 receptor agonists: an unmeasured variable in emergency department procedural sedation risk.
Arthroscopic Bankart versus the open Latarjet procedure for anterior-inferior shoulder instability in young males: a randomised controlled trial with minimum 5-year follow-up.
Short hospital contacts without documented in-hospital intervention following emergency medical services transport in the Central Denmark Region: a population-based cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To identify and characterise emergency medical services (EMS)-conveyed patients with short hospital stays without documented in-hospital intervention, and compare mortality across groups.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Population-based cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Tax-funded EMS system in the Central Denmark Region, covering emergency calls from January 2022 to December 2023.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: EMS-attended patient contacts with a completed prehospital record and linkage to hospital data. Interfacility transfers and missions cancelled before patient contact were excluded. Patients were classified as non-conveyed or, if transported, by hospital-contact duration and documented procedures, medication or diagnostic imaging.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Prehospital characteristics, hospital diagnoses and resource use and short-term mortality across the four study groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 89 560 emergency calls resulting in EMS dispatch, 13 539 (15.1%) patients were non-conveyed after on-scene assessment and 76 021 (84.9%) were transported. Among transported patients, 14 551 (19.1%) had a hospital contact ≤6 hours without documented in-hospital procedures, medication or diagnostic imaging. This group was younger, had lower comorbidity, fewer markers of pronounced physiological compromise and was frequently discharged with non-specific diagnoses. Short-term mortality, defined as death on the index date or during the following two calendar days, was 0.4% among short stays without intervention, <0.1% among non-conveyed patients, 1.7% among short stays with intervention and 1.3% among stays >6 hours. Compared with stays >6 hours, absolute risk differences were −0.95 percentage points (95% CI −1.09 to −0.81), −1.27 (95% CI −1.38 to −1.16) and 0.40 (0.16 to 0.63), respectively. Among transported patients, index-day mortality was 0.2%, 1.4% and 0.2% in short stays without intervention, short stays with intervention and stays >6 hours, respectively. Among index-day survivors, corresponding mortality during days 1–7 was 0.2%, 0.6% and 2.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Nearly one-fifth of hospital contacts following EMS transport were short stays without documented intervention. Low short-term mortality supports prospective evaluation of prehospital risk stratification and alternative care pathways.

articles.title: Gastroduodenal artery pseudoaneurysm presenting as severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding in an adolescent: transarterial embolisation.

abstract.text: An adolescent male presented with severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding following recent non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use given after a neurosurgical procedure. On postoperative day 9 following this intervention, he presented to an outside emergency department with abdominal pain and constipation and was managed conservatively. On postoperative day 14, he re-presented with melena, syncope and haemodynamic instability consistent with haemorrhagic shock. Endoscopy demonstrated a large adherent clot along the posterior wall of the duodenal bulb that could not be dislodged despite extensive lavage, preventing identification of the underlying bleeding source. Haemostatic spray was applied; however, given persistent concern for an underlying vascular lesion, mesenteric angiography demonstrated a gastroduodenal artery pseudoaneurysm with active contrast extravasation. Selective transarterial coil embolisation achieved definitive haemostasis. The patient stabilised with no further bleeding. Follow-up endoscopy demonstrated ulcer healing with mild asymptomatic duodenal stenosis. This case highlights the importance of considering vascular causes in severe paediatric upper gastrointestinal bleeding and supports early angiographic evaluation when endoscopic assessment is inconclusive or definitive haemostasis is not feasible.

articles.title: The Psychological Impact of Sudden Unexplained Death in Childhood: Associations Between Early Professional Interactions and Long-Term Distress Among Bereaved Caregivers.

abstract.text: Each year, approximately 500 U.S. children aged 1-18 years die suddenly and without explanation. Sudden Unexplained Death in Childhood (SUDC) is a devastating loss with profound psychological consequences for caregivers. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 174 caregivers whose child's death was classified as SUDC at least one year earlier. Using a trauma-informed framework, we assessed anxiety (GAD-7), depression (PHQ-9), prolonged grief (BGQ), posttraumatic stress disorder (PCL-6), functional impairment (WSAS), and experiences with emergency medical services (EMS) and emergency department (ED) personnel. Moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression were reported by 26.4% and 22.4% of caregivers, respectively, and 35.4% had probable PTSD. Distress was greatest among caregivers whose loss occurred 1-2 years earlier and those aged ≤40 years. Nearly half reported neutral or negative interactions with EMS and ED personnel, highlighting the need for trauma-informed training for professionals supporting families following a child's sudden and unexplained death.

articles.title: Impact of earthquake-related mass casualty burden on hospital microbial ecology and surgical site infections after elective orthopaedic surgery: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to compare surgical site infections (SSIs) developing after primary elective orthopaedic procedures before and after the 6th February, 2023, earthquakes and to investigate the incidence, causative pathogen distribution, and antimicrobial resistance patterns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing primary total or partial hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, or open reduction and internal fixation. The patients were divided into pre-earthquake (1st June, 2018-5th February, 2023) and postearthquake (1st June, 2023-1st November, 2025) periods. The SSI cases were defined according to periprosthetic joint infection (International Consensus Meeting [ICM] 2025) and fracture-related infection (FRI 2018) criteria. Microbiological profiles, resistance patterns, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 99 and 118 SSI cases were identified in the pre- and postearthquake cohorts, respectively. Overall SSI rates were similar between groups (0.98% vs 1.19%; P = 0.143). However, postearthquake infections were associated with significantly longer hospital stays (28 vs 22 days; P = 0.025) and increased debridement procedures (2.0 vs 1.0; P = 0.006). Polymicrobial infections increased significantly (12.1% vs 23.7%; P = 0.028). A marked microbiological shift was observed, with Gram-negative organisms becoming predominant (67.7% vs 47.6%; P = 0.004), whereas Gram-positive organisms decreased. Staphylococcus aureus isolation significantly declined (35.4% vs 17.2%; P = 0.008). Meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased (34.9% vs 60.0%; P = 0.022), whereas no significant change in Gram-negative carbapenem resistance was observed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our study results showed that the rates of polymicrobial infections and meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased significantly. This microbiological shift was also associated with clinically relevant outcomes, including prolonged hospital stays and an increased number of debridement procedures. Taken together, in centres exposed to a high burden of mass casualty patients, the infection dynamics of routine elective surgical cases may continue to evolve even months after the disaster. Reassessment of existing empirical treatment protocols is warranted in such settings.

articles.title: Personal VOC exposure in a multi-source open-air mass gathering environment: An integrated passive air and biomonitoring study.

abstract.text: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are ubiquitous air pollutants emitted from diverse everyday sources and are public health concerns. University festivals attract thousands of participants and constitute fully open-air environments with diverse emission sources, including crowd-related dust, stage effects, and cooking activities. However, studies assessing personal VOC exposure in such multi-source festival settings remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate personal VOC exposure in a fully open-air, multi-source university festival by integrating personal air sampling with urinary biomonitoring. This study measured VOC concentrations during the performances (18:00-22:00) on the first day of a university festival held in Jeonbuk, Korea, in May 2025. VOC exposure was assessed by measuring 10 VOCs using expanded polytetrafluoroethylene passive samplers and 7 urinary metabolites. Thirty participants wore neck and wrist samplers during the event, and urine samples were collected before and after the event. VOCs and their metabolites were assessed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry and high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, respectively. On the festival day, 9 of 10 VOCs were detected in over 70% of samples. Compared with the non-festival days, concentrations of o-xylene, styrene, limonene, α-pinene, and β-pinene measured by passive samplers increased significantly-by approximately 1.8-21.1 times-at both the neck and wrist during the performances. In addition, urinary metabolite concentrations of o-, m,p-, and o,m,p-methylhippuric acids, mandelic acid, and phenylglyoxylic acid were significantly higher after the festival than before, showing increases of approximately 1.3-2.0 times. This study indicates increased VOC exposure in both personal air and urine samples during the university festival. To support sustainable festival management, appropriate strategies to reduce VOC exposure should be formulated.

articles.title: FDMSNet: A frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid framework for renewable energy power forecasting.

abstract.text: Accurate renewable energy power forecasting is of great significance for the safe operation, dispatch optimization, and efficient management of modern power systems. However, wind and photovoltaic power generation series usually exhibit significant non-stationarity, volatility, and multi-scale variation characteristics, posing great challenges to medium- and long-term forecasting. To address these issues, this paper proposes FDMSNet, a frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid network for renewable energy power forecasting. The model first divides the input sequence into non-stationary and stationary components through a frequency decomposition module. For the non-stationary component, a multilayer perceptron is adopted to extract global nonlinear variation features. For the stationary component, a multi-scale forecasting module is designed based on multi-branch downsampling and cross-scale prediction fusion. Subsequently, the forecasting results of different components are fused to generate the final power prediction. Experiments are conducted on real-world wind farm and photovoltaic power station datasets under multiple prediction horizons. MAE, MSE, and RSE are used as evaluation metrics, and FDMSNet is compared with different types of forecasting models. The experimental results show that FDMSNet achieves strong forecasting accuracy and stability in both wind and photovoltaic power forecasting tasks. Further average ranking analysis, significance testing, ablation experiments, and parameter sensitivity analysis verify the effectiveness and robustness of the frequency decomposition module, the multi-scale modeling structure, and the key parameter settings.

articles.title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance - a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. The aim of this study was to determine whether creatine monohydrate loading improves BH exercise performance in trained BH divers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study assessed the effects of a 7-day creatine monohydrate loading protocol (20 g/day) on performance outcomes and fatigue markers during BH exercise performed on a bicycle ergometer in 20 trained BH divers (18 males, 2 females; mean age 41.6 ± 8.6 years). The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07233707) on 16th November 2025 under the title Load and Hold: Impact of 7-Day Creatine Monohydrate Loading on Breath-Hold Cycling Performance (BREATHE-C). Testing consisted of a brief warm-up followed by a maximal cycling trial performed on a single breath, during which participants aimed to cover the greatest possible distance. Following pre-supplementation testing, participants were randomly assigned to either the creatine monohydrate (CR) or the placebo (PL) group. Pre- and post-supplementation measurements included total work (TW), time to exhaustion (TTE), peripheral blood lactate accumulation (LA), mean partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO₂) in exhaled air following BH exercise, and ratings of perceived exertions for BH (RPE-BH) and muscle fatigue (RPE-MF). In addition, participants underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry to assess changes in body composition.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant Time × Group interactions were observed for TW (p = 0.011), TTE (p = 0.028), and fat-free mass (p = 0.017), with greater changes observed following creatine supplementation compared to PL. Furthermore, there was a significant Time × Group interaction for LA (p = 0.003), with greater changes observed in the PL group compared to CR. No significant between-group differences were observed for pCO₂, RPE-BH, RPE-MF, fat mass, or total body mass.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Creatine enhanced performance, as reflected by increases in TW and TTE, without elevating RPE-BH, although a slight increase in RPE-MF was observed.
