LA was lower in the CR compared to PL group, despite greater performance improvements. Overall, creatine appears to enhance BH exercise performance in trained BH divers, suggesting a potentially effective ergogenic strategy for BH-related sports.

articles.title: First responders' experiences and training needs at the scene of a suspected suicide in Ireland: A mixed methods study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: First responders are categorised as those who are the first to respond to emergency calls and attend the site of an emergency. They include, but are not limited to police, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and water safety personnel. First responders play a critical role in suicide postvention, supporting those bereaved by suicide and preventing adverse outcomes. However, many responders feel uncertain about how to effectively support those bereaved by suicide and often lack formal postvention training. This study aimed to explore and understand the experiences and training needs of first responders when attending the scene of a suspected suicide.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A mixed-method approach was adopted. A national quantitative survey with first responders was conducted. The impact of previous suicide-related training on suicide literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge was analysed using multivariate ANOVA, adjusting for sociodemographic factors. Qualitative data were collected through focus groups and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1587 first responders completed surveys. Participants demonstrated positive and non-stigmatising attitudes towards suicide prevention and suicidal individuals, though lower scores were achieved for suicide literacy, postvention knowledge, organisation support, and preparedness. Previous suicide-related training was significantly associated with higher literacy, attitudes, and postvention knowledge, although effect-sizes were small. Qualitative findings from 10 focus groups revealed substantial gaps in training and confidence when responding to suspected suicides. Participants also described the considerable emotional toll of attending the scene and emphasised the need for support in the aftermath.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Attending the scene of a suspected suicide has an impact on first responders. Limited suicide prevention and postvention training creates challenges, particularly in communicating with the bereaved. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive suicide prevention and postvention training and the allocation of adequate support.

articles.title: Shark Bites in Florida Are Underreported: A Multi-Dataset Analysis.

abstract.text: IntroductionThere is uncertainty about the number of shark bites on humans in Florida (FL).MethodsThe International Shark Attack File (ISAF) and Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) databases (2016-2024) were compared with the non-inpatient FL Ambulatory and Emergency Department Patient Data database (AHCA) (2018-2023) and the National Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Information System (NEMSIS) (2016-2024).ResultsBetween 2016-2024 there were 244 FL shark encounters reported in ISAF (mean 27.1 per year), 214 in GSAF (mean 23.8 per year), and 293 in a merged ISAF and GSAF (mean 32.6 per year). Between 2020-2023, there were 373 FL shark encounters reported in AHCA (mean 62.2 per year) compared with 114 encounters reported in NEMSIS (mean 22.8 per year) for 2020-2024. The rate ratio for AHCA FL shark encounters compared to the merged ISAF and GSAF was 1.91 (95% CI 1.64-2.23); p < .001. The percentage of shark encounters in Volusia County, FL, compared with all of FL shark encounters showed no significant differences between the ISAF and GSAF (40.2% and 33.6%, respectively) (p = .16) and between the AHCA and NEMSIS (7.2% and 7.5%, respectively) (p = 1.0). However, when comparing either ISAF or GSAF with either AHCA or NEMSIS, there were significant differences (p < .001 for all).DiscussionThe AHCA dataset identified about twice as many shark bites as either the ISAF or GSAF. Many FL shark encounters did not require EMS or admission to the hospital. The discrepancy in the number of shark encounters attributed to Volusia County, FL, varied based on the dataset being examined.

articles.title: From call to home: The role of dispatcher-assisted CPR in patient survival.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Dispatcher-assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (DA-CPR) is a key strategy to reduce no-flow time in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet its impact on long-term survival remains various across emergency medical systems.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: We aimed to evaluate the association between DA-CPR and resuscitation outcomes in a nationwide cohort of OHCA patients presenting with an initial shockable rhythm.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational study including all adult OHCA cases with ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (VF/VT) in which resuscitation was carried out by emergency medical services in Hungary during 2019, 2022, and 2023. Patients were stratified according to whether DA-CPR was ongoing upon ambulance arrival, or initiated by the ambulance crew. Primary outcomes were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and hospital admission with sustained circulation. Utstein-style consensus reporting guidelines were followed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 3,674 VF/VT OHCA cases were included, of whom 1,744 (47.5%) received DA-CPR. Patients in the DA-CPR group had significantly higher rates of ROSC (92.0% vs. 12.4%), hospital admission with sustained circulation (90.8% vs. 11.7%), 30-day survival (54.6% vs. 7.1%), and one-year survival (45.8% vs. 6.2%) compared with those without DA-CPR (all P < 0.001). DA-CPR occurrence increased over time, while declined in 2022 followed by partial recovery in 2023.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this nationwide cohort of OHCA patients with shockable rhythms, dispatcher-assisted CPR was strongly associated with improved early resuscitation success and long-term survival. These findings support DA-CPR as a critical system-level intervention and highlight the importance of centralised protocols and continuous performance monitoring.

articles.title: Wireless versus cart-based ultrasound in musculoskeletal and superficial soft-tissue imaging: a prospective blinded cross-over study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Wireless ultrasound probes are increasingly used in point-of-care settings, but their performance in musculoskeletal and superficial soft-tissue imaging remains incompletely defined. This study compared image quality and clinical-pragmatic performance of a wireless ultrasound probe with a high-end cart-based ultrasound system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective blinded cross-over study included 41 musculoskeletal or superficial soft-tissue anatomical regions examined in routine clinical practice. Each region was assessed with both the Mindray Resona I9 Elite Edition cart-based system and the Mindray TE-Air e5M wireless probe. Device order was randomized. Images were acquired by one experienced operator, anonymized, coded, and reviewed offline by an experienced reviewer blinded to device type. Image quality, anatomical margin definition, tissue contrast, speckle noise, diagnostic confidence, interpretability, diagnosis possibility, pathological finding detection, clinical decision sufficiency, and the need for further imaging were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cart-based system showed superior image quality. Median global image quality was 5 versus 3, anatomical margin definition 5 versus 3 and tissue contrast 5 versus 4. Diagnostic confidence was higher with the cart-based system, 97.95 ± 5.32 versus 69.10 ± 16.05. Clinical-pragmatic endpoints showed a less pronounced reduction: examination interpretability was 97.6% versus 90.2%, diagnosis was considered possible in 73.2% versus 61.0%, and images were sufficient for clinical decision-making in 70.7% versus 58.5%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The wireless probe provided lower image quality and confidence but retained clinically useful performance in selected cases. It should be considered complementary rather than a substitute for high-end cart-based ultrasound.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Effects Associated with the Female Athlete Triad: Emerging Evidence Statement from the Female and Male Athlete Triad Coalition.

abstract.text: This is an emerging evidence statement from the Female and Male Athlete Triad Coalition. This paper complements the 2025 updates to the Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statements addressing the State of the Science and Clinical Guidelines for Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment and Return to Play. This paper examines emerging evidence of cardiovascular alterations in Triad-affected female athletes with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea and functional hypothalamic oligomenorrhea, including vascular, hemodynamic, autonomic and lipid perturbations. The clinical significance of these surrogate markers of cardiovascular function and their long-term cardiovascular implications remain to be determined. Notwithstanding, the current work extends existing Triad frameworks by recognizing cardiovascular perturbations potentially associated with energy deficiency and hypoestrogenism as an important consideration in female athlete health. We outline an evidence-informed research framework, including longitudinal, dose-response, and multimodal assessments, to characterize the onset, magnitude, physiological significance, and reversibility of cardiovascular alterations in athletes with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea and functional hypothalamic oligomenorrhea. By integrating evidence from sports physiology, endocrinology, and cardiovascular medicine, this state-of-the-science synthesis provides a roadmap for future research, screening, and intervention strategies. It also underscores the importance of evaluating cardiovascular health as a potential component of the broader physiological consequences of energy deficiency, alongside menstrual dysfunction, and impaired bone health.

articles.title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review.

abstract.text: This narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search. Candidate references were screened manually against pre-specified eligibility criteria by a single reviewer, with the search parameters independently verified by the senior author. Of 71 records identified, 63 met the inclusion criteria. The included studies comprised 32 original studies, 10 systematic or scoping reviews, 20 narrative or operational papers, and one guideline. In CBRN scenarios, lung ultrasound demonstrated sensitivities of 90-97% for COVID-19 pneumonia versus 60-69% for chest radiography while minimizing healthcare worker exposure. For blast and ballistic injuries, FAST showed a pooled sensitivity of 92.1% (95% CI: 87.8-95.6) and specificity of 98.7% (95% CI: 96.0-99.9) for intra-abdominal hemorrhage. In natural disasters, ultrasound altered management in up to 44% of patients. Post-disaster applications included vascular access, tube confirmation, and complication monitoring. Ultraportable POCUS demonstrates diagnostic utility and operational feasibility across multiple disaster domains. However, evidence quality varies significantly, and standardized protocols remain lacking. Prospective studies linking ultrasound deployment to improved patient outcomes are needed. KEY POINTS: Question When disasters disable conventional imaging, how does ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography perform for diagnosis, triage, and procedural guidance across the four domains of disaster medicine? Findings Across 63 studies, FAST reached 92.1% pooled sensitivity for hemoperitoneum, lung ultrasound 90-97% versus 60-69% for radiography; management changed in up to 44%. Critical relevance statement This review critically appraises ultraportable ultrasound across all four disaster domains, showing that radiation-free bedside imaging accelerates triage, conserves scarce CT capacity, and extends radiological expertise through tele-guidance, while exposing an evidence base still lacking prospective outcome data.

articles.title: Prehospital recognition of sepsis is associated with earlier antibiotic administration in the emergency department : A retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early antibiotic administration is crucial in the treatment of sepsis. The impact of prehospital sepsis recognition remains unclear. We investigated whether an emergency medical services (EMS) suspicion of sepsis was associated with earlier antibiotic administration after patients arrived at the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational cohort study involving adult patients (≥ 18 years) admitted via EMS between January 2022 and June 2025 with a sepsis diagnosis made in the ED. Prehospital sepsis recognition was defined as documentation of the term "sepsis" in the EMS protocol. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients who received antibiotic treatment within 1 h of ED admission. Logistic regression was used to adjust for age, sex, and illness severity (quick sequential organ failure assessment [qSOFA]).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 134 patients (43% female; mean age 71 ± 15 years). The EMS suspected sepsis in 30 patients (22%). Among these, 63.3% received antibiotics within 1 h of ED admission, compared with 19.2% of patients without an EMS suspicion (p < 0.001). The median time to antibiotic administration was shorter in the EMS suspected group (32.0 min, interquartile range, IQR 16.5-76.8 min versus 124.5 min, IQR 72.5-211.5 min; p < 0.001). Prehospital sepsis suspicion was independently associated with antibiotic administration within 1h (adjusted odds ratio, OR 5.77, 95% confidence interval, CI 2.14-16.4; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prehospital recognition of sepsis by EMS was strongly associated with earlier antibiotic treatment after ED admission. This highlights the potential of systematic sepsis detection in prehospital settings.

articles.title: Teleassistance and Artificial Intelligence to Support Prehospital Triage by Emergency Nurses: A Scoping Review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: To map and critically synthesize international evidence on the use of teleassistance and artificial intelligence to support emergency nurses in prehospital triage.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping emergency care systems. In Europe, emergency nurses working within dispatch and telecommunication centers (112/118; 112 being the pan-European emergency number and 118 being the Italian national emergency medical service number) increasingly manage remote assessments using video and algorithmic tools. However, evidence on their impact, safety, and integration into clinical practice remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Searches in PubMed, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and Embase (2005-2024) identified studies involving nurses using teleassistance or artificial intelligence in prehospital triage. The protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework. Data were synthesized narratively, and the methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The search identified 1214 records. After removing 304 duplicates, 910 titles and abstracts were screened independently by 2 reviewers, of which 165 reports were sought for retrieval in full text. Of note, 72 reports (43.6%) could not be retrieved, principally reflecting restricted full-text access rather than deliberate exclusion. The remaining 93 reports were assessed for eligibility, and only 5 studies met the inclusion criteria: 2 experimental studies on video calls, 2 observational studies on digital and artificial intelligence triage systems, and 1 qualitative study on cognitive processes in telephone triage. Video teleassistance was associated with fewer inappropriate ED transfers and increased professional confidence. Digital and artificial intelligence systems were associated with improved triage consistency and timeliness. The qualitative study illustrated the high cognitive complexity of remote assessment. The mean Joanna Briggs Institute quality score was 83%, with no high-risk studies.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This scoping review maps a small but consistent body of evidence indicating that teleassistance and artificial intelligence can strengthen the accuracy, timeliness, and confidence of emergency nurses during remote triage, while confirming that structured governance, training, and human oversight remain essential and that further nurse-led research is needed.

articles.title: Living status and multidomain clinical outcomes in adults following acute mild traumatic brain injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to evaluate the role of living status in multidomain clinical outcomes in adults following acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Adults presenting to emergency departments or a specialty concussion clinic within < 72 hours (h) of mTBI were enrolled. Multidomain clinical measures (e.g. Concussion Clinical Profile Screen [CP Screen], Patient Health Questionnaire 9 [PHQ-9], Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist [PCL-5], Perceived Stress Scale [PSS]) were collected at <72 h and 10 days (d) post-injury. Participants were grouped by living status: alone (Alone), with a spouse/significant other/roommate (Cohabitant), or with a partner and children/extended family (Family). Two-way mixed-effects models evaluated the interaction of group and time on clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: One hundred fourteen participants (age = 33.2 ± 13.8 years; 63F) were enrolled: 27 (24%) in the Alone group, 41 (36%) Cohabitant, and 46 (40%) Family. A significant interaction was observed for the CP Screen Cognitive/Fatigue (F[2,51] = 5.5, p = 0.007), PHQ-9 (F[2,49] = 4.3, p = 0.020), PCL-5 (F[2,51] = 3.3, p = 0.044), and PSS (F[2,50] = 3.9 , p = 0.027). The Alone group exhibited significant increases in Cognitive/Fatigue problems (Δ3.1, p < 0.001), depression symptoms (Δ5.4, p < 0.001), and PTSD (Δ10.1, p = 0.006), but a significant decrease in perceived stress (Δ-4.5, p = 0.012) over time compared to the Cohabitant and Family groups (p > 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Adults living alone demonstrated a significant increase in cognitive/fatigue, depression, and stress-related symptoms from <72 h to 10d post-mTBI compared to those living with a cohabitant/family.

articles.title: Incorporating Realism: Damage Zone-Based Population Sorting for Nuclear Detonation Modeling.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Response agencies use mathematical modeling to quantify the consequences of mass-casualty incidents. Medical consequence models estimate the number of people to be treated for their injuries and rely on triage protocols based on injury severity to estimate the number of people who are expected to die. Available models ignore the time required to be rescued, which presents an incomplete picture of how many people would live long enough to be rescued and treated. We propose a new damage zone-based population sorting algorithm to improve estimates of people who would require treatment after a nuclear detonation in a U.S. urban setting.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We expanded the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR)nuclear detonation model to include specific blast injuries such as casualties with fractures or hemorrhage. We evaluated 3 population sorting methods: no sorting (i.e., count everyone as treatable), sorting based on Department of War (DOW)/North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) expectant rules, and damage zone-based population sorting. Damage zone-based population sorting introduces a new population category termed unrescuable, who are expected to die before being rescued based on the damage zone, injury severity, and the expected timing of response operations. We assessed the impact of population sorting on the number of injured and the number of injuries to be treated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Damage zone-based sorting significantly decreases the estimates of expectants and increases estimates of the population requiring medical treatment for the most serious trauma injuries compared to population sorting based on DOW/NATO expectant rules.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The new damage zone-based population sorting method represents an important modeling refinement that incorporates realism into modeling results estimating the number of trauma-injured people requiring treatment and numbers of specific trauma injuries that would need to be treated in the aftermath of a nuclear detonation. We saw that the choice of population sorting method can influence the allocation of medical countermeasures required to respond in mass-casualty incidents, impacting medical countermeasure requirements, development, and investments.

articles.title: Pilot Evaluation of a Modular Simulation Training Program Incorporating Radiation Source-Free Modules for Nuclear Disaster Preparedness Among Public Health Officials in Japan.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Public health officials hold critical roles in nuclear emergencies, but repeated, scenario-based training is often hindered by regulatory and safety constraints surrounding the use of radioactive sources. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary educational outcomes of a modular training program incorporating radiation source-free simulation modules for public health officials.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed a half-day program integrating augmented reality (AR) for simulated contamination searches and a radiation source-free measurement system (USOTOPE). Twenty local government public health officials participated; paired pre-post analyses included 19 participants. Assessments measured radiation-related knowledge and self-rated procedural confidence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Analysis of 19 participants showed significant improvements in knowledge (P = 0.001) and procedural confidence (P < 0.001). Item-level analyses suggested larger improvements in practical contamination management and context-specific knowledge, whereas some items addressing procedural details showed smaller changes. Participants rated the AR and USOTOPE modules as highly realistic and educationally valuable. The radiation source-free simulation modules were feasible to implement without dedicated radioactive sources or specialized source-management requirements.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This modular training program incorporating radiation source-free simulation modules was associated with short-term improvements in knowledge and procedural confidence among public health officials. Further validation using objective measures of operational performance and preparedness is warranted.

articles.title: Shifts in Dermatology Outpatient Diagnostic Patterns Following a Major Earthquake: A Comparative Pre- and Post-Disaster Study.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare dermatologic outpatient diagnostic frequencies before and after the February 6, 2023 Hatay earthquake and to evaluate the implications of these temporal changes for disaster-responsive dermatologic care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study compared tertiary-center dermatology outpatient diagnosis records from the pre-earthquake (February 6, 2021-February 3, 2023) and post-earthquake (May 11, 2023-February 6, 2025) periods. Diagnoses were classified into 18 categories and 69 ICD-10-coded subdiagnoses. Logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and calendar month using patient-clustered robust standard errors; aORs with 95% CIs and FDR-adjusted q values were reported.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 41,012 diagnosis records, 19,646 were from the pre-earthquake period and 21,366 from the post-earthquake period. After adjustment, infestations/insect bites were more frequently represented in the post-earthquake diagnostic mix (aOR 2.55, q < 0.001). Dermatitis (aOR 1.17, q < 0.001), bacterial diseases (aOR 1.58, q < 0.001), environmentally induced diseases (aOR 1.51, q = 0.003), and sexually transmitted diseases (aOR 1.50, q < 0.001) were also more frequently represented. Acneiform disorders were less frequently represented (aOR 0.61, q < 0.001). Despite a crude increase, fungal infections did not differ significantly in the adjusted analysis (aOR 1.04, q = 0.149).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Post-earthquake records showed more infestations and selected infectious and environmentally related diagnoses, but lower representation of some chronic disorders. These clinic-based associations support dermatologic surveillance, infection control, and continuity of care in disaster planning without implying population-level prevalence changes or causal earthquake effects.

articles.title: A generation in mourning: War-related bereavement and mental health among young adults.

abstract.text: War and mass-casualty events expose civilians to sudden loss, yet the mental health consequences of war-related bereavement among young adults remain underexamined. This study assessed associations between war-related bereavement and mental health outcomes during the ongoing war in Israel. An online survey of 948 young adults (18-30 years) was conducted between July and September 2025. Exposures included war-related and non-war-related bereavement. Outcomes were posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS), depressive symptoms, and mental well-being. Multivariable regression models adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, war-related stressors, health factors, and resilience resources. Overall, 30.4% reported war-related bereavement. War-related bereavement was associated with higher PTSS and depressive symptoms and lower well-being; non-war-related bereavement was associated with depressive symptoms only. Economic hardship, media exposure, and poor health were linked to worse outcomes, whereas resilience and social support were protective. War-related bereavement is an important risk factor for distress among young adults in conflict settings.

articles.title: Calprotectin as a Prognostic Marker for Sepsis Independent of Renal Dysfunction.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The role of calprotectin in sepsis pathophysiology is becoming increasingly recognized; however, optimal biomarkers for sepsis prognosis are lacking. We compared the prognostic accuracy of calprotectin with that of established biomarkers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this single-center prospective cohort study, patients who met the Sepsis-3 criteria were recruited between December 2022 and January 2024. Blood samples were collected at sepsis recognition (day 0) in the emergency department and on days 3 and 7 during the intensive care unit admission.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ninety patients with community-onset sepsis were included (median age, 79 yrs [69-85]; 51 women [56.7%]), and 17 patients (18.9%) died during hospitalization. Pneumonia was the most common etiology in both survivors and non-survivors. Calprotectin showed good prognostic performance across all time points, without significant temporal differences (area under the curve [AUC], day 0, 0.785 [95% confidence interval, 0.681-0.890]; day 3, 0.800 [0.680-0.921]; day 7, 0.813 [0.696-0.930]; all P <0.001). After estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) adjustment, the predictive performance of calprotectin was preserved, whereas presepsin and procalcitonin showed significant renal function dependency. Calprotectin did not significantly correlate with eGFR and showed good prognostic performance regardless of renal dysfunction status. Incremental value analyses revealed that serial calprotectin measurements provided no significant improvement over baseline assessment. In pneumonia-induced sepsis, calprotectin consistently showed the highest AUC, regardless of renal adjustment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Calprotectin demonstrated reliable prognostic performance for hospital mortality in community-onset sepsis independently of renal dysfunction, warranting validation in larger cohorts. A single measurement at initial presentation could provide clinically useful early prognostic information.

articles.title: ESR and CRP Testing in an Urban Emergency Department: Should We Still Be Doing This?

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Pediatricians in the Emergency Department frequently evaluate febrile children. To help identify the cause of fever and assess the severity of the underlying condition, practitioners often utilize erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein testing. While these markers of inflammation are deeply embedded in the practice of pediatrics, they were each developed more than 90 years ago, and their utility to current clinical practice is not well characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a 1-year retrospective study of children who underwent CRP and ESR testing at an urban Children's Hospital. We recorded and analyzed indications for testing, concordance between testing methods and metrics, including admission status and test performance, as reflected by sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ESR and CRP tests were frequently ordered in patients with clinically evident diagnoses. There were no cases of occult bacteremia, and patients with bacteremia typically had presentations indicative of bacterial infection. CRP was superior to ESR as a predictor of bacterial infection; however, the positive likelihood ratio was only 2.1. Combined testing was ordered for 39.4% of all CRP tests, and there was a high concordance (69.9%) between CRP and ESR testing. Combined testing offered limited incremental value for the detection of bacterial infections.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: CRP and ESR testing are currently overused in our Pediatric Emergency Department, providing limited diagnostic value while adding unnecessary hospital cost. Combined CRP and ESR testing provides limited incremental value. Stewardship of these testing modalities and an active reconsideration of how these tests are employed should be considered.

articles.title: Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers Presenting to a Pediatric Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterize the clinical presentation and management of anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 0 to 24 months presenting to a pediatric emergency department between June 2019 and June 2022 with concern for anaphylaxis. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth and 10th Revision codes associated with anaphylaxis and confirmed to meet 2006 National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases/Food Allergy and Anaphylaxis Network clinical criteria by chart review. Demographic and clinical information-including presenting symptoms, administered treatment, and patient disposition-were abstracted from the electronic medical record. Treatments of interest included epinephrine, antihistamines, corticosteroids, albuterol, and intravenous fluids. Data were analyzed descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 225 potentially eligible encounters, we identified 155 patients who met inclusion criteria. Median age was 10.8 months (interquartile range: 8.4 to 15.6). Food triggered 96.1% of episodes. Skin and mucosal symptoms occurred in 99.4% of patients, gastrointestinal symptoms in 74.2%, respiratory symptoms in 57.4%, and cardiovascular symptoms in 5.8%. Intramuscular epinephrine was administered to 87.1% of patients, 90.4% of whom received a single dose. Most patients (88.4%) were discharged home, and none of those admitted required additional epinephrine.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this cohort, reactions were most often food-triggered and characterized by mucocutaneous symptoms with gastrointestinal and/or mild-to-moderate respiratory symptoms. Severe respiratory or cardiovascular involvement was uncommon. Symptoms tended to resolve after a single dose of epinephrine, and most patients were discharged home.

articles.title: Gait Retraining for Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome: A Biomechanical Approach to Pain Relief and Performance Optimization.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) is common among runners and is linked to biomechanical dysfunctions that increase patellofemoral joint stress. Gait retraining has been proposed to redistribute this loading, but the effectiveness of different retraining strategies and their long-term impact remain unclear. This scoping review synthesizes existing evidence on gait retraining strategies for PFPS, focusing on pain, function, and biomechanics.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, PEDro, and Web of Science were searched, following the methodological framework of the Joanna Briggs Institute for scoping reviews. Studies investigating gait retraining interventions in runners diagnosed with PFPS were included. Key outcomes were pain reduction, functional improvement, biomechanical adaptations, and adverse effects.

abstract.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Three randomized controlled trials met the inclusion criteria, examining cadence modification, impact reduction, and foot strike adjustments. Intervention groups experienced significant pain reduction, with Visual Analog Scale scores improving by 2 to 4 points, alongside functional gains reflected by increased Kujala and Knee Outcome Survey of the Activities of Daily Living Scale scores. Biomechanical adaptations included decreased patellofemoral joint stress, lower impact forces, and improved load distribution. Some participants reported transient calf discomfort during the adaptation period, which resolved over time.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Gait retraining is an effective intervention for runners with PFPS, showing sustained pain relief, functional improvement, and biomechanical benefits. Individualized protocols and gradual implementation are essential to optimize outcomes and minimize discomfort. Future research should address long-term retention of gait modifications, optimal training parameters, and applicability beyond runners.

articles.title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

articles.title: Ten-Year Experience with Combined Hyperbaric Oxygen and Steroid Therapy for Idiopathic Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss: A Retrospective Cohort of 332 Patients.
articles.journal_full: The journal of international advanced otology

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) combined with systemic corticosteroids in patients with idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL), with particular focus on treatment timing, predictors of hearing recovery, and the impact of comorbidities.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center (AOU "San Giovanni di Dio e Ruggi d'Aragona," Salerno, Italy). A total of 332 adult patients with ISSNHL treated between 2014 and 2024 were included. All patients received combined therapy with systemic corticosteroids (oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, tapered over 10-15 days) and HBOT (2.4 atmospheres absolute, 90 minutes per session; median of 10 sessions). Audiometric outcomes were assessed using pure-tone average (PTA). Treatment response was defined as a ≥30% improvement in PTA compared with baseline. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of hearing improvement. Safety outcomes were also recorded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean baseline PTA was 61.3 ± 21.5 dB HL, improving to 44.6 ± 22.7 dB HL after treatment, with a mean hearing gain of 16.7 ± 14.2 dB HL (P < .001). Overall, 151 patients (43.5%) met the response criteria. Responders presented with significantly higher baseline PTA compared with nonresponders (67.6 vs. 56.8 dB HL, P < .001) and more frequently reported tinnitus (64.2% vs. 51.5%, P = .014). Median time to treatment initiation was 15 days (interquartile range: 7-30). Multivariate analysis identified shorter time to treatment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98), presence of tinnitus (OR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.15-2.80), and higher baseline PTA (OR: 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05) as independent predictors of hearing improvement. Common comorbidities, including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, were not significantly associated with treatment response. No serious adverse events related to HBOT were observed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy combined with systemic corticosteroids was associated with improved audiometric outcomes in patients with ISSNHL, particularly when initiated early. Shorter time to treatment, greater baseline hearing loss, and the presence of tinnitus emerged as independent predictors of hearing recovery. Overall, these findings suggest an association between early HBOT use and improved audiometric outcomes and support its consideration as an adjunctive component of multimodal treatment strategies for ISSNHL.

articles.title: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus bacteraemia with suspected infective endocarditis in a patient with bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement and atrial septal defect repair.

abstract.text: Introduction. Despite the established pathogenicity of Aggregatibacter aphrophilus, few clinical cases have been described in published literature. A. aphrophilus is a rare cause of prosthetic valve endocarditis and diagnosis is challenging based on nonspecific symptoms on presentation. High clinical suspicion for infective endocarditis is warranted in patients with cardiac prosthetic material and positive blood cultures. Poor dentition and dental procedures, along with other risk factors, are associated with A. aphrophilus bacteraemia. We describe a case of A. aphrophilus bacteraemia in which the diagnosis of infective endocarditis was complicated by equivocal echocardiographic findings and an initially challenging Gram stain interpretation. Case Presentation. A 59-year-old male patient with a history of bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, atrial septal defect repair and remote dental cleaning presented to the emergency department with persistent high fevers, headaches and lethargy. Initial blood cultures were drawn and were positive for 'Gram-positive organisms', but specific morphology was challenging to determine. Subsequent testing, including MALDI-TOF, confirmed the growth of A. aphrophilus. Conclusion. Rapid identification of A. aphrophilus and recognition of the potential for infective endocarditis are paramount to ensuring adequate treatment initiation and success. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty associated with initial Gram stain interpretation of this fastidious organism.

articles.title: Safety of Intravenous Ibuprofen Administration in the Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: The journal of pediatric pharmacology and therapeutics : JPPT : the official journal of PPAG

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Intravenous (IV) ibuprofen has recently been approved for treating moderate acute pain and fever, but evidence in pediatric use remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term safety of IV ibuprofen in children treated in a pediatric emergency department (PED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective observational study was conducted including children aged 6 months to younger than 14 years who received IV ibuprofen between January 2021 and September 2023 in a PED of a tertiary hospital. IV ibuprofen was administered for moderate acute pain or fever when oral administration was not feasible due to vomiting or the need for fasting before a potential surgical intervention. Physicians documented patient history, previous analgesia, reasons for consultation and IV ibuprofen administration, vital signs, pain scores (0-10) before and 10 minutes after administration, and any adverse events (AEs).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 287 patients, with a median age of 9 years (IQR, 6-11). No serious AEs occurred, and no hospital admissions were required due to IV ibuprofen. Mild AEs occurred in 15 patients (5.2%), most commonly transient pain or itching at the infusion site. One patient developed a mild skin rash leading to treatment discontinuation, with complete recovery. Pain scores showed a median reduction of 3 points (IQR, 2-4).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Short-term use of IV ibuprofen in the PED was associated with an acceptable safety profile and clinically relevant pain reduction. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate safety with repeated dosing or longer duration of use.

articles.title: Management of Bupropion Toxicity With Intravenous Lipid Emulsion Therapy in a Pediatric Patient: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: The journal of pediatric pharmacology and therapeutics : JPPT : the official journal of PPAG

abstract.text: This case report involves a 2-year-old female with no past medical history who presented after ingestion of an unknown amount of 300 mg bupropion extended-release tablets. Shortly after ingestion, the mother mechanically induced vomiting, which recovered only small pieces of the tablets. The patient remained asymptomatic for a short period, then she began vomiting and had several tonic-clonic seizures, leading to emergency medical service (EMS) being called and ultimately, intubation for airway protection. On arrival at the pediatric intensive care unit (estimated 6 hours post ingestion), the patient was unresponsive with fixed and dilated pupils and no cough, gag, or respiratory effort. An electrocardiogram revealed that the patient had a first-degree heart block with a prolonged QTc interval. The patient remained unresponsive while off sedation with no effort to breathe over the ventilator. A bolus of intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE) 1.5 mL/kg followed by a continuous infusion of 0.5 mL/kg/min was administered (estimated 8 hours post ingestion). A few minutes following the start of the infusion, the patient began to spontaneously breathe over the ventilator. The patient was successfully extubated within 36 hours after ILE, and within 72 hours the patient had recovered to baseline and discharged home. This case displays successful use of ILE for bupropion toxicity in a young child. More studies are needed to fully understand the benefits and potential risks of the use of ILE in this population.

articles.title: The Critical Role of Pharmacists in Addressing the Pediatric Mental Health Crisis: A Pediatric Pharmacy Association Position Paper.
articles.journal_full: The journal of pediatric pharmacology and therapeutics : JPPT : the official journal of PPAG

abstract.text: The significant rise in rates of depression and anxiety in children and adolescents coupled with underdiagnosis and undertreatment poses a serious health threat to the pediatric population. The escalating pediatric mental health crisis has been associated with rising suicide rates and attempts, increased deaths due to drug overdose, higher health care costs, and limited access to adequate care. A shortage of mental health resources and specialized providers in both community and institutional settings further exacerbates these challenges. This paucity of care highlights the need for additional support, and pharmacists, as accessible health professionals, can help bridge the gap in pediatric mental health care. Pharmacists play a vital role in pediatric mental health by advocating for and performing mental health screenings for pediatric patients presenting with acute psychological and behavioral health issues across various care settings, including emergency departments, inpatient units and outpatient pharmacies. Additionally, pharmacists enhance the efficacy and safety of psychotropic therapies in children with diagnosed mental health conditions by minimizing drug interactions, optimizing dosing, monitoring for adverse effects, and providing patient and family education. This article serves as a Position Statement of the Pediatric Pharmacy Association (PPA), which strongly advocates for the inclusion of pharmacists as key members of multidisciplinary teams supporting pediatric patients with mental health challenges, emphasizing their critical role in improving patient outcomes. Additionally, PPA advocates for routine mental health screenings for all pediatric patients and recommends utilization of referrals and standardized workflows for managing pediatric mental health conditions and substance use disorders.

articles.title: Trends and Outcomes of Voxelotor Treatment in Pediatric Patients With Sickle Cell Disease: A Retrospective Study.
articles.journal_full: The journal of pediatric pharmacology and therapeutics : JPPT : the official journal of PPAG

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is characterized by hemoglobin S polymerization, leading to anemia, pain, and organ damage. Voxelotor is a therapy for SCD that was withdrawn from worldwide markets in September 2024. We evaluated trends in voxelotor use and its impact on pediatric SCD patients before withdrawal.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective study was conducted using patient records from 4 Children's Healthcare of Atlanta (CHOA) hospitals. Data on patient demographics, length of time on voxelotor, clinical markers, hospital usage, side effects, and discontinuation reasons were analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Two hundred forty-five patients were taking voxelotor between 2019 and 2024 outside of clinical trials. Of these, 188 (77%) patients were on voxelotor for at least 6 consecutive months, with an average of 25.0 months on treatment. The main reason for discontinuation was due to a side effect (47%) for patients on treatment for less than 6 months and market withdrawal (69%) for those taking 6 months or more. On average, patients had a significant increase in mean hemoglobin (0.5 g/dL, p < 0.001), a decrease in hemolysis markers, and a mean decrease in annualized emergency department visits. At the time of market withdrawal, 123 patients were actively taking voxelotor.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Overall, patients had a positive hematologic and clinical response to voxelotor, with the majority remaining on treatment for at least 6 consecutive months. Despite market withdrawal due to safety and efficacy concerns, a subset of patients derived clinical benefits from voxelotor, highlighting the need for continued development of effective therapeutics for SCD.

articles.title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis-induced left ventricular (LV) dysfunction complicates fluid resuscitation, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema and worsening outcomes. Echocardiographic assessment is often delayed, and natriuretic peptides such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) have limited diagnostic accuracy in this setting. We evaluated a smartphone-based electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis application for screening LV dysfunction in patients with sepsis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, we included 425 adult sepsis patients from three university hospitals who underwent both a 12-lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiography within 72 hours of emergency department admission. ECG images displayed on a monitor were photographed and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based smartphone application (ECG Buddy™), which generated a quantitative digital biomarker for LV dysfunction (quantitative electrocardiogram scores for LV dysfunction [QCG-LVDys]). LV dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%. The diagnostic performance of QCG-LVDys for detecting LV dysfunction was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). A predefined comparison with NT-proBNP was performed in the single center where NT-proBNP was routinely measured.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the overall multicenter cohort, QCG-LVDys showed high diagnostic performance for LV dysfunction, with an ROC-AUC of 0.901. Using an optimized threshold (37.35), QCG-LVDys achieved a sensitivity of 89.6%, specificity of 75.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97.5%. In the NT-proBNP subset, QCG-LVDys outperformed NT-proBNP (ROC-AUC 0.911 vs. 0.637, P < 0.001). Higher QCG-LVDys values were associated with increased lactate levels (P = 0.002) and 28-day in-hospital mortality (P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.

articles.title: Work-related musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and dietary habits in athletic trainers and physical therapists providing sports team support.

abstract.text: BackgroundAthletic professionals (athletic trainers and physical therapists) perform injury prevention, health management, evaluation, emergency care, post-injury protection, rehabilitation, and administrative duties. Their focus on athletes' health may lead them to overlook high physical and psychosocial demands that may increase musculoskeletal pain (MSP), fatigue, and unhealthy dietary habits.ObjectiveTo examine MSP, fatigue, and dietary habits among athletic professionals who provide on-site team support and explore how fatigue and dietary habits relate to MSP.MethodsParticipants were required to be athletic professionals providing on-site team support. This cross-sectional online survey assessed 3-month work-related MSP in body regions, fatigue using a modified Fatigue Assessment Scale, and dietary habits using a structured food-frequency questionnaire. Logistic regression and mediation analyses examined associations and indirect associations, adjusting for relevant confounders.ResultsA total of 132 valid responses were included. MSP was highly prevalent, particularly in the lower back (83%), wrists/fingers (80%), and neck (67%). Fatigue (OR = 3.1, 95% CI = 1.34-7.45) and several suboptimal dietary habits (e.g., irregular meal timing, inadequate intake, fast eating, unbalanced diet, replacing meals with snacks, emotional eating) were significantly associated with MSP. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated statistically significant indirect associations via inadequate intake, replacing meals with snacks, and emotional eating, suggesting these behaviours may partially account for the fatigue-MSP association.ConclusionsAthletic professionals experience a high burden of MSP, fatigue, and suboptimal dietary habits that may be interrelated in ways that exacerbate work-related health. Workplace strategies should address workload, fatigue management, and access to healthy eating options to support sustainable practice and well-being.

articles.title: Community Paramedics Address Health Inequities Within EMS Through Mobile Integrated Healthcare (MIH) Program Referrals from a "Medical Home".

abstract.text: To advance local health equity, a large urban fire department's Mobile Integrated Healthcare (MIH) Unit worked with a Chicago-based health care organization to refer patients in "medical homes" to a MIH program. Medical home coordinators referred individuals to Community Paramedics (CPs) in the MIH Unit for program enrollment with a 4-visit model in 4 clinical pathways (hypertension, diabetes, asthma/Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease [COPD], and heart failure). A total of 911 utilization of ambulance transportation, emergency department (ED) visits, and inpatient hospitalizations before and after intervention were measured to gauge program impact. A postgraduation survey was distributed to participants. From November 2022 to March 2025, 68 referred individuals completed the program and graduated with a total of 321 in-person visits by CPs. Data were gathered for 6 months before program enrollment and 6 months post-intervention. The most common clinical pathway for graduated patients was hypertension (75%), diabetes (57%), asthma/COPD (47%), and heart failure (41%). Among graduated patients, there was a 43% decrease in 911 ambulance transports, a 46% decrease in ED utilization, and a 42% decrease in hospital admissions. The postgraduation survey was completed by 53% of program graduates; 81% reported symptom improvement, 58% indicated an improved relationship with their primary care clinic, and 74% agreed that CPs improved their overall health care experience. Creating a partnership between a patient's primary care medical home and a large urban fire department's MIH program is a successful strategy for decreasing 911 ambulance transports, ED utilization, and inpatient hospital admissions for individuals at risk for poor health outcomes.

articles.title: Injury surveillance, on-field rehabilitation and return-to-play criteria: A survey of current practices in male professional football.

abstract.text: Injuries in professional football present complex challenges to multiple stakeholders. Subsequent rehabilitation processes are guided by epidemiological research and rehabilitation frameworks providing objective criteria informing decision-making. Processes must constantly evolve to provide support and minimise subsequent injury risk. The aims of this exploratory study were to investigate current practices in injury surveillance, on-field rehabilitation (OFR) and return-to-play (RTP) criteria in male professional football. In total, 81 practitioners responded to an online survey consisting of 34 questions divided into four sections: 1) practitioner demographics, 2) injury data collection and monitoring, 3) OFR and RTP criteria, and 4) decision-making process for return-to-training and RTP. Results indicate that for injury data collection, variability exists in rehabilitation end-date classification, post-rehabilitation timeframes, and a potential disparity between subsequent injury classification and reporting. A range of external running load metrics and objective targets are used to monitor and progress OFR, indicating lack of consensus and availability of validated objective criteria. A multidisciplinary, shared decision-making approach is adopted, including input from players; however, communication was highlighted as a key area to improve. Findings of this study may be beneficial for practitioners developing internal rehabilitation procedures and for identifying future research gaps that could result in positive rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Pragmatic weight estimation for dosing of a new paediatric treatment for schistosomiasis prevention and control in preschool-aged children: a feasibility study in Uganda and Côte d'Ivoire.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Schistosomiasis remains a major public health concern in endemic settings. The Pediatric Praziquantel Consortium has developed a new paediatric treatment, arpraziquantel, for preschool-aged children. Because the treatment is dosed according to body weight, dose determination by scales poses operational challenges in community-based mass treatment campaigns. This study assessed the performance of the Pediatric Advanced Weight Prediction in the Emergency Room Extra-Long Mid-Arm Circumference (PAWPER XL-MAC) tape for weight estimation during mass drug administration in Uganda and Côte d'Ivoire.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A mixed-methods study evaluated feasibility in terms of accuracy, reliability and acceptability of the PAWPER XL-MAC tape across delivery platforms and users between March 2025 and March 2026. Accuracy metrics comprised (1) the mean relative difference and mean absolute relative difference between predicted (tape) and observed (scale) weight and (2) the proportion of estimates within 10% (PW10) and 20% (PW20) of observed weight. Reliability was evaluated by calculating the intraclass-correlation coefficient (ICC). User experiences were collected through observations, questionnaires, focus group discussions and in-depth interviews.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In Uganda (n = 3369), mean absolute differences were 11.0-11.1%; PW10 60.2-61.0%. In Côte d'Ivoire (n = 1249), accuracy was higher (6.8-7.7%; PW10 72.4-78.2%). Reliability was high between users and countries (ICCs ≥ 0.84). Sufficient time for practical training was essential to achieve solid performance. With continued use, an increase in confidence, efficiency, and accuracy was observed. Qualitative results indicated strong acceptability and practical advantages amongst users.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This is the first study to demonstrate that the PAWPER XL-MAC tape offers reliable, accurate, and acceptable weight estimation for community-based interventions, supporting its use in routine child healthcare and public health programmes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06698510, date of registration: 21.11.2024.

articles.title: Charting the rise of artificial intelligence in medical education: a global bibliometric and network analysis, 2000-2026.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral curiosity to a core feature of modern medical education through adaptive learning, simulation-based training, automated assessment, and large language models such as ChatGPT. Publication activity has accelerated rapidly, but the structure of this expanding literature has not been comprehensively mapped.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy that combined medical education terms in the title field with artificial intelligence terms in the topic field. Articles, review articles, and data papers published from 2000 to 2026 were included. A total of 2,298 records were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analyses, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct keyword co-occurrence, country collaboration, and institutional collaboration networks. Data for 2026 represent a partial calendar year.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Publication output remained limited until the late 2010s and rose sharply after 2021. Of the 2,298 records, 2,066 (89.9%) were published from 2021 to 2026, with the highest complete-year output in 2025 (821 publications). The United States led in publication volume (918 records) and raw citation count (14,582 citations), followed by the People's Republic of China (367 records; 4,404 citations). The Journal of Surgical Education published the most articles. Harvard Medical School led institutional output, whereas Stanford University and the University of California San Francisco had higher raw citation totals despite fewer publications. Artificial intelligence, medical education, ChatGPT, medical students, and machine learning were the most prominent keywords.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Artificial intelligence in medical education is a rapidly expanding but geographically and institutionally concentrated field. Raw citation patterns differed from publication volume, although these unadjusted measures should not be interpreted as direct comparisons of research quality. Thematic patterns emphasize learner-facing applications, assessment, and generative AI, while responsible curricular integration and empirical evaluation remain important priorities. These findings are especially relevant to emergency medicine education, where simulation, time-sensitive decision-making, and competency assessment are central.

articles.title: Conceptualising Health Economic Models Using a Graph Retrieval-Augmented, Agentic AI Framework with Human-in-the-Loop Validation: Proof-of-Concept Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Health economic models (HEMs) are crucial for assessing the cost-effectiveness of healthcare interventions, informing policy decisions and guiding reimbursement strategies. This study examines the feasibility of employing generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) for the conceptualisation of HEMs. Two proof-of-concept studies were conducted, implementing a first-of-its-kind agentic Gen-AI-augmented approach for model conceptualisation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An agentic Gen-AI framework was developed, incorporating the chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning algorithm through advanced prompt engineering, compounded with self-consistency, executed in an external Python programming environment. Within this framework, an agentic execution layer (the 'agent') autonomously orchestrated a multi-step retrieval-reasoning-generation task. Additionally, a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technique was implemented by linking the large language model (LLM) to an external database curated with user-selected data specific to HEM. Two case studies were explored: breast cancer, representing a data-rich disease area, and transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), exemplifying a data-sparse rare disease.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The agentic Gen-AI framework successfully generated two key outputs that were subsequently validated against published literature and expert review from health economic (HE) modelers and clinicians: (1) a disease concept diagram illustrating the progression of the disease and its associated health states, and (2) a model structure diagram depicting patient transitions between various health states.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The findings suggest that Gen-AI-augmented methodologies can enhance multiple aspects of HEM conceptualisation, including problem definition, disease and treatment effect pathway development, model structure recommendations, and drafting of model specification plans. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to integrate cutting-edge Gen-AI techniques such as human-in-the-loop (HITL), chain of thought-self-consistency (CoT-SC), and graph-based RAG for HEM conceptualisation or broader health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) applications.

articles.title: Opportunities for age-friendly emergency care: a mixed-methods study of older adult experiences in a Canadian Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to gain insight into the perceptions of care quality and ED experiences of older adults in a Canadian emergency department to develop targeted interventions to improve care experience and outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study utilized a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured phone interviews were conducted within 30 days of the index ED visit for 19 consenting participants. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data from interviews were coded using Nvivo software until thematic saturation was achieved.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Surveys were administered to 120 older adults (65 years and older). The majority of older adults surveyed use the ED 2-5 times per year and primarily resided in an urban setting. Survey results identified that older adults were hungry and thirsty during their stay (56.7%), relied on care partners for help during their ED visit (29.2%), and the majority felt heard at triage (93.3%). Interview results identified four major themes and 12 subthemes, highlighting many challenges and opportunities in the care of older adults in the ED. Major themes were communication, care, facilities, and attitudes. While older adults expressed appreciation and general acceptance of current ED conditions, they highlighted several areas needing improvement, including enhanced communication from physicians, better privacy measures, parking accessibility, and improved accommodations for caregivers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study highlights the unique challenges older adults face in the ED. While many expressed satisfaction and appreciation for their care, key areas for improvement emerged, especially in communication, privacy, and support services. Targeted interventions, such as geriatric friendly infrastructure and multidisciplinary teams, could improve care quality, patient satisfaction, and outcomes for older adults in the ED.

articles.title: Lessons learned while implementing a reusable orthopedic assistive devices recycling program in the pediatric emergency department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Lower extremity injuries are a common pediatric emergency presentation that require families to purchase crutches. These may not be affordable for many families, and crutches are often stored or discarded after treatment. There is a need for a solution to reduce the financial burden for families and medical waste. Using Quality Improvement methodology, our group implemented a reusable orthopedic assistive devices recycling program (ROAR) where crutches were dispensed for return and re-use in our pediatric emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Our aim was to dispense 120 pairs, or at least 50% of crutches used in our department at no cost. After collaborative planning, an operational workflow was designed, and the program was launched in April of 2024.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: To date, 57 pairs of crutches were dispensed to families at no cost. 25 pairs of these crutches were returned at the time of submission. This represents a 44% return rate within the ROAR program. The program was well received by patients and staff, but faced barriers in recuperation of crutches, ultimately limiting its ability to meet our aim and increasing the cost of the program.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Valuable progress was made including alleviating some financial strain on families in purchasing medical devices in our emergency department. In future iterations, adoption and staff buy-in should be maximized by emphasizing repeated education for staff, simple documentation and creative replacement of supplies including considering device donations.

articles.title: Return to sport after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in athletes with a preinjury Tegner Activity Scale ≥7: a longitudinal, nationwide, registry-based cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to longitudinally assess the rate and timing of return to sports (RTS) and its predictors after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACL-R) in preinjury Tegner Activity Scale≥7 (TAS≥7) athletes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective, longitudinal, registry-based cohort study included 511 athletes aged 16–40 with a preinjury TAS≥7 registered in the Swedish National Knee Ligament Registry following primary ACL-R. The primary outcomes were RTS TAS≥7 and associated predictors. Secondary outcomes included RTS at preinjury TAS levels, associated predictors, secondary ACL injury rates and assessment of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Associations were analysed using log-binomial and multivariable Cox regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 62% (n=315) achieved RTS TAS≥7 after ACL-R within 12.3 months (SD 4.7), while only 51% achieved RTS preinjury TAS level within 12.7 months (SD 4.9). Negative predictors for RTS TAS≥7 included female sex, older age, low sporting level and delayed surgery. ACL-Return to Sports after Injury (ACL-RSI) score >4.2 at 3 months postoperatively was associated with higher likelihood of RTS TAS≥7 and RTS preinjury TAS level. No differences in secondary ACL injury rates were observed between RTS groups or sexes, with overall secondary ACL injury rates of 9.2% (n=47) within 24 months. Participants returning to TAS≥7 reported better PROMs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Three out of five athletes returned to knee-demanding sports following ACL-R. Female sex, older age, lower sporting level and delayed surgery were associated with reduced RTS≥7 rates. Psychological readiness at 3 months post-surgery emerged as a potentially modifiable factor associated with RTS outcomes after ACL-R.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of an oxygen saturation-based prehospital cardiac risk assessment index (P-CRAI) for predicting 30-day mortality in acute myocardial infarction: a multicentre registry study from the Mie ACS Registry, Japan.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Early risk stratification of patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in the prehospital setting remains challenging. The aim of this study was to develop and internally validate a Prehospital Cardiac Risk Assessment Index (P-CRAI) based on peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) for predicting 30-day mortality in patients with AMI.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective analysis of a prospective multicentre registry.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: 17 cardiovascular centres participating in the Mie ACS Registry in Japan.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A total of 3584 consecutive patients with AMI who were transported directly by ambulance between 2013 and 2023 were included.

abstract.label: PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE
abstract.text: The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 30-day. Candidate predictors were age, sex, heart rate, systolic blood pressure and peripheral SpO₂ at first medical contact. P-CRAI was developed by adding SpO₂ and sex to the Prehospital-Simple Risk Index (pre-SRI). Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, overall prediction accuracy and decision curve analysis, with bootstrap internal validation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The P-CRAI was calculated as follows: (heart rate×[age/10]²)/systolic blood pressure+1.1(100−SpO₂)−1.5 (male sex). The model demonstrated good discrimination for predicting 30-day mortality (area under the curve (AUC) 0.830, 95% CI 0.817 to 0.842). Discrimination was significantly improved compared with the pre-SRI (AUC 0.805, p<0.001) and was comparable to that of the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events score (AUC 0.846, p=0.28). Calibration analysis showed an excellent agreement between the predicted and observed mortality rates, with a mean absolute error of 0.018. Harrell’s C-index was 0.821 and the Brier score was 0.050. Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit of P-CRAI than the pre-SRI across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significant graded separation of 30-day survival across increasing P-CRAI quartiles (log-rank p<0.001). P-CRAI remained independently associated with 30-day mortality after multivariable analysis (adjusted HR 6.37, 95% CI 4.35 to 9.32; p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: P-CRAI is a simple prehospital model using variables available at first medical contact that showed good discrimination for 30-day mortality in AMI and may support triage and early transfer of high-risk patients to specialised cardiovascular centres. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: A decade of asthma emergency department presentations in New South Wales: Temporal, seasonal and age-specific trends.

abstract.text: Asthma remains a major contributor to emergency department (ED) utilisation. Although international studies have described temporal, seasonal and age-specific patterns of asthma-related ED utilisation, contemporary Australian evidence remains limited. We conducted a retrospective, population-based ecological time-series study of monthly asthma-related ED presentations in New South Wales, Australia, between 2015 and 2024. A total of 231,670 presentations were recorded, averaging 1,931 per month (24.1/100,000 population). Children aged 0-15 years experienced the highest presentation rates. Rates showed marked seasonal variation, peaking in May and June (30.2 and 29.3/100,000 population respectively). These findings support targeted prevention and healthcare resource planning during peak season.

articles.title: Mechanical versus manual bag-valve ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in adults with cardiac arrest: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Optimal ventilation delivery during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) remains uncertain. Current resuscitation guidelines do not recommend mechanical ventilation (MV) over manual bag-valve ventilation (BV). We evaluated the association between MV use during CPR and clinical outcomes in adults with cardiac arrest compared with manual BV.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched 6 bibliographic databases from inception through May 31, 2026. Included studies compared MV and BV ventilation CPR in adult cardiac arrest patients. Patients receiving MV at any moment during CPR were classified as the MV group; those receiving only BV comprised the BV group. Primary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital admission, survival to hospital discharge, and good neurological outcome. Secondary outcomes included physiologic variables and pneumothorax. We calculated pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) using Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight studies involving 6847 patients were included. For the primary outcome, MV use during CPR was associated with a higher rate of ROSC than BV use (pooled RR, 1.20; 95% CrI, 1.04-1.42), with a 99% posterior probability of benefit. Posterior probabilities favoring MV for survival to admission, survival to discharge, and good neurological outcome were 92.3%, 93.6%, and 92.2%, respectively. Pneumothorax incidence was similar between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In adult cardiac arrest, MV use during CPR was associated with higher ROSC compared with manual BV. Evidence for improved survival and neurological outcomes remains imprecise and inconclusive.

articles.title: Application of healthcare failure mode and effect analysis in optimizing the emergency management process for acute myocardial infarction: An observational study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the effectiveness of Healthcare Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (HFMEA) in optimizing the emergency management workflow for Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) and to assess its impact on emergency efficiency, clinical outcomes, and patient satisfaction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: AMI patients treated at our hospital during different periods were enrolled and divided into two groups: a control group receiving conventional emergency procedures and a post-optimization group managed with an HFMEA-optimized emergency workflow. The HFMEA implementation involved forming a multidisciplinary team, constructing an integrated prehospital-to-in-hospital treatment process map, identifying high-risk failure modes based on the Risk Priority Number (RPN), developing targeted improvement measures, and establishing an information-based quality monitoring system. Outcome measures included key emergency time intervals, clinical outcomes, and healthcare quality indicators.

abstract.label: RESULTS
