abstract.text: Following HFMEA implementation, the post-optimization group showed significant reductions in all key emergency time metrics compared with the control group, including triage time, time to first electrocardiogram, Door-to-Catheterization (D-to-C) time, and Door-to-Balloon (D-to-B) time (all P < 0.001), and the effect sizes for all major time-related indicators between the two groups reached the large-effect level (Cohen's d ≥ 0.8, r ≥ 0.5). The total incidence of adverse events was significantly lower in the post-optimization group (P < 0.05), while rescue success rates did not differ significantly between groups (P > 0.05). Regarding healthcare quality, patients in the post-optimization group had shorter hospital stays and higher satisfaction scores as measured by a dedicated survey instrument (both P < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HFMEA effectively identifies high-risk steps within the AMI emergency workflow. Targeted process optimization can significantly enhance emergency efficiency, reduce adverse events, improve healthcare quality, and optimize patient experience.

articles.title: Progression of knee osteoarthritis among female occupational breath-hold divers (Haenyeo): A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative disease in older adults, particularly postmenopausal women. Aquatic activity is known to relieve symptoms and may protect joint health. Haenyeo, traditional female occupational breath-hold divers of Jeju Island, South Korea, perform lifelong breath-hold diving with intense aquatic labour, offering a unique model to study long-term aquatic exposure and knee OA outcomes.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of lifelong aquatic activity on OA progression and postoperative outcomes in Haenyeo compared with non-diving women.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 16 763 women aged ≥50 years with clinically confirmed primary knee OA treated at a tertiary hospital in South Korea between 2004 and 2023. Of these, 2390 were identified as Haenyeo from occupational history. Patients were followed until total knee arthroplasty (TKA), death, or August 2024. Outcomes included age at diagnosis, risk of TKA, 30-day readmission, complications and length of hospital stay. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for disease severity and comorbidities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Haenyeo were diagnosed later than non-Haenyeo (mean difference 2.8 years; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.4-3.2) and showed a reduced risk of TKA (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.77-0.95). Among 3989 TKA patients, Haenyeo had lower 30-day readmission (adjusted HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58-0.85), with no significant differences in complications or length of hospital stay.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Haenyeo exhibited delayed diagnosis, slower OA progression and favourable short-term postoperative outcomes. Sustained aquatic activity may provide protective effects on joint health and recovery in older women.

articles.title: Plastic Surgery Response to the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquake: Injury Patterns, Surgical Spectrum, and Departmental Organization.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The February 6, 2023, Kahramanmaraş earthquakes caused catastrophic damage in Turkey and Syria, resulting in mass casualties and disrupted health care. This study aims to describe the experience of a plastic and reconstructive surgery department during the acute disaster response period.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective study was conducted, including 145 patients hospitalized in the Department of Plastic, Reconstructive, and Aesthetic Surgery at a tertiary referral center between February 6 and February 21, 2023. Demographic characteristics, anatomic distribution of injuries, injury types, and surgical procedures were analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 88 females and 57 males with a mean age of 33.3±19.6 years. A total of 264 injuries were documented, mostly consisting of crush injuries in the extremities and associated fasciotomy defects. Surgical interventions included 77 debridements, 47 split-thickness skin grafts (STSG), 31 primary closures, and 20 maxillofacial reconstructions. 23 primary fasciotomies were performed, along with 15 fasciotomy extensions for inadequate prior decompressions. 14 microvascular free flap reconstructions and 7 locoregional flaps were carried out, with 1 free flap failure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In a mass-casualty earthquake setting, strict adherence to traditional stepwise reconstructive algorithms is often impractical. A flexible, elevator-based reconstructive approach allows surgeons to achieve definitive reconstruction earlier, shorten hospital stays, and use limited surgical capacity more efficiently under resource-constrained conditions. Inadequate fasciotomies performed at referring centers were frequently encountered, highlighting the need for systematic decompression protocols in disaster triage. Early integration of plastic and reconstructive surgeons into disaster response planning is strongly recommended.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV-retrospective case series.

articles.title: Western Trauma Association critical decisions in trauma: Traumatic hemothorax.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: ABSTRACT
abstract.text: Traumatic hemothorax is a common consequence of thoracic injury, with management strategies ranging from observation to tube thoracostomy and operative intervention. This Western Trauma Association algorithm provides a practical framework for the evaluation and management of patients with traumatic hemothorax. Recommendations were developed through review of the available literature, including randomized and observational studies, supplemented by expert consensus where high-quality evidence is limited. The proposed pathway incorporates patient physiology, hemothorax size, adequacy of pleural drainage, and evidence of ongoing hemorrhage to guide management decisions. Because clinical circumstances, institutional resources, and local practice patterns vary, the algorithm is intended to support rather than replace individualized clinical judgment. It may be used as a bedside reference and as a framework for the development of institution-specific protocols.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Consensus algorithm from the Western Trauma Association; Level V.

articles.title: Psychological care after pediatric trauma: When, who, and what next?
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

articles.title: Reductions in PTSD symptom clusters among perinatal and postnatal survivors of intimate partner violence participating in the Heartbeats program.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a leading cause of injury among women, especially during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Experiencing IPV increases the risk of mental health disorders, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). PTSD during the perinatal period is associated with poorer maternal mental health and adverse early child outcomes. Heartbeats (HB) is a hospital-based, community-linked violence intervention program designed to reduce morbidity and mortality among perinatal and postnatal survivors of IPV. HB provides crisis intervention, intensive case management, and counseling to pregnant patients up to 2 years postpartum who have experienced IPV. Given the high burden of mental health concerns in this population, a primary goal of HB is to reduce PTSD symptoms.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was conducted at a Level 1 trauma center. Participants were identified through IPV-related injury presentations, routine hospital screening, or referrals. Seventy-four participants completed the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) at intake (baseline) and 4 months postbaseline (follow-up). Total PTSD and subscale scores were calculated for intrusion (re-experiencing), avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and alterations in arousal and reactivity (hyperarousal). Paired-samples t tests assessed changes from baseline to follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant reductions were observed in total PTSD symptoms (M=9.16, SD=23.64, p =0.003) and across all subscales: intrusion (re-experiencing; M=2.76, SD=6.19, p <0.001), avoidance (M=1.18, SD=2.90, p <0.001), negative alterations in cognition and mood (M=3.82, SD=8.83, p <0.001), and alterations in arousal and reactivity (hyperarousal; M=2.33, SD=7.25, p =0.008).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: HB program participation was associated with significant reductions in overall PTSD severity and each DSM-5 symptom cluster. These findings support the potential of integrated hospital-based, community-linked programs to improve trauma recovery outcomes among perinatal survivors of IPV.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Knowledge, willingness, and self-efficacy in CPR: A two-phase study of prevalence and preliminary peer-led workshop in a Malaysian tertiary institution.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains a major public health concern, and early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) by bystanders is crucial for improving survival outcomes. University students represent an important target population for CPR education because they are socially active, highly accessible, and capable of disseminating lifesaving knowledge within the wider community. However, inadequate CPR knowledge, low willingness to perform CPR, and poor self-efficacy remain common among university students in Malaysia.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This two-phase study aims to determine the prevalence of self-reported CPR-related knowledge, willingness, and self-efficacy among students in a Malaysian tertiary institution (Phase 1) and to explore the preliminary changes in these outcomes following a peer-led CPR workshop (Phase 2).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In Phase 1, a cross-sectional survey was conducted at a tertiary institute in Selangor, Malaysia using a validated questionnaire on knowledge, attitudes, behavioral intention, and self-efficacy (KABSE) (N = 431). In Phase 2, a two-hour peer-led workshop, delivered by medical students, targeted students without CPR training in the past two years, and pre-post KABSE changes were measured (N = 33).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Phase 1 baseline findings revealed CPR knowledge and self-efficacy levels were relatively lower than attitudes and willingness to perform CPR. Females showed higher knowledge and attitudes, while males reported greater self-efficacy. Older and married participants demonstrated better attitudes, and those with a healthcare-related background had higher knowledge, attitudes, and self-efficacy, though similar behavioral intention. Higher scores were also linked to AED awareness, AED usage capability, and recent CPR training. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations among the KABSE domains. Following the peer-led workshop, the participants showed significant gains in self-reported knowledge (p < 0.001), attitude (p < 0.001), behavioral intention (p < 0.01), and self-efficacy (p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Although participants displayed positive attitudes toward CPR, baseline knowledge and self-efficacy were limited. The peer-led workshop demonstrated feasibility as a proof-of-concept intervention, generating significant short-term gains in self-reported knowledge and confidence.

articles.title: Application of bedside ultrasound guidance in difficult diagnostic lumbar puncture in infectious diseases: Technical specifications, clinical evidence, and practical prospects.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of international medical research

abstract.text: Diagnostic lumbar puncture is a core procedure in the diagnosis and management of infectious diseases. However, in patients with complex anatomical conditions, such as obesity and spinal deformities, the traditional blind puncture method is often challenging to perform, resulting in a substantially higher failure rates and increased complication risks. Bedside ultrasound guidance provides a precise, visual solution to these challenges and represents an emerging tool for improving clinical practice. This narrative review aimed to comprehensively examine the clinical value of ultrasound-guided lumbar puncture in infectious diseases, focusing on the current evidence base, core ultrasound technical principles, standardized pre-puncture assessment procedures, and clinical implementation strategies. Furthermore, it sought to empower infectious disease physicians to utilize safe, efficient, and scalable auxiliary techniques while outlining future directions. Compared with traditional landmark-based methods, ultrasound guidance significantly improves the first-attempt puncture success rate by approximately 20%-30%. Its key technical advantages include real-time visualization of the needle tip, identification of the optimal insertion point, and reduction of procedural complications.

articles.title: Morphological adaptations of cervical vertebrae in plunge-diving sulids.

abstract.text: Foraging strategy frequently drives morphological diversification in birds. The plunge-diving behavior of certain species makes the functional and ecological trade-offs of variation in cervical vertebrae an especially intriguing question. This study compares cervical vertebrae across five plunge-diving species and two non-plunge-diving species, using morphometric analysis of micro-CT scans to test whether diving birds share specialized cervical vertebrae morphologies distinct from non-divers. Plunge-divers repeatedly experience extreme impact forces during headfirst water entry, requiring the neck to function as a shock-absorbing spring rather than a flexible manipulative system. To withstand these forces, plunge-divers exhibit reinforced cervical vertebrae-short, wide vertebrae with expanded joints and thickened arches. These features help distribute compressive and bending loads and reduce stress on the spinal column during impact. Gannets and boobies, the most extreme plunge divers, have an additional articulating surface on the dorsal arch of their anterior cervical vertebrae which limits flexion in the beginning of the neck further reinforcing against high loads. Additionally, we see that all plunge-diving sulids experience similar water impact durations and that the ratio between the radius of the head and the neck scales with impact velocity.

articles.title: Anesthetic Challenges in Interarterial Right Coronary Artery Anomaly from the Left Sinus of Valsalva: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Coronary artery anomalies are rare but clinically significant malformations, particularly when involving an interarterial course, which predisposes to ischemia and sudden cardiac death. We report the case of a previously healthy 22-year-old man who suffered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest associated with recreational inhalant use. Imaging revealed an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left sinus of Valsalva with interarterial trajectory. Surgical reimplantation was performed under tailored anesthetic management emphasizing hemodynamic stability. The patient recovered uneventfully. This case discusses and highlights anesthetic priorities and the potential role of external triggers in vulnerable coronary anatomy.

articles.title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

articles.title: Three-Point Bedside Congestion Score (IJV Collapsibility + IVC Collapsibility + Central Venous Pressure) in Elective Mitral Valve Surgery: A Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Systemic venous congestion and right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction are key drivers of postoperative hemodynamic instability, prolonged ventilation, and acute kidney injury (AKI) after mitral valve surgery. Comprehensive echocardiography is informative but may be impractical in high-throughput pre-anesthesia workflows. We evaluated a pragmatic three-point bedside congestion score combining internal jugular vein (IJV) collapsibility, inferior vena cava (IVC) collapsibility, and invasively measured central venous pressure (CVP) for preoperative risk stratification.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, observational, single-center study, 100 consecutive adults (>18 years) undergoing elective mitral valve surgery for mitral stenosis were enrolled. A bedside ultrasound was performed in the preoperative area with patients in a 45° head-elevated position during quiet, spontaneous respiration. One point was assigned for each abnormal component (IJV collapsibility <18%, IVC collapsibility <25%, and CVP >12 mmHg), yielding a total score of 0 to 3. Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) was dichotomized at 17 mm. Outcomes included vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay, AKI, and in-hospital mortality. Discrimination for AKI and mortality was evaluated using a 5-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area under the curve (AUC) with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Calibration was assessed using recalibration intercept and slope, and decision curve analysis was used to explore clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The observed score distribution concentrated at 0 to 2 and 3; therefore, patients were analyzed as low score (0 to 2; n = 50) versus high score (3; n = 50). Compared with low-score patients, high-score patients had higher postoperative VIS (median 18.0 vs 10.0), longer ventilation (31.5 vs 22.0 hours), longer ICU stay (10.0 vs 5.5 days), and longer hospital stay (23.0 vs 12.5 days). AKI occurred in 40% versus 20%, and mortality in 10% versus 2% in high- versus low-score groups. In the combined 2 × 2 stratification, low score with normal TAPSE had no AKI or mortality, whereas high score with abnormal TAPSE had AKI in 55.6% and mortality in 14.8%. The combined score + TAPSE model showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.77 for AKI; AUC 0.782 for mortality) with near-ideal calibration in this dataset. Decision curve analysis suggested a higher net benefit for the combined model than single-predictor models across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05 to 0.30.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A simple three-point bedside congestion score stratifies postoperative risk after elective mitral valve surgery. Incorporating TAPSE into preoperative assessment provided a rapid and reliable means of excluding significant RV dysfunction, thereby reinforcing the validity of the threepoint scoring system. Multicenter external validation and evaluation of score-guided perioperative protocols are warranted.

articles.title: Emergency physicians' knowledge and practice in reporting medically unfit drivers in Atlantic Canada.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Emergency physicians frequently encounter patients with medical conditions affecting their fitness to drive. Emergency physicians have legal and ethical duties to report medically unfit drivers. However, many report low confidence in making these decisions. This may lead to underreporting. We aimed to assess knowledge, practice, and barriers regarding reporting of unfit drivers by Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of emergency physicians from four Atlantic Provinces. The survey contained 62 questions across four categories: 1) Demographics (seven), 2) General knowledge (five), 3) Scenarios/practice (34), 4) Barriers/needs (16). Where appropriate, participants rated answers on a five-point Likert scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-eight emergency physicians (response rate 20.6%) completed the survey: male (59.0%), age 35-44 (37.2%), formally trained in emergency medicine (74.7%). Overall, 88.5% lacked formal training to determine fitness to drive. Familiarity was low regarding provincial regulations (61.5% "slightly" or "somewhat" familiar) and the Canadian Medical Association Driver's guide (85.9% "not at all" to "somewhat" familiar) while most (80.8%) use clinical judgment to guide decisions. Half indicated they report (56.4%) and document (50.0%) unfit drivers only "sometimes" or less frequently. When presented with clinical scenarios where reporting is indicated (first seizure, recurrent seizure), most (100% and 96.2%) would advise the patients not to drive, but a third (33.4% and 37.2%) would either not report or leave it to another physician to do so. Lack of guideline knowledge was the most significant barrier to reporting, while pocket cards, an electronic app and electronic method to report were identified as enablers. Most emergency physicians (85.9%) would like formal education on this topic.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians expressed low familiarity with guidelines for determining medical fitness to drive and disclosed potential underreporting. Efforts should focus on targeted education and streamlined tools to improve reporting and enhance road safety.

articles.title: Healthcare pathways and outpatient management prior to community-acquired sepsis hospitalization in Germany, 2016-2019.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Sepsis often presents with non-specific symptoms that delay diagnosis and treatment. This study characterized pre-hospital outpatient and emergency care among patients with community-acquired sepsis (CAS) in Germany prior to hospitalization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This population-based observational cohort study used de-identified health claims data from over 340,000 AOK-insured adults admitted to hospital between 2016 and 2019 with an ICD-10-GM code for sepsis plus organ dysfunction, with each patient contributing only their first qualifying hospitalization (index case). Patients without ICD-10-GM codes for and suggestive of nosocomial infection were included and their healthcare utilization in the week before admission was categorized into: hospital emergency care (HEC), outpatient care only (OC), or no healthcare utilization (no HCU) (excluding patients exclusively hospitalized in the week prior sepsis hospitalization). Treatment and patient characteristics, sepsis features, and outcomes as documented in health claims data were compared across groups using descriptive and non-parametric statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 238,247 patients identified with CAS, 12.7% received HEC, 61.8% OC, and 25.5% had no HCU. HEC patients were younger, more severely ill, with higher ICU admission and mortality rates compared to the other groups. In the OC group, most patients (82.3%) had encounters with general practitioners, and 45.1% received OC on the day of admission. The last infection-related encounter occurred on average 2.0 days (SD 2.3) prior to sepsis hospitalization. Among OC patients, 48.7% underwent infection-related laboratory diagnostics, and 11.4% received anti-infective prescriptions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Most patients with CAS had healthcare contact in the week prior to hospitalization, predominantly in outpatient care. The frequent encounters shortly before admission and low rates of anti-infective prescription may suggest opportunities for earlier recognition and better risk stratification, e.g. by strengthening sepsis awareness and diagnostic strategies in outpatient settings.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: The study was pre-registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00031302) on 05/05/2023.

articles.title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Change in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments. Carotid Doppler spectrograms from a wireless, wearable critical care Doppler ultrasound system are analyzed for ccFTΔ during a PC (either infusion of 300 mL of crystalloid over 3 min or a Trendelenburg maneuver). The primary objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of PR patients by previously described ccFTΔ thresholds (i.e., both 4 and 7 ms ccFTΔ ), describe time-to-peak (TTP) ccFTΔ, and evaluate the ability of baseline ccFT to detect ccFTΔ during PC, using both the equations of Wodey and Bazett. Comparisons of related outcomes were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure, baseline ccFT discrimination was quantified using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and TTP was estimated using patient-level bootstrap resampling. Threshold-agnostic ccFTΔ trajectories were additionally explored using unsupervised k-means clustering of patient-level temporal responses for both correction equations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A PC was attempted in 4367 patients and an adequate ccFTΔ was collected from 4,128 patients (95%). In total, 982,937 Doppler cardiac cycles are included. The median ccFTΔ was 7.3 milliseconds (ms). 51.9% of patients had a ccFTΔ ≥ 7 ms, while 68.6% had a ccFTΔ ≥ 4 ms by the equation of Wodey. For Bazett, these fractions were 61.2% and 73.5%, respectively. For patients identified as PR based upon either a 4 ms or 7 ms ccFTΔ threshold, the time-to-peak ccFTΔ was 27.5 s for both equations. Baseline absolute ccFT did not discriminate PR from PUR patients under both correction formulae (AUROC 0.56-0.57).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: To our knowledge this is the largest reported dataset of ED patients with suspected sepsis receiving PR assessments by Doppler ultrasound, comprising nearly 1 million Doppler cardiac cycles obtained from over 4100 ED patients. Both 7 ms and 4 ms ccFTΔ thresholds described clinically-accepted rates of PR. The TTP was roughly 30 s into PC and baseline ccFT did not accurately detect ccFTΔ during PC. Finally, a hypothesis-generating analysis identified four distinct ccFTΔ trajectories during PC which may represent unique preload response patterns during PR testing.

articles.title: Clinical validation of the DRoPH score: a preoperative tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fractures.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Proximal humerus fractures are common injuries that are frequently associated with considerable technical challenges during surgical reduction and fixation. Although anatomical reduction is crucial for fracture healing and functional recovery, the anticipated difficulty of achieving satisfactory reduction is difficult to estimate preoperatively. The Difficulty of Reduction of Proximal Humerus Fractures (DRoPH) score was recently developed through a structured expert consensus process to estimate anticipated reduction difficulty based on predefined fracture- and patient-related characteristics. The aim of this study was to perform an initial clinical validation of the score.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent plate fixation of proximal humerus fractures at a tertiary trauma center between January 2014 and December 2024. DRoPH scores (0-10 points) were stratified into low (0-3), moderate (4-6), and high (7-10) difficulty categories. Validation was based on operative duration, postoperative reduction quality according to the criteria described by Schnetzke et al., and postoperative complications. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to assess the independent association of the DRoPH score with the primary outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, and surgical approach. Inter- and intra-rater reliability were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,012 patients treated for proximal humerus fractures, 392 met the inclusion criteria and had complete datasets available for analysis. Of these, 151 (38.5%) were classified as low, 186 (47.4%) as moderate, and 55 (14.0%) as high difficulty according to the DRoPH score. Operative duration increased significantly with increasing DRoPH scores, with an adjusted increase of 7.3 min per score point (95% CI 5.7-9.0; p < 0.001). Reduction quality deteriorated across difficulty categories, and higher DRoPH scores were independently associated with malreduction (OR 1.30 per point, 95% CI 1.12-1.50; p = 0.001). Overall complication rates increased from 15.2% in low-difficulty fractures to 34.5% in high-difficulty fractures, and the DRoPH score remained independently associated with complications in multivariable analysis (OR 1.15 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.28; p = 0.012). Inter- and intra-rater reliability of the overall DRoPH score were excellent (ICC 0.96 and 0.95, respectively).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study provides initial clinical validation of the DRoPH score as a reliable and clinically applicable tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fracture fixation. Higher DRoPH scores are independently associated with longer operative duration, increased risk of malreduction, and higher complication rates. The score may therefore serve as a useful adjunct for preoperative planning and risk stratification in surgically treated proximal humerus fractures. Further multicenter validation studies are warranted.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Severe MDMB-4en-PINACA toxicity following use of an electronic vaping device.
Comment on safety of acetylcysteine.
Technological translation tools for official language minorities in primary and emergency care: A rapid scoping review and environmental scan.
articles.journal_full: The European journal of general practice

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Language barriers cause miscommunication in healthcare, thereby threatening care quality and patient safety, including for official language minorities. Various technological solutions exist to minimise these barriers.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To map and summarise technological translation tools used in patient-provider communication in primary and/or emergency care.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A rapid scoping review using adapted Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology combined with an environmental scan. MEDLINE, Web of Science, and grey literature via ProQuest, ClinicalTrials.gov were searched. The environmental scan included a structured Google search, documents from the DOcKTEuR project steering committee and relevant Belgian organisations' websites. Sources describing technological translation tools used during clinical encounters with patients experiencing language barriers in primary or emergency care, published in English, French, or Dutch from 2019 onward were included. Qualitative content analysis was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidance.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty sources were included. Five categories were identified: video interpreter, telephone interpreter, translation application (AI), fixed-phrase healthcare translation application, and portable general translation device. Three domains of characteristics emerged: patient-provider interaction, operational feasibility, and ethical considerations. Video interpreter support provided high-quality interpretation and non-verbal communication however faced scheduling and technical challenges. Telephone interpreter support provided broad language coverage but lacked visual cues. AI-based applications enabled rapid multilingual support but raised concerns about accuracy. Fixed-phrase applications facilitated predefined healthcare communication, whereas portable devices offered flexible support but raised concerns about contextual appropriateness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Technological translation tools vary in interaction quality, feasibility and ethical considerations. Evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, highlighting the need for robust evaluation of effectiveness, safety, and implementation in routine practice.

articles.title: Deconstructing the Modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) Score: A Decision Tree Analysis Reveals the Pathophysiological Hierarchy of Organ Dysfunction Predictors in Prehospital Critical Care.
articles.journal_full: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early recognition of multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) in the prehospital setting remains challenging and is critical for reducing mortality among critically ill patients. The modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score was developed for prehospital use with point-of-care testing; however, the internal decision architecture of this score remains unexplored.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A prospective, multicentre, observational study was conducted across three emergency medical systems (EMS) in Spain, included adults (n = 12,212) with acute illness transferred to emergency departments with high priority. A decision tree (DT) model was developed using the five components of the mSOFA score, lactate, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), oxygen saturation-to-fraction of inspired oxygen ratio (SaFi), mean blood pressure (MBP), and creatinine, to predict in-hospital mortality at 2 days. The study followed the STROBE and TRIPOD+AI guidelines.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Cohort mortality was 5.0% (n = 609). Lactate emerged as the primary decision variable, with a threshold of 3.8 mmol/L, followed by SaFi, GCS, and creatinine in patients with hyperlactataemia, and by GCS and creatinine when lactate was below the threshold.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The DT deconstructs the mSOFA from a static score into a dynamic, interpretable clinical decision framework. By revealing the pathophysiological hierarchy underlying the score, with lactate as the central stratification axis, this approach enables EMS clinicians to identify distinct clinical phenotypes and anticipate deterioration based on the sequential evaluation of organ dysfunction rather than a single numerical threshold.

articles.title: A Two-Year Recovery Report From the Emergency Medicine Association of Türkiye (EMAT) Perspective: The 6 February Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: On 6 February 2023, sequential Mw 7.7 and 7.6 earthquakes devastated 11 provinces in Türkiye. Two years on, the Emergency Medicine Association of Türkiye (EMAT) assessed recovery from an emergency department (ED) perspective.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of emergency physicians and residents in the most affected provinces (Kahramanmaraş, Adıyaman, Malatya).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Respondents were predominantly male (81.1%) and residents (70.3%). Family routines had partly stabilized (48.6%), yet ongoing household mental-health problems were common (54.1%). Housing remained strained: most homes were slightly damaged (59.5%); 13.5% of physicians continued to live in temporary shelters. Concerns persisted about hospital structural safety (59.4%). Equipment issues centered on delayed maintenance/repair (64.9%). ED operations suffered from crowding (70.3%), workload related to staffing gaps (67.6%), and inadequate physical space (56.8%). Academic activity was disrupted (51.4%), with perceived declines in educational standards versus non-affected provinces (40.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Two years post-earthquake, substantial deficits persist across infrastructure, workforce, equipment maintenance, psychosocial well-being, and training. EMAT recommends coordinated actions on structural safety, supply chains, psychosocial support, durable housing, academic workforce recovery, governance/coordination, targeted financial incentives, and continuous monitoring to restore resilient, high-quality emergency care in the region.

articles.title: Temporal Associations Between Nonpharmaceutical Interventions and COVID-19 Transmission in Delaware.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Understanding how nonpharmaceutical interventions temporally align with changes in COVID-19 transmission remains important for public health monitoring and evaluation. However, substate-level evidence remains limited. Delaware provides a useful setting for such analyses due to its small population and largely uniform statewide policy implementation during 2020.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed COVID-19 transmission dynamics in Delaware and its 3 counties (Kent, New Castle, and Sussex) between March 2020 and March 2023, with policy-focused analyses restricted to major statewide interventions implemented in 2020. Incident infections were reconstructed using a deconvolution-based approach, and the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) was estimated using the EpiEstim R package.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Rt estimates varied across policy periods and revealed substantial spatial heterogeneity. The most consistent increases in Rt were associated with the transition to hybrid school reopening, while decreases in Rt were associated with limits on social gatherings, the public mask mandate, and the stay-at-home advisory and overnight curfew. During Phase 1 reopening, Rt changes were small statewide, while Sussex County exhibited a larger increase than other counties.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: COVID-19 transmission dynamics in Delaware during 2020 varied across policy periods and counties, illustrating substate heterogeneity under uniform statewide interventions and the use of Rt-based estimates for monitoring epidemic dynamics.

articles.title: Beyond Bedside Care: Reframing Disaster Nursing Education as a Health System Resilience Strategy.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: The increasing frequency and complexity of disasters are placing unprecedented demands on health systems and the nursing workforce. Despite nurses playing a central role in disaster preparedness and response, disaster-related competencies remain inconsistently integrated into nursing education. This gap should be viewed not merely as an educational issue, but as a matter of health system resilience. Future disaster-ready nurses require competencies extending beyond clinical care, including leadership, systems thinking, ethical decision-making, and interprofessional collaboration. Competency-based education, simulation training, and emerging digital technologies may help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world practice. Reframing disaster nursing education as a health system resilience strategy may strengthen preparedness and ensure that nurses are equipped not only to respond to crises, but also to lead through them.

articles.title: Disaster Report: Military Helicopter Crash in a Deployed Environment - Providers' and Patient's Perspectives.

abstract.text: The crash of a military helicopter during a 2023 United States Army deployment produced a mass-casualty incident (MASCAL) in an austere setting. One of the casualties was an Emergency Medicine (EM) physician who oversaw point-of-injury (POI) triage and early casualty evacuation with a Special Operations Forces (SOF) medic to the nearest Role II Military Treatment Facility (MTF), followed by movement of the six most severely injured patients to Role III, and subsequent transfer to Landstuhl Regional Medical Center (LRMC) via Critical Care Air Transport Team (CCATT). This disaster report explores the EM physician's actions as the initial provider, another EM physician as a receiving provider for a multi-leg fixed-wing transport, and a practicing trauma surgeon's unique perspective as one of the significantly injured patients. The viewpoints in this report highlight operational decisions including dispersion of medical assets, dynamic triage, destination/platform selection, and significant stressors of flight. Disaster care pathways should anticipate aeromedical stressors, emphasize patient positioning and communication, and align evacuation decisions with changing resources and injury patterns. These lessons are directly relevant to prehospital/disaster systems operating in contested, austere, or resource-limited environments.

articles.title: Health Care Use Among Recently Enrolled Young Adults in an Integrated Health Plan.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Early establishment of a primary care practitioner (PCP) may enhance young adults' ability to navigate the health care system, particularly those new to integrated care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study population included 18- to 26-year-old individuals newly enrolled in 2023 at Kaiser Permanente Northern California (N = 30,099). This cross-sectional study examined associations between early establishment of a PCP (indicated in the electronic health record) and several outcomes: creation of secure messaging accounts, secure messaging use, appointment and advice call center use, e-visit use, emergency department (ED) utilization, and screening for mental health, alcohol, exercise, and tobacco use. Adjusted incidence rate ratios were estimated using a modified Poisson model controlling for sex, age, race and ethnicity, need for an interpreter, insurance type, neighborhood deprivation, and chronic health problem.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Young members with early establishment of a PCP were more likely to utilize modalities of care that were outside of traditional office visits and had higher rates of preventive screening. They also demonstrated a 10% reduction in the likelihood of a low-acuity ED visit compared to those without early PCP connection.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Improved navigation of health care resources and uptake of preventive screening with reduced reliance on ED visits were seen among some groups with early establishment of a PCP.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Promoting PCP visits and targeted PCP outreach to those living in lower socioeconomic neighborhoods may foster beneficial health care relationships during this transitional life stage.

articles.title: Diagnostic Variability in the Modified Kocher Criteria for Septic Arthritis of the Hip: Implications for Aspiration Decision-Making.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study evaluates the clinical application of the modified Kocher criteria (MKC) in assessing septic arthritis of the hip (SAH) at a tertiary children's hospital.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on subjects presenting to the emergency department and receiving a hip ultrasound over a 1-year period. Those without a hip effusion were excluded. Patient demographics, symptoms, imaging, labs, treatment, and final diagnoses were collected. SAH was defined clinically by the treating team, supported by patient presentation, lab/imaging findings, operative intervention, and antibiotic therapy. Descriptive and bivariate statistics based on variable distribution were used during analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 326 subjects were identified, and 110 had effusion present on ultrasound. Eighteen (16.4%) underwent aspiration. Aspirated subjects had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores (P=0.001) and higher median values for all individual MKC components, including CRP, WBC, ESR, maximum temperature, and a higher prevalence of non-weight-bearing (P<0.05). SAH was diagnosed in 38.9% of the aspirated group (n=7), with MKC scores of 2 (n=2), 3 (n=3), and 5 (n=2). Aspiration rates increased across MKC scores 0 to 3, and synovial fluid inflammatory markers trended higher with increasing MKC scores. Thirteen subjects with an MKC score of 2 were not aspirated; final diagnoses included transient synovitis (n=9), hip effusion, osteomyelitis, sickle cell crisis, or limp (each n=1). Three subjects with an MKC score of 3 were not aspirated and later diagnosed with metastatic tumor, osteomyelitis, and rheumatic fever.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pediatric patients undergoing hip aspiration with a concern for SAH had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores and higher levels of all individual MKC components than their nonaspirated counterparts. However, nearly 15% of patients had MKC scores of 2 or 3 that were not aspirated in the ED, and SAH was identified even in lower-score subjects. While MKC scores appear to influence clinical decision-making, diagnostic variability remains. In patients with intermediate MKC scores of 2 to 3, the criteria should prompt further evaluation, taking into consideration the overall clinical context to guide aspiration decision-making.

articles.title: Similar Presentations, Divergent Clinical Courses: Pediatric Headache Care in the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pediatric emergency department (ED) headache presentations may follow heterogeneous clinical courses.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare presentation characteristics, migraine order-set activation, pain-score change, treatment intensity, and health care utilization between pediatric ED headache encounters with and without a clinician-documented persistent/intractable headache.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multisite retrospective cross-sectional study of children aged 3 to 18 years presenting to 2 pediatric EDs with headache or migraine as a chief complaint from 2019 to 2023. Encounters were classified by clinician documentation of an intractable/refractory headache diagnosis or persistent symptoms despite initial treatment. The primary outcome was change from arrival to posttreatment/disposition pain score. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to each patient's first encounter and to clinician-documented migraine or status migrainosus.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 529 encounters, 18.5% had a documented persistent/intractable headache course. Most presentation characteristics were similar, although symptom duration and pulmonary comorbidity differed. Order-set activation did not differ significantly (76.5% vs. 68.2%; P = 0.106). Encounters with a persistent/intractable headache had less pain improvement [median: -4 (interquartile range: -6.75 to -1) vs. -5 (interquartile range: -7 to -3); P = 0.002], received more medications, radiologic imaging (39.8% vs. 26%; P = 0.006), neurology consultation (56.1% vs. 39.4%; P = 0.003), hospitalization (19.4% vs. 3.2%; P < 0.001), and 30-day return ED visits (10.2% vs. 4.6%; P = 0.049). The pain-score difference was attenuated in the first-encounter analysis (P = 0.060), but persisted in the clinician-documented migraine subgroup (P = 0.006).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Headache presentation characteristics and order-set activation did not distinguish the ED course, but pain improvement, treatment intensity, and utilization differed during ED care. Prospective studies should evaluate standardized early reassessment measures.

articles.title: Invasive Bacterial Infections Other Than Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae in Febrile Infants Younger Than 90 Days: A Multicenter Emergency Department Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Invasive bacterial infections (IBIs) in febrile infants ≤90 days are mostly caused by Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae. However, data on IBIs caused by other pathogens remain limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of febrile infants aged ≤90 days diagnosed with IBI between 2008 and 2022 at 12 Spanish pediatric emergency departments. Epidemiology, clinical features, microbiology and outcomes of cases caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae were analyzed. Adverse outcomes included death, inotropic or respiratory support, acute complications, or sequelae.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 375 infants with IBI, 106 (28.3%) had infections caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae. The most frequent pathogens were Staphylococcus aureus (n = 30, 8.0%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (n = 15, 4.0%) and Enterococcus faecalis (n = 14, 3.7%). Most cases presented as isolated bacteremia (65.1%), followed by bacteremic urinary tract infection (18.9%) and meningitis (12.3%); 46.2% of infants with meningitis had a concomitant urinary tract infection. The distribution of pathogens varied according to age, with S. aureus being more frequent among younger infants and S. pneumoniae accounting for 8.6% of IBIs in infants aged 61-90 days. Listeria monocytogenes caused 1.3% of IBIs, with only 1 case identified in the last decade. Adverse outcomes occurred in 7.5% of infants with infections caused by other pathogens and 8.6% of those with E. coli/S. agalactiae (absolute risk difference, -1.0% [95% confidence interval, -7.1 to 5.0]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: IBIs caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae accounted for a substantial proportion of cases and showed an age-dependent distribution. Most presented as isolated bacteremia, while meningitis was associated with a higher observed frequency of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Peripheral perfusion index for differentiating cardiac and pulmonary dyspnea in the emergency department: A prospective observational study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Dyspnea is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits, often caused by cardiac or pulmonary conditions with overlapping clinical presentations. Rapid differentiation between these etiologies is crucial for timely management and prognosis. The peripheral perfusion index (PPI), derived from pulse oximetry, has emerged as a non-invasive biomarker of tissue perfusion. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PPI in distinguishing cardiac from pulmonary causes of dyspnea and to assess its prognostic value for clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational study in the adult ED of Ankara Etlik City Hospital between March 1 and March 31, 2025. Adult patients presenting with dyspnea were consecutively enrolled, with predefined exclusion criteria applied. Demographic data, vital signs, laboratory parameters, and PPI values were collected within 30 min of presentation. Final diagnoses were established using clinical, laboratory, imaging findings, and specialist consultation. The primary outcome was the diagnostic accuracy of PPI in differentiating cardiac and pulmonary dyspnea. Secondary outcomes included ED disposition and 30-day mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 320 patients were included (median age: 73 years; 56.9% female). Pulmonary diseases accounted for 55.9% (n = 179), and cardiac diseases for 44.1% (n = 141). Median PPI was significantly lower in the cardiac group compared with the pulmonary group (1.8 [IQR 1.2-2.2] vs. 2.8 [IQR 2.0-4.3]; p < 0.001). PPI values were also lower in patients admitted to the ICU (1.5) and in 30-day non-survivors (1.5) compared with discharged patients (4.1; p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance for pulmonary disease prediction (AUC: 0.801; 95% CI: 0.749-0.844), with an optimal cutoff of >2.2 (sensitivity 71%, specificity 74%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PPI is a simple, non-invasive, and rapidly obtainable parameter that may aid in differentiating cardiac from pulmonary causes of dyspnea in the ED. Lower PPI values were observed in patients with cardiac-origin dyspnea and were associated with ICU admission and 30-day mortality; however, the prognostic findings should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for residual confounding.

articles.title: Acute hemorrhagic shock from vaginal laceration during intercourse requiring operative management.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: Vaginal laceration during consensual intercourse is a rare cause of acute vaginal bleeding. Most coital injuries are minor, although may result in acute hemorrhage and hemodynamic instability. A 30-year-old G3P2012 otherwise healthy woman presented to the emergency department (ED) with acute vaginal bleeding immediately during consensual intercourse. She was initially well-appearing then developed hemorrhagic shock in the ED from ongoing vaginal exsanguination. The bleeding source could not be visualized on speculum examination. She was resuscitated with tranexamic acid, crystalloid, and two units of unmatched whole blood and taken emergently to the operating room. Examination under anesthesia after evacuation identified a horizontal posterior vaginal wall laceration. The laceration was repaired transvaginally with hemostasis, and the patient recovered uneventfully. A vaginal laceration during intercourse may cause acute life-threatening hemorrhage. Bleeding is often occult on speculum examinations although may progress rapidly to shock. Emergency clinicians should exclude pregnancy, initiate early resuscitation, and urgently consult gynecology for examination under anesthesia and repair when indicated.

articles.title: Palliative Care Screening Without Consultation: An Implementation Gap in Geriatric Emergency Department Palliative Care Screening.

abstract.label: CONTEXT
abstract.text: The Palliative Care and Rapid Emergency Screening (P-CaRES) tool identifies emergency department (ED) patients with unmet palliative care needs. Whether a documented positive screen changes consultation when no referral pathway is attached has not been reported.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To describe inpatient specialty palliative care consultation after P-CaRES screening in a geriatric ED where results generated no alert, order set, or referral.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study of patients 65+ screened with P-CaRES from 2019 to 2024, comparing P-CaRES-positive and -negative patients; the primary outcome was inpatient specialty palliative care consultation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 421 patients, 115 (27.3%) screened positive; they were older with longer hospitalizations. Consultation rates were nearly identical between positive and negative patients (13.9% vs. 13.7%, p = 1.00).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: P-CaRES identified older adults with serious illness but showed no meaningful difference in consultation (95% confidence interval [CI] excluded differences >8 points), indicating that a passively documented positive screen was not associated with specialty consultation.

articles.title: Thoracoscopic Management of Recurrent Pneumothorax in an Adult Patient with Cri du Chat Syndrome and Severe Scoliosis: A Case Report.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Cri du chat syndrome (CdCS) is a rare genetic disorder that can be associated with scoliosis and marked thoracic deformity. Although scoliosis has been reported to be associated with an increased incidence of pneumothorax, reports of pneumothorax surgery in patients with severe scoliosis associated with CdCS are extremely rare. Herein, we report a case of recurrent pneumothorax in an adult patient with CdCS associated with severe scoliosis who was successfully treated by thoracoscopic surgery.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 41-year-old man with CdCS presented with severe scoliosis, intellectual disability, and dental abnormalities. He was transported to our emergency department with severe left pneumothorax associated with complete left lung collapse and marked hypoxemia. CT after chest drainage revealed a bulla located in the deep thoracic cavity near the mediastinum. Because severe thoracic deformity raised concerns regarding both airway management and thoracoscopic manipulation, the patient was initially managed conservatively. However, severe left pneumothorax repeatedly recurred, and surgical intervention was ultimately indicated. Thoracoscopic surgery was performed under 1-lung ventilation using a bronchial blocker. Intrathoracic manipulation was technically challenging because of the marked thoracic deformity associated with severe scoliosis; however, safe operative exposure was achieved using same-axis thoracoscopic manipulation with the thoracoscope and instruments through the same port. A broad-based causative bulla located near the S6-S10 boundary adjacent to the descending thoracic aorta was ligated using ENDOLOOP, followed by intrathoracic administration of 20 mL of 50% glucose solution. The postoperative course was uneventful with no recurrence during 7 years of follow-up.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In patients with severe scoliosis associated with CdCS, thoracic deformity may complicate both airway management and thoracoscopic manipulation. However, thoracoscopic surgery may be feasible with appropriate anesthetic planning and adaptation of the operative strategy. In particular, same-axis thoracoscopic manipulation using the thoracoscope and instruments through the same port may be useful for maintaining safe visualization and instrument handling within a narrow thoracic cavity.

articles.title: Age and intensive care unit admissions following opioid overdose.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Older adults are increasingly impacted by the opioid crisis, yet age-related differences in overdose presentation, management, and outcomes leading to intensive care unit (ICU) admission remain poorly characterized. This study examined age-related variations in drug exposures, interventions provided, and hospital utilization among patients experiencing an opioid overdose.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Fentalog Study was conducted at 10 US medical centers and collected data on patients who presented to emergency departments with confirmed non-fatal opioid overdose, and available waste serum samples between 9/21/2020-4/14/2026 were included. Chart reviews captured presentations, treatments, and hospital utilization. Toxicologic analyses were performed at the Center for Forensic Science Research and Education. Nested multivariable logistic regressions assessed whether age improved predicted ICU admission, after accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and drug classes detected.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1930 patients, 15.3% were admitted to the ICU, 7.8% received cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and 5.8% were intubated. Length of hospital stay varied by age, with patients 65 + years old staying longest (median: 22.0h, IQR: 87.0, p < 0.001). Illicit opioids were less commonly detected in older adults (p < 0.001), while prescription opioids were more common (p < 0.001). Age cohort did not significantly predict ICU admission, although prescription benzodiazepine (AOR: 1.4, 95% CI: 1.1, 1.9) and opioid (AOR: 0.7, 95% CI: 0.5, 0.9) detection did.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Older age was associated with longer hospital stays but did not predict ICU admission after adjustment for relevant covariates. Benzodiazepine and opioid exposures showed a modest association with ICU utilization. Further work should clarify how pharmacologic combinations influence clinical severity across age groups.

articles.title: Prehospital fluid resuscitation in patients with severe burns - A nationwide cohort study.
articles.journal_full: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prehospital fluid administration is widely used in patients with severe burns to stabilize hemodynamics and organ perfusion, but its effect on outcomes remains unclear. We examined the association between prehospital fluid administration and early mortality in patients with severe burns.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this retrospective observational study using Japan's nationwide trauma registry, we identified patients with severe burns - defined as burns involving ≥ 20% of the total body surface area (TBSA) in patients 5 years of age or older, or ≥ 10% in younger children - who were transported directly from the scene of injury between January 2019 and December 2023. The primary outcome was death from any cause within 48 h after hospital arrival; the secondary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. Missing covariate values were handled by multiple imputation, and confounding was addressed with stabilized inverse probability weighting based on propensity scores. Effect estimates were expressed as odds ratios with cluster-robust 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 884 patients analyzed, 94 (10.6%) received prehospital fluid administration. Early death occurred in 22 of 94 patients (23.4%) in the fluid group and in 106 of 790 patients (13.4%) in the non-fluid group; in-hospital mortality occurred in 42 (44.7%) and 224 (28.4%), respectively. After adjustment, the odds ratios for 48-hour and in-hospital deaths related to prehospital fluid administration were 0.88 (95% confidence interval, 0.32-2.39) and 1.30 (95% confidence interval, 0.75-2.25), respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients with severe burns, prehospital fluid administration was not significantly associated with early or in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: Training and Use of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) in Pediatrics and Neonatology in Latin America: A Multinational Survey Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study characterizes the current state of training, clinical use, and implementation barriers of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in Latin America. POCUS has become a fundamental diagnostic tool. However, limited information exists regarding its implementation in this region.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multinational cross-sectional survey study was conducted using an electronic survey administered to health care professionals caring for pediatric and neonatal populations across 21 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean (December 2025 to January 2026). We assessed the prevalence of formal training, frequency of clinical use, implementation barriers, and interest in further training. Analyses were performed using epidemiologically appropriate denominators.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 662 professionals were included, predominantly pediatric intensivists (45.2%) working in high-complexity settings (73.3%). Formal POCUS training was reported by 68.7%. Overall, 80.4% currently use POCUS; among them, 14.5% reported no formal training. Self-perceived unsupervised competence among trained participants was moderate. The most frequent clinical applications were pleural effusion and cardiac tamponade. The main barriers identified were lack of training (77.5%), limited access to equipment (50.5%), and absence of institutional protocols (48.9%). Interest in formal training was very high (92.9%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Substantial gaps remain in structured education, equipment access, and institutional protocol development. The significant proportion of untrained users and moderate self-perceived competence highlight an urgent need for standardized training programs. The high level of interest in training represents an opportunity to develop coordinated regional strategies to promote safe and effective POCUS implementation in Latin America.

articles.title: Remediating kelp habitat destruction to restore ecosystem services by curbing urchin proliferation in southeastern Australia.

abstract.text: Shallow, rocky reef habitats are key components of temperate marine ecosystems, providing shelter, feeding and breeding habitat for a wide variety of organisms. In these ecosystems, urchins occur alongside other benthic species, such as abalone, competing for food and space. As active grazers, urchins are habitat engineers, whereas gastropods like abalone are habitat responders. Increasing abundance of the long-spined urchin (Centrostephanus rodgersii), in eastern Victoria, on Australia's Great Southern Reef, under the influence of the warm East Australian Current, has led to overgrazing of macroalgae, deforesting kelp canopies to form urchin barrens with greatly reduced biodiversity. This in turn has weakened the resilience of abalone populations and limited productivity from commercial stocks. A collaborative government-industry reef restoration strategy was implemented in response through an urchin removal trial at Gunshot Reef in eastern Victoria. Divers removed urchins from vegetated areas, clearing them up to 100 m from the kelp/barren junction in all directions, resulting in greatly reduced urchin density. Video-transect surveys before and after urchin removal assessed the effectiveness of reducing urchin density and promoting subsequent habitat recovery. Spatiotemporal patterns in divers' effort were evaluated by geospatial analysis of vessel-diver GPS tracking. Findings indicated positive signs of site-scale habitat recovery progression over ∼2.5 years post-treatment, with increased macro, turfing, and coralline algae. The cost of urchin removal, in 2019-2020, was AUD$9385 Ha-1 suggesting further work to evaluate the cost-benefit trade-offs among alternative remediation approaches including maintenance harvesting and broader potential for targeted urchin control, although regional applicability requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Status of post-crash response systems and policy indicators in the WHO African region: a cross-sectional descriptive study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The WHO African region has the highest estimated road traffic fatality rate globally. Effective post-crash response and care are essential to mitigate the severity and fatality of injuries from road traffic crashes. Post-crash response can be conceptualised as a continuum of emergency care functions spanning the scene of injury, prehospital and facility-based care. This study describes the reported fatality-to-crash ratio and the status of post-crash response system and policy indicators in the WHO African region using the most recent data available. It identifies the gaps to inform the strengthening of post-crash response systems in the region.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive analysis using data from the Global Status Report on Road Safety 2018 and 2023 databases. Indicators were selected to reflect key components of the post-crash continuum, including prehospital services, facility-based emergency care and system-level enabling factors. We analysed the reported fatality-to-crash ratio and the availability of selected policy and system indicators related to post-crash response and care. Comparisons between 2018 and 2023 were conducted for a subset of comparable indicators. The analysis is descriptive and does not assess policy implementation or effectiveness.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Across the 40 countries reporting complete data, 238 851 crashes resulted in 340 170 injuries and 50 993 deaths, corresponding to a reported regional fatality-to-crash ratio of 21% with substantial variability observed across countries, including values exceeding 100%, which may reflect differences in reporting systems, under-reporting of non-fatal crashes and the occurrence of crashes involving multiple fatalities. Indicators showed limited reported availability of prehospital services, uneven access to emergency care facilities and shortages of trained personnel. Free psychological support and rehabilitation services were rarely available. Between 2018 and 2023, most comparable indicators showed declines in reported availability. However, interpretation of these findings is limited by substantial missing data for several indicators and potential inconsistencies in reporting across countries.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings suggest important gaps in post-crash response systems across the WHO African Region, particularly in prehospital care, emergency service capacity and rehabilitation. Strengthening emergency care systems and improving the quality and integration of injury data systems are important priorities for strengthening post-crash response in the region. Further research is needed to assess policy implementation and barriers to effective post-crash care.

articles.title: Automated Calculation of the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) Intra-Abdominal Injury Rule from Unstructured Emergency Department Notes Using a Large Language Model.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) intra-abdominal injury clinical prediction rule identifies children at very low risk for clinically significant intra-abdominal injury after blunt abdominal trauma. However, retrospective evaluation of the rule's use in practice requires resource-intensive chart review. We investigated whether large language models (LLMs) can automatically calculate PECARN intra-abdominal injury risk scores from real-world unstructured emergency department (ED) notes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective secondary analysis of children after blunt abdominal trauma presenting to 2 urban pediatric EDs. The LLM, OpenAI o1, was compared with clinician-derived standards for PECARN risk scores and predictor variable extraction from unstructured physician ED notes. Performance was assessed using standard diagnostic test characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 196 children with complete ED notes, the LLM calculated binary PECARN risk scores with 95.4% accuracy (95% confidence interval [CI] 92.5 to 98.3), 94.4% sensitivity (95% CI 90.6 to 98.2), 98.2% specificity (95% CI 94.6 to 100), and an F1 score of 0.97 (95% CI 0.90 to 0.98). Agreement by weighted Cohen's kappa between multicategorical LLM-derived risk scores and clinician-derived risk scores was high, 0.96 (95% CI 0.92 to 1.00). Predictor variable extraction demonstrated strong performance across all PECARN variables, with accuracy greater than 94%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The LLM had comparable performance to clinicians in calculating binary and multicategorical PECARN intra-abdominal injury risk scores and extracting predictor variables from unstructured ED notes. LLMs may enable automated calculation of clinical prediction rules from clinical documentation.

articles.title: Correlation of blood biomarkers with microstructural brain injury in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.text: In-hospital mortality among resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains high. Identifying patients who will benefit from intensive care while avoiding prolonged, potentially unnecessary treatments is essential. Blood-based biomarkers provide a novel method for evaluating brain injury. The ability of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and total-tau (t-tau) to measure white and grey matter injury is unestablished in comatose OHCA survivors treated with targeted temperature management (TTM) or xenon combined with TTM. We examined correlations between the biomarkers and white and grey matter injury assessed with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). This was a randomized, single-blind, phase 2 clinical drug trial involving two multipurpose intensive care units in Finland. It was conducted between August 2009 and March 2015. One hundred and ten comatose OHCA patients aged 24 to 76 years were randomly assigned to either inhaled xenon treatment combined with 24-h TTM (33°C) (n = 55, xenon group) or TTM alone (n = 55, control group). MRI data were available from 96 patients, with a median imaging time of 53 h (interquartile range, 47-64 h) after OHCA. Biomarker data were obtained from 105 patients. In the control group of 48 patients, after adjusting for age, sex and site, a disruption of white matter microintegrity as measured by decreased fractional anisotropy (FA) of DTI, the primary endpoint of the trial, showed a significant negative correlation with NfL at 24, 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.28 to -0.37; P < 0.05), NSE at 48 and 72 h (ρ = -0.30 to -0.35; P < 0.05) and t-tau only at 72 h (ρ = -0.30; P < 0.05). In the xenon group (n = 48), these correlations were absent at all timepoints. The NfL-FA partial correlations showed progressive divergence between the xenon and control groups, with a statistically significant between-group difference observed at 72 h (ρ = -0.37 versus ρ = 0.14; P = 0.016). Cortical or basal ganglia grey matter mean diffusivity did not have a consistent correlation with biomarker levels at different time points. No statistically significant differences were found between the xenon and control groups in the adjusted geometric mean levels of GFAP, NfL, NSE or t-tau at various time points following OHCA. In conclusion, NfL correlated with FA in controls but not in the xenon group. This between-group difference reached significance at 72 h, suggesting that xenon may modify the relationship between axonal injury and white matter microstructure after OHCA.

articles.title: An Innovative Decoupled Spatio-Vertical-Temporal Learning Model Based on Topography Guidance for Wind Vector Forecasting.

abstract.text: Accurate wind speed forecasting (WSF) is pivotal for the secure grid integration of wind farms and the optimization of power dispatching. However, the stochastic nature of atmospheric dynamics and their complex interactions with local terrain pose significant challenges. Traditional spatiotemporal models inherently suffer from severe homogenization, irreversibly destroying fine-grained aerodynamic textures and leading to cumulative directional errors over extended horizons. To dismantle these limitations, this study proposes a novel Topography-Guided Spatio-Vertical-Temporal Transformer (TG-SVTFormer) for the multi-step forecasting of zonal and meridional wind vectors. Specifically, a dual-stage topography-guided mechanism explicitly injects static geographical variables (elevation, slope, and roughness) into both the spatial encoding and microscopic decoding phases, imposing key physical constraints on aerodynamic friction. Furthermore, the architecture employs a structured decoupled learning paradigm: a re-engineered Mix-Transformer spatial encoder deliberately eliminates deep-stage downsampling in favor of dilated convolutions-drastically expanding the global receptive field while preserving the intrinsic meteorological textures. Subsequently, the temporal evolution hub explicitly decouples the vertical dimension, utilizing upper-air atmospheric states to guide the target surface layer via simulated vertical momentum transport. The experiments showed the accuracy of TG-SVTFormer in predicting the wind speed with mean absolute error of 0.71 m/s in 3 h, 0.85 m/s in 6 h, and 1.06 m/s in 12 h. Compared to five existing baseline WSF models, the proposed TG-SVTFormer model demonstrates superior performance in wind speed forecasting and, more importantly, offers a transferable and physics-informed framework that can be adapted to other terrain-complex regions and extended to related renewable-energy and air-quality forecasting tasks.

articles.title: Patient Posture-Adaptive Non-Contact Respiratory Rate Measurement Inside a Moving Ambulance Using RGB and Thermal Cameras.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Monitoring and evaluating respiratory rate (RR) plays a critical role during emergency transport. Conventional RR measurement methods have primarily relied on electrocardiogram-based approaches, which are susceptible to large errors caused by patient body movement and impose a burden on patients due to their contact-based nature.
