This study aimed to develop a non-contact RR measurement method using RGB and thermal cameras that can be applied inside a moving ambulance. Methods: One of the key challenges in non-contact RR measurement inside an ambulance is accommodating changes in patient posture. We addressed this by patient posture-adaptive automatic image registration between RGB and thermal cameras and developing a nostril detection method robust to posture changes. Results: The image registration error of the proposed method was evaluated at various distances from the camera, and the error was confirmed to remain within 1 pixel. RR measurement experiments simulating various respiratory conditions were then conducted inside a moving ambulance. The average of mean absolute error (MAE) was 0.95, 0.59, and 2.80 breaths per minute (breaths/min) for bradypnea, normal, and tachypnea, respectively, in the supine position, and 1.08, 1.90, and 4.38 breaths/min, respectively, in the semi-sitting position. Evaluation of the proposed nostril detection method further confirmed improved RR estimation accuracy compared with the conventional method. Conclusions: This study achieved patient posture-adaptive automatic image registration and robust nostril detection and successfully conducted experiments under realistic and challenging conditions, representing a substantial step toward the real-world implementation of a non-contact RR measurement system in ambulances.

articles.title: Emergency medicine updates: Contrast media hypersensitivity.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Contrast media hypersensitivity reaction is a rare but clinically significant condition that can meaningfully affect emergency department (ED) patient care. Therefore, it is important for emergency medicine clinicians to be aware of the current evidence regarding the diagnosis, prevention, and management of this condition.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This paper evaluates key evidence-based updates concerning contrast media hypersensitivity reactions for the emergency clinician.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Adverse reactions to contrast media are divided into common physiologic reactions and less common hypersensitivity reactions. Hypersensitivity reactions can be immediate or delayed, ranging from mild urticaria to anaphylaxis. The greatest risk factor for hypersensitivity reaction to contrast media is a prior hypersensitivity reaction to contrast media. It is crucial to discern and document the specific culprit agent, severity, type, and timing of previous and current reactions. Physiologic reactions can be treated with supportive care and usually self-resolve. Acute evaluation and treatment of moderate-to-severe hypersensitivity reactions mirrors standard anaphylaxis care, with intramuscular epinephrine as the first-line drug for severe reactions, and allergist referral should be considered. Patients with a prior physiologic reaction do not require premedication or contrast switching. For prevention of breakthrough hypersensitivity reactions, switching to a chemically different contrast agent is more effective than corticosteroid premedication. Routine corticosteroid premedication is no longer recommended, as literature has not demonstrated corticosteroid pretreatment reduces hypersensitivity reactions. Second-generation antihistamines may be of benefit for patients with a history of mild-moderate reactions. Severe or anaphylactic reactions warrant strong consideration of alternative imaging. Collaboration with key stakeholders, including radiology and pharmacy, is important to improve workflows, protocols, and patient care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: An understanding of literature updates can improve the ED care of patients with contrast media hypersensitivity reactions.

articles.title: Association of neighborhood social vulnerability with reoperation after operative treatment of proximal humerus fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Neighborhood-level indices may capture different dimensions of social risk. We evaluated whether the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) was associated with reoperation after operative treatment of acute proximal humerus fractures (PHFs), using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) as a secondary comparator.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort included 438 distinct fracture episodes treated within a single United States practice group from January 2021 through December 2024. The outcome was ipsilateral shoulder reoperation for a postoperative complication. Primary logistic regression models adjusted for age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, and diabetes mellitus; ADI analyses included 414 fractures.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-one fractures (11.6%) underwent reoperation. Reoperation increased from 6.4% to 16.1% across SVI quartiles (ordered trend P = 0.028; omnibus P = 0.163). Each 0.10 increase in SVI was associated with reoperation in the primary model (odds ratio [OR], 1.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.26; P = 0.033) and after adjustment for procedure category (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.01-1.26; P = 0.027). ADI national and state ranks were not associated with reoperation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Higher SVI was associated with reoperation, whereas ADI national and state ranks were not. These index-specific, hypothesis-generating findings require external validation.

articles.title: Creation of a formal chest wall injury program improves compliance with rib fixation indications.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) improves outcomes but remains underutilized. This study evaluated the impact of the creation of a dedicated, institutional chest wall injury program on SSRF utilization, hypothesizing such a program would increase utilization of SSRF for those patients meeting criteria.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study of adults with radiographically confirmed rib fractures presenting to a Level I trauma center between January 2016 and April 2023. Patients were classified by the Chest Wall Injury Society SSRF operative criteria and whether or not they underwent SSRF. Basic demographics were obtained. The chest wall injury program was developed in 2020 with elements including standardized guideline adoption, daily multidisciplinary rounds to identify candidates early, and establishment of a dedicated outpatient follow-up clinic. Additionally, the program facilitated consistent documentation of SSRF candidacy and improved interdisciplinary communication regarding treatment plans. The primary outcome was the relationship between operative and non-operative cases when SSRF criteria were met.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 3488 patients were included, of whom 1629 met operative indications for SSRF. Overall, 457 patients (28.1%) underwent fixation. Compared to non-operative patients, the SSRF group had similar age and predominantly sustained blunt trauma. Implementation of the dedicated chest wall injury program in 2020 was associated with a significant increase in SSRF utilization among eligible patients, rising from 21.5% to 32.1% in 2020 (rise of 10.6%). Utilization continued to increase each subsequent year, reaching 45.3% by 2023. Among patients meeting SSRF criteria, SSRF utilization increased from 19.8% before 2021-41.1% from 2021 onward (p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age and gender, the 2021-onward period remained independently associated with receipt of SSRF (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 2.25-3.52; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Establishing a dedicated chest wall injury program was associated with higher adherence to SSRF guidelines and increased operative management of eligible patients.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV, therapeutic/care management.

articles.title: Alcohol-Related Emergency Department Visits of Young Adults in a University City in the Netherlands.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to examine the incidence and characteristics of alcohol-related emergency department (ED) visits in young adults compared with older age groups.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective electronic health record study of patients aged ≥18 years with an alcohol-related ED visit, including acute alcohol intoxication (AAI) and alcohol-related injuries, was conducted at Reinier de Graaf Gasthuis (RdGG) from January 1, 2022 to January 1, 2024. Young adults (18 to 24 years) were compared with older age groups (25 to 39, 40 to 54, 55 to 69, >70 years) regarding visit type, blood alcohol concentration (BAC), diagnostic tests, and hospital admission. Within young adults, student status and peak visit times were analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 49,226 ED visits, 888 (1.8%) were alcohol-related, including 192 (21.6%) young adults, of whom 40% were students. Men were more frequently admitted with alcohol-related injuries (36.4% vs 25.4%), women for AAI (67.8% vs 47.3%, P < .001). Alcohol-related visits were highest among young adults (4.3% vs. 0.7-2.8%, P < .001). AAI was significantly more prevalent in the 18 to 24 group than in older groups. Most injuries in young adults involved head or neck trauma (84%). Students had higher mean BACs than nonstudents (2.34 vs 1.84 g/L, P = .019).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Young adults account for the highest incidence of alcohol-related ED visits. Students exhibit higher BACs than nonstudents. These findings underscore the critical need to reduce alcohol-related harm and promote safe drinking habits among young adults especially during specific periods.

articles.title: Minimally Invasive Revision Surgery Combining Endoscopic Double-Row Reinsertion and Flexor Hallucis Longus Transfer for Insertional Achilles Tendon Re-Rupture in a Semi-Professional Rugby Player: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Acute insertional Achilles tendon rupture (A-IATR) is a rare, often season-ending injury in athletes. Revision after a failed repair is particularly challenging, and return to sport (RTS) after such surgery is rarely documented. We report one such case. Methods: A 32-year-old semi-professional rugby prop forward sustained an insertional re-rupture eighteen months after open transosseous reinsertion without suture anchors. MRI showed complete detachment with 15 mm of retraction and no residual tendon on the footprint. A single-stage procedure combining endoscopic double-row (SpeedBridge™) reinsertion and flexor hallucis longus (FHL) transfer was performed, followed by six weeks of non-weight-bearing cast immobilization and criteria-based rehabilitation, with Ankle-GO™-guided return to play. Results: At three months, MRI showed tendon continuity without re-rupture. Return to play was authorized at 8.2 months (Ankle-GO™ 16/25); the patient returned to official competition at 9.4 months and was still competing approximately 17 months after surgery. At 15 months, the Achilles Tendon Total Rupture Score was 84 and the AOFAS score 90. No complication occurred. Conclusions: To our knowledge, this is the first report of RTS after this combined endoscopic revision technique. This single case suggests that this approach may be a feasible revision option in high-demand athletes; comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: From Trauma to Tumour: Incidental Giant Left Adrenal Myelolipoma in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.

abstract.text: Adrenal myelolipomas are rare, benign tumours composed of mature adipose and haematopoietic tissue. Patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) are predisposed to their development, with chronic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) hypersecretion secondary to impaired cortisol synthesis thought to be the principal driver of myelolipoma formation in this population. A 49-year-old female with known CAH presented to the emergency department following a stab wound to the abdomen. Computed tomography (CT) incidentally identified a 12 cm encapsulated left adrenal lesion consistent with a giant myelolipoma. Despite reported adherence to hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement therapy, persistently elevated adrenal steroid precursors and plasma renin levels suggested suboptimal glucocorticoid control. Following multidisciplinary team (MDT) review, the patient was offered a left adrenalectomy given the lesion size (>10 cm) and concerns regarding the risk of spontaneous haemorrhage. This case underscores the importance of systematic imaging review beyond the primary indication for scanning, and the value of optimising biochemical monitoring and considering adrenal imaging in selected high-risk CAH patients.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in German general practice: a qualitative study of opportunities and barriers.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: International studies show that point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly being used in primary care settings and can improve diagnostic decision-making. Particularly in the field of general practice, which is characterised by a lower prevalence of severe diseases, the use of POCUS may facilitate patient history-taking and diagnosis in a more targeted and efficient manner. This study aims to investigate how German general practitioners (GPs) perceive the clinical benefits, barriers, and implementation of conventional ultrasound use to date, as well as the benefit, barriers, and implementation requirements of POCUS in primary care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Between March and June 2023, two focus groups (FGs) were held at each of two locations (in Bavaria and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania) as part of general practice quality circles. Using a convenience sample, each of the four FGs included between five and eight GPs. Semi-structured FGs were transcribed and anonymised. Using Mayring's inductive content analysis method, two researchers analysed the FGs. The aim was to develop and identify new hypotheses and unexpected themes shedding light on both perspectives regarding the practical benefit and structural challenges of conventional ultrasound, as well as the potential of and barriers to the use of POCUS in general practice.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From the participants' perspective, ultrasound has proven to be extremely relevant in everyday general practice. However, existing reimbursement frameworks and training requirements were perceived as significant barriers. The participants considered the implementation of POCUS in primary care as an opportunity to lower these barriers, improve diagnostic processes, and strengthen GPs' skills.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our findings make it clear that the use of ultrasound currently depends largely on the individual commitment of GPs - in terms of the time involved and the financial resources required. However, it is also clear that POCUS could offer the potential to improve the conditions for the use of ultrasound in GP practices. In this way, the introduction of POCUS may improve diagnostic workflows and their accessibility in primary care.

articles.title: Resuscitation training with school children - Analysis of factors affecting chest compression quality.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) improves survival after sudden cardiac arrest, but bystander CPR rates remain low. International guidelines therefore recommend CPR training during childhood. This study evaluated CPR performance in children aged 8-13 years and assessed determinants of chest compression quality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this observational cross-sectional study (2019-2022), 784 schoolchildren aged 8-13 years completed a standardized 90-min CPR training session. Anthropometric data and CPR quality parameters were recorded using Resusci Anne QCPR Torso manikins (Laerdal Medical AS, Starvanger, Norway) and SimPad Plus SkillReporter systems (Laerdal Medical AS, Starvanger, Norway). Associations were analyzed using multivariate statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 784 children (mean age 11 ± 1 years) were included. Two minutes of chest compressions were completed by 93% of children. Mean compression depth was 40.0 ± 9.9 mm and correlated with weight (r = 0.663), height (r = 0.623), and age (r = 0,544; all p < .001). In multivariable analysis, these factors explained 50% of variance (R2 = 0.50, p < .001). Mean compression rate (115 ± 8/min) was higher in younger children and became more consistent with increasing age (ß = -0.119, p = .02). Correct hand positioning was achieved almost universally (median 100%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: A tailored and focused CPR training is feasible and effective in children aged 8-13 years but higher body weight improves compression depth, older age improves compression, while correct hand position is largely independent of these variables.

articles.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Prognosis and Emergency Treatment of Patients with Ischemic Stroke in Suzhou, China: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted stroke care globally. This study aimed to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical characteristics, acute treatment, and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in Suzhou, China.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study retrospectively analyzed 506 hospitalized AIS patients from four stroke centers between December 10, 2022, and January 20, 2023. Patients were grouped by COVID- 19 infection status and timing. Clinical data and outcomes were compared with a pre-pandemic cohort from the SUMMITS-II Study.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among included AIS patients, 54.3% were COVID-19-positive. Infected patients had higher baseline NIHSS scores, elevated inflammatory markers, and more in-hospital complications. Intravenous thrombolysis rates increased slightly during the pandemic, despite longer prehospital delays. Emotional disorders were more frequent post-stroke. COVID-19 infection, particularly concurrent with stroke onset, was linked to worse outcomes at 90 days and 1 year.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The findings suggest that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly influenced the clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke in Suzhou. Patients with AIS with concomitant COVID-19 infection presented with a higher prevalence of vascular risk factors and elevated inflammatory and coagulation markers. Moreover, COVID-19 infection occurring within one week of stroke onset was associated with more severe neurological deficits and poorer short- and long-term prognosis, highlighting the potential role of COVID-19 in worsening stroke outcomes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic adversely affected stroke severity and prognosis. While in-hospital workflows were preserved, delayed presentation and increased systemic burden contributed to unfavorable stroke outcomes. Strengthening stroke care delivery and psychological support during public health crises is essential.

articles.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Point-of-Care Ultrasound Utilization Among Emergency Medicine Residents and Emergency Nurse Practitioners Following Institutional Training.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) serves as a critical diagnostic tool in emergency medicine; however, a persistent gap remains between competency acquired during training and consistent clinical application. This study sought to identify barriers and facilitators influencing POCUS examination frequency among emergency medicine (EM) residents and emergency nurse practitioners after institutional training, and to examine the association between individual-level factors and the frequency of POCUS examinations.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study was conducted in the Department of Emergency Medicine at Srinagarind Hospital, Khon Kaen University, Thailand, from January 2024 to December 2025. Cohort 1 included 76 providers (16 EM residents and 60 nurse practitioners) who completed institutional POCUS training between January 2024 and December 2025. Data collected included provider characteristics, competency scores, workload, and responses to a 5-point Likert-scale survey assessing perceived barriers and facilitators. Cohort 2 consisted of 2,097 documented, archived POCUS examinations performed by these providers during a standardized 1-month post-training observation period per provider. Associations were evaluated using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: EM residents demonstrated significantly higher competency scores than nurse practitioners (86.3±5.7 vs 78.9±7.4, p=0.002). The most prevalent barriers identified were high workload and time constraints, limited equipment availability, and reduced interpretive confidence. Nurse practitioners expressed greater concern regarding insufficient institutional support (3.88±0.72 vs 3.06±0.89, p=0.001) and medicolegal risk (3.65±0.79 vs 2.94±0.93, p=0.004), whereas residents rated structured feedback more favorably (p=0.012). Multivariable regression identified competency score (adjusted β = 3.97 per 10-point increase, p < 0.001) and provider type (adjusted β = 9.64, p = 0.007) as independently associated with higher documented POCUS examination frequency, while patient volume per shift was negatively associated (adjusted β = -1.89 per 5-patient increase, p = 0.010).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings indicate that formal training alone may be insufficient to achieve equitable competency or utilization. Additional multi-center studies are required to validate these results. The competency score showed a more consistent association with POCUS examination frequency than other variables examined, suggesting it may represent an important, though not exclusive, factor influencing real-world use. As examination quality, interpretive accuracy, and clinical impact were not assessed in this study, higher frequency should not be interpreted as better implementation.

articles.title: Constipation status and the enhanced recovery pathway in bladder reconstruction.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Preoperative constipation may contribute to postoperative recovery and has been associated with increased postoperative complications in adults, but its impact in pediatric urology patients remains unclear. Enhanced recovery pathways (ERPs) have been shown to improve recovery through standardized perioperative protocols, although they are not well-studied in pediatric populations. We assessed whether surgical outcomes differ between patients with and without constipation undergoing bladder reconstruction under an ERP, hypothesizing that constipation would increase length of stay and delay return of bowel function.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a post hoc analysis of prospectively enrolled patients aged 4-25 years undergoing bladder reconstruction from 2019 to 2024 at our single institution as part of a multi-institutional ERP study. Patients with constipation, defined as Bristol type ≤2 or stools less frequent than every other day, were included at our institution but excluded from the multi-institutional study. Study outcomes were length of stay, time to return of bowel function, and 90-day adverse outcomes (composite of Clavien grade ≥2 complications, emergency department visits, readmissions, and reoperations). All patients followed the same ERP regardless of constipation status. Propensity score weighting was applied to balance baseline covariates. Weighted Poisson and logistic regression models then fit associations between constipation and study outcomes and included unbalanced covariates for doubly robust estimation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included a total of 59 patients (median age 11 years [IQR 9-13]), 22 (37%) with constipation. Patients with constipation were more likely to be female (86% v 60%, p = 0.03) and have no prior abdominal surgery (68% v 38%, p = 0.02) when compared to patients without constipation. In final weighted and adjusted outcome models, constipation was not significantly associated with length of stay or time to return of bowel function. In contrast, constipation was significantly associated with higher odds of 90-day adverse outcomes (OR 5.13, 95% CI 1.64-16.1). However, the significant association with 90-day adverse outcomes was driven by unplanned reoperations and emergency department visits, which were predominantly related to channel/catheter troubleshooting rather than constipation-related reasons.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings suggest that constipation was not associated with length of stay or return of bowel function following bladder reconstruction within an ERP, though in a stratified analysis of patients with spina bifida, constipation was associated with longer length of stay, a finding that warrants further investigation. These findings provide a foundation for future prospective studies to validate and expand upon these observations in larger, multi-institutional cohorts.

articles.title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.text: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.

articles.title: The association between advanced practice nurse visiting services and acute healthcare utilization in long-term care residents: A retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Residents in long-term care settings have complex medical and functional needs, and the early period following facility admission represents a vulnerable transitional phase. Registered nurses are often not available on-site in institutional long-term care settings, in Korea and globally, limiting the capacity to respond to acute challenges. In 2014, Korea expanded home-visit advanced practice nurse visiting services to cover long-term care residents, enabling advanced practice nurses to deliver skilled nursing interventions within institutional long-term care settings.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study evaluates the impact of advanced practice nurse visiting services on acute healthcare utilization among long-term care residents with nursing care needs.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study using Korean nationwide claims data.

abstract.label: SETTING(S)
abstract.text: Institutional long-term care settings.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: 32,018 long-term care residents with nursing needs were included, and 1507 were selected through 1:3 propensity score and exact matching.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A 1:3 matched cohort was constructed using propensity score matching and exact matching on functional status and clinical severity. Outcomes were emergency department visits, acute hospital admissions, and long-term care hospital admissions within 6 months of Institutional long-term care admission. Left-truncated Cox models estimated hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1507 matched participants, those who received advanced practice nurse visiting service had significantly lower risks of admission to acute hospitals (hazard ratio 0.62) and long-term care hospitals (hazard ratio 0.52), with no difference in emergency department visits. In subgroup analyses, advanced practice nurse visiting service use was associated with a lower risk of acute hospital admission among residents with long-term care eligibility grades 1 and 2, indicating high functional dependence, with grade 1 reflecting greater dependence than grade 2 (grade 1: hazard ratio 0.56; grade 2: hazard ratio 0.53). A lower risk was also observed among residents with Charlson Comorbidity Index scores of 0-2 (hazard ratio 0.58) and 3-4 (hazard ratio 0.62). For long-term care hospital admission, a significantly lower risk was observed among residents with Charlson Comorbidity Index scores of 3-4 and above (hazard ratio 0.47).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Advanced practice nurse visiting services were associated with lower risks of acute hospitalization, particularly among residents with high care needs. Furthermore, a lower risk of admission to a long-term care hospital was observed among residents. This suggests the services may help prevent avoidable hospitalizations and enhance continuity of care for high-risk residents in long-term care settings.

articles.title: Delayed diagnosis of a traumatic gluteal pseudoaneurysm with arteriovenous fistula and dual arterial supply mimicking a buttock abscess after a stab wound: a case report.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs), with or without associated pseudoaneurysms, are uncommon complications of penetrating vascular injuries that may cause substantial morbidity and potentially fatal complications. Evidence is largely derived from case reports and case series, with important contributions from military experience. Delayed gluteal lesions may mimic a hematoma or abscess, creating a diagnostic pitfall.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 51-year-old male presented with a one-month history of a progressively enlarging painful left buttock mass following a stab wound that had been primarily sutured at a local hospital. Initial ultrasound suggested a hematoma, and the patient was admitted with a working diagnosis of "left buttock mass." Physical examination revealed a 7 × 7 cm fluctuant mass with tenderness but without overt signs of infection. Contrast-enhanced pelvic CT demonstrated a 6.8 × 3.2 cm intensely enhancing lesion within the left gluteus maximus with prominent feeding vessels, suggestive of an arteriovenous fistula or vascular malformation. Digital subtraction angiography confirmed a left gluteal pseudoaneurysm with an associated arteriovenous fistula supplied by branches of both the inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries, with early venous opacification. The patient underwent successful transcatheter embolization using fibered platinum coils and a cyanoacrylate-lipiodol mixture, with complete occlusion of the fistula confirmed on completion angiography. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 2. At three-month follow-up, the patient reported no specific discomfort, and color Doppler ultrasonography showed a marked reduction in mass size with no detectable flow within the lesion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Penetrating buttock trauma may cause a gluteal pseudoaneurysm with an associated AVF supplied by more than one internal iliac artery branch. Contrast-enhanced CT and selective angiography are important for recognizing the vascular lesion and delineating all feeding arteries. In this patient, embolization of both the inferior gluteal and internal pudendal arterial feeders achieved complete angiographic occlusion and a favorable clinical outcome, with a markedly smaller mass and no detectable intralesional flow on color Doppler ultrasonography at three months.

articles.title: Emergency Medical Technician Program Certification Pass Rates by Size and Geographic Region: A Five-Year Descriptive Analysis.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Emergency medical technician (EMT) educational programs demonstrate student certification performance variability. Prior evaluations identified program size and regional disparities, yet whether these patterns persist is unclear. This study described national variation in EMT certification pass rates by cohort size, geographic region and cohort year.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a repeated cross-sectional descriptive analysis of United States civilian EMT annual program cohorts from 2018 to 2022 using National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians Cognitive Examination data. We included cohorts with >5 candidates testing annually. Cohorts were grouped by fixed cohort size quartiles (Q) and National Association of State EMS Officials (NASEMSO) region. Outcomes were first- and cumulative third-attempt pass rates. Descriptive statistics summarized cohort characteristics and outcomes, and pairwise comparisons assessed group differences.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 10,923 EMT educational program cohorts identified, 8567 (78.4%) were included. Median first- and cumulative-third attempt pass rates were 63.9% (interquartile rate [IQR]: 50.0, 77.7) and 77.8% (66.7, 88.3), respectively. Pass rates varied by cohort year, cohort size, and region. Median pass rates were highest in 2022. Q4 (≥46 candidates) had higher median first-attempt and third-attempt rates compared with Q1 (6-10) (first: 68.2%, 60.0%; third attempt: 81.6%, 71.4%). West NASEMSO region cohorts had higher median pass rates than all other regions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: From 2018 to 2022, EMT program success varied across cohort size, geographic region, and cohort year. Larger cohorts had higher median pass rates, and NASEMSO West cohorts had the highest median pass rates. These findings support continued EMT program evaluation and highlight the need for more education data to understand mechanisms for differences.

articles.title: Association Between Weather Variables and Viral Gastroenteritis in the United States.

abstract.text: Infectious gastroenteritis (IGE) is a major cause of pediatric morbidity globally, with viral pathogens accounting for a substantial proportion of cases. While seasonal patterns of viral IGE are well recognized, the association between specific environmental exposures, such as ambient temperature, and viral IGE has not been fully quantified. First, we performed a secondary analysis of data from a prospective, multisite study of children presenting to emergency departments at 5 medical centers across the continental United States, linking individual-level laboratory data to environmental exposures, including temperature, humidity, and air pollutants, measured during the 14 days preceding symptom onset. Mixed-effects logistic regression was applied to evaluate the association between viral IGE and environmental exposures, adjusting for site-level clustering and patient age. Among 868 children with IGE, higher ambient temperature was inversely associated with viral etiology (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, .36-.68; P < .001). We did not find statistically significant associations between other environmental variables and viral IGE. Then, to contextualize these individual-level findings in children, we examined all-ages population-level surveillance data from GermWatch, a regional laboratory testing-based infectious disease surveillance system, which demonstrated concordant declines in viral pathogen detection with increasing temperature. These findings support the association of ambient temperature with viral transmission patterns. Incorporating environmental context into clinical decision-making may improve diagnostic stewardship and support more effective resource allocation during periods of increased viral IGE prevalence.

articles.title: Handheld Ultrasound: Technical Review and International Expert Consensus Recommendations.

abstract.text: Background: Handheld ultrasound (HHUS) is increasingly used in point-of-care imaging because of its portability, accessibility, versatility, and comparatively low cost. Methods: This structured narrative technical review evaluated current HHUS technology, image quality and functionality, clinical applications, regulatory considerations, and future perspectives using recent literature, comparative studies, technical sources, and previous EFSUMB/WFUMB position papers. A structured SWOT analysis informed draft recommendations, which underwent three rounds of scientific discussion and revision by a 17-member international multidisciplinary expert panel. Each of the seven final recommendations was subsequently voted on separately, with consensus predefined as ≥80% agreement. Results: While HHUS devices are increasingly suitable for routine clinical use, further standardization, clinician training, and regulatory alignment are essential for widespread adoption. Conclusions: HHUS can expand access to focused ultrasound imaging, particularly in point-of-care and resource-limited settings. Its appropriate use requires task-specific device selection, adequate training, quality assurance, and recognition of its limitations compared with comprehensive ultrasound systems.

articles.title: Timing of First Systemic Antibiotic Administration and Risk of Deep Infection in Adults with Open Long-Bone Fractures: A Systematic Review and Threshold-Specific Evidence Synthesis.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Early systemic antibiotics are central to open-fracture care, but a 60 min operational target does not establish a biological infection threshold. We examined how time origin, cutoff, and outcome definition affect interpretation of reported associations. Methods: Evidence was reconstructed from two preserved bibliographic inventories containing 24 entries. Complete database-search exports were unavailable, and selection, extraction, ROBINS-E, and GRADE were not independently duplicated. The protocol was archived retrospectively on OSF (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/7J8QN). Estimates were described separately by time origin, cutoff, adjustment, outcome, and follow-up for a target population aged at least 18 years. No pooled estimate was retained. Results: The historical evidence map contained 16 reports, including contextual reports that did not establish applicability to the target population. This is not a verified final included-study count. Within the preserved inventory, no threshold-by-time-origin group supplied two compatible adjusted estimates. A 191-patient cohort reported an adjusted odds ratio of 1.02 (95% CI 0.39-2.68) at 60 min after emergency-department arrival. Recorded appraisals indicated predominantly high or very high risk of bias and very low certainty; these judgements were not independently verified. Conclusions: Distinguishing care-process targets from causal thresholds improves interpretation of the available reports. However, incomplete searching and single-investigator assessment limit the reliability and completeness of this synthesis. The observational associations establish neither causal thresholds nor the safety of delay and do not justify postponing indicated prophylaxis.

articles.title: Paramedics' Perceptions and Experiences Providing End-of-Life Care: A Cross-Sectional Survey.

abstract.text: Background: Many people spend their last year of life at home, with most wishing to die there. Evidence suggests paramedics facilitate over half of Emergency Department visits for palliative care patients, many of which are avoidable. Objective: To explore the perceptions and experiences of providing end-of-life care amongst paramedics in one region of the United Kingdom. Design: Online descriptive cross-sectional survey design using the ParAid Questionnaire. Quantitative data analysed using descriptive statistics. Setting and Participants: 182 paramedic respondents completed the questionnaire online (34% response rate). Results: Respondents reported numerous barriers to delivering end-of-life care. Access to medicines was problematic, with 54% reporting that they 'always' or 'often' had no access to specific medicines needed for symptom control. Education gaps were also evident: 67% reported that lack of pre-registration end-of-life care education and 71% that lack of post-registration education 'always' or 'often' influenced their ability to meet patients' needs. Only 28% felt 'very' or 'extremely' competent in supporting patients and families in the last year of life, while 47% reported experiencing a 'fear of doing the wrong thing' 'always' or 'often'. Access to information and referral pathways also presented challenges: 88% reported that they 'always' or 'often' lacked access to existing Advance Care Planning documentation, while 62% reported that they 'rarely' or 'never' had access to a specialist palliative care team out-of-hours. Conclusions: Findings emphasise the need for improved palliative care education, support structures, and improved access to information and medicines for paramedics. Findings identify potential areas for service development, including training, communication, and referral pathways, which may better support paramedics in providing end-of-life care.

articles.title: Accuracy of Caregiver Dosing of Acetaminophen and Ibuprofen for Febrile Children Presenting to a Saudi Arabian Tertiary Hospital Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Background: Fever and its related symptoms are common reasons for pediatric emergency department (ED) visits. Parents are often concerned about fever in children, and a frequent reason for ED visits is the persistence of fever despite the administration of antipyretics at home. It is hypothesized that caregivers often administer incorrect doses of acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Objective: To assess caregivers' dosing practices in children with fever by evaluating the accuracy of acetaminophen and ibuprofen dosing and to identify factors associated with inaccurate dosing in Saudi Arabia. Methodology: A cross-sectional survey was conducted over a six-month period from 1 January 2022 to 30 June 2022 in the emergency department. We included caregivers of children under 14 who received a quantifiable dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Multivariable regression analysis was utilized to identify factors associated with inaccurate dosing. Results: A total of 330 caregivers of children were included in the study. The caregivers' ages ranged from 18 to 60 years, with a mean age of 32.3 ± 6.4. Of these, 148 (44.8%) had university-level education or higher, while 33 (10%) had education below high school level. Only 81 caregivers (24.5%) administered the correct dose of medication. In contrast, 118 (35.8%) gave subtherapeutic doses, 40 (12.1%) administered higher-than-recommended doses, and 91 (27.6%) were unsure about the correct dose. Multivariable regression indicated that caregivers with education below high school (aOR = 2.65; 95% CI: 1.30-5.40 for low dose) and those making self-directed dosing decisions (aOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.15-3.85 for low dose) were significantly associated with incorrect dosing. Conclusions: The study indicates that approximately three-quarters of caregivers either administered incorrect doses of acetaminophen or ibuprofen or were unsure of the correct dose. Given that 93% of caregivers were unaware of medication concentrations, targeted educational interventions are required to improve dosing accuracy.

articles.title: Longitudinal measurements of inflammatory mediators in patients at risk of sepsis in the Emergency Department.

abstract.text: Sepsis is a complex condition with time‑dependent evolution, and longitudinal biomarker dynamics may improve its characterisation. We hypothesised that biomarker kinetics are associated with sepsis, the intensity of organ dysfunction, and patient survival. This single‑centre, prospective, observational study included adult patients presenting to the Emergency Department with suspected infection and a National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) ≥3. Blood samples were collected at baseline, 4 and 24 h and pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, as well as other inflammatory mediators or acute-phase reactants, were analysed. Linear and nonlinear mixed-effects models assessed associations between biomarker trajectories over time, sepsis diagnosis, and organ dysfunction severity. Joint models evaluated the predictive value of biomarker kinetics during the first 24 h for in‑hospital mortality. Of 214 screened patients, 173 were analysed and 137(79%) developed sepsis. Linear and nonlinear mixed models showed significant time‑dependent decreases in IL10 (β -0.016, 95%CI -0.028 to -0.004), IL1RN (β -0.014, 95%CI -0.024 to -0.004), and IL6 (β -1.021, 95%CI -1.609 to -0.433 for the first spline 0-4 h). Sepsis diagnosis was associated with higher IL1RN (β 0.378, 95%CI 0.153-0.603) and TNFRSF1A (β 0.40, 95%CI 0.21-0.58); a significant interaction between sepsis and time was observed only for IL6 (β -0.33, CI95% -0.653 to-0.007) for the second spline 4-24 h. Increasing SOFA scores correlated with elevated IL10 (β 0.048), IL1RN (β 0.044), CCL2 (β 0.046), TNFRSF1A (β 0.050), and procalcitonin (PCT; β 2.15), all p < 0.01. The SOFA score-time interaction was significant only for IL6 (β 0.122, 95%CI 0.006 to 0.238 during the first spline 0-4 h followed by β -0.080, 95%CI -0.133 to -0.027 for the second spline 4-24 h). Joint survival models adjusted identified associations between longitudinal IL8 (HR 0.655, 95%CrI 0.582-0.728), TNFRSF1A (HR 0.505, 95%CrI 0.419-0.682), and PCT (HR 1.004, 95%CrI 1.001-1.008) concentrations and survival outcome. However, IL8 and TNFRSF1A showed an unexpected inverse association with survival, and the overall discriminatory performance was modest. In conclusion, Sepsis status and organ dysfunction severity were associated with distinct inflammatory biomarker levels and kinetics. IL6 showed a unique time‑dependent relationship, whereas the dynamics of TNFRSF1A, IL8 and PCT showed exploratory associations with survival. Further studies are warranted to confirm our results.

articles.title: Association of Maintenance Hemodialysis with Transfer to Post-Acute Rehabilitation After Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Maintenance hemodialysis (HD) is associated with poor outcomes after stroke, but its association with access to post-acute rehabilitation remains unclear. We examined rehabilitation transfer and outcomes according to maintenance HD status.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort included consecutive stroke patients admitted to a tertiary emergency care center during 2015-2023. The primary outcome was rehabilitation transfer among in-hospital survivors. Rehabilitation eligibility and reasons for non-transfer were assessed in the HD group. Firth logistic regression evaluated rehabilitation transfer, and multivariable logistic regression evaluated in-hospital mortality and favorable functional outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1173 patients, 54 received maintenance HD. Rehabilitation transfer occurred in 2 of 33 HD survivors (6.1%) and 299 of 937 non-HD survivors (31.9%; risk ratio, 0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.05-0.62; p < 0.001). After adjustment using Firth logistic regression, maintenance HD remained associated with lower odds of rehabilitation transfer (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.65; p = 0.005). Of 12 rehabilitation-eligible HD patients, 2 (16.7%) were transferred; no facility providing both maintenance HD and inpatient rehabilitation could be secured for the other 10. Maintenance HD was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR, 4.26; 95% CI, 2.20-8.24; p < 0.001) and lower odds of a favorable functional outcome (aOR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.19-0.77; p = 0.007).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Maintenance HD was associated with markedly lower rehabilitation transfer and poorer acute outcomes. Expanding access to facilities integrating dialysis and rehabilitation may improve continuity and equity of post-stroke care.

articles.title: Suicidal ideation and psychiatric comorbidity in a nationally representative sample of ED visits with documented gambling concerns.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Gambling disorder is associated with suicide and other severe harms. In an era of rapid gambling expansion, psychiatrists might benefit from information about the clinical needs of patients with gambling concerns who present to the emergency department (ED). We explored the characteristics of ED visits involving patients with gambling concerns and examined the prevalence and correlates of suicidal ideation within these visits.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2022 Nationwide Emergency Department Sample, representing 111,340,613 weighted visits by adult patients. Visits were assigned to the "gambling concerns" group if the record included a diagnostic code for gambling disorder or the "gambling and betting" lifestyle factor.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Several characteristics distinguished visits by patients with gambling concerns (weighted N = 1089) from the full sample, including a primary diagnosis of affective/anxiety disorder or a substance use disorder (SUD); hospitalization; and presence of suicidal ideation or intentional self-harm injury. Suicidal ideation and intentional self-harm injuries were documented in 39.7% and 7.8% of visits by patients with gambling concerns, respectively. Gambling concerns were rarely recorded as the primary diagnosis. Instead, over half of visits by patients with gambling concerns included a primary diagnosis of a psychiatric or SUD. Among visits by patients with gambling concerns, a primary diagnosis of affective/anxiety disorder was associated with higher likelihood of suicidal ideation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Gambling problems are often hidden within behavioral health ED presentations. The ED might provide a novel setting for detecting gambling disorder and gambling-related suicidality among patients with urgent behavioral health concerns.

articles.title: Quality of Movement Assessment after ACL Reconstruction in Youth: A Clinical Framework to Guide Rehabilitation and Return-to-Sport Decision-Making.
articles.journal_full: International journal of sports physical therapy

abstract.text: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most common knee injuries requiring surgical intervention in youth athletes. After ACL reconstruction surgery, youth athletes undergo prolonged rehabilitation which often concludes with return-to-sport (RTS) testing to determine the athlete's readiness to resume sports participation. Most rehabilitation and RTS literature have focused primarily on quantitative outcomes to guide these decisions. Given the relationship between trunk and lower extremity biomechanics with ACL injury risk, there has been a call to action for the inclusion of qualitative assessments in rehabilitation and return-to-sport assessments. The purpose of this commentary is to describe quality of movement assessment tools that can guide rehabilitation and RTS decision making in pediatric and adolescent patients following ACL reconstruction. Specifically, it provides a framework for the implementation and interpretation of tools to assess single-leg, double-leg, and change of direction tasks as well as practical strategies and considerations for their use with pediatric and adolescent patients after ACL reconstruction. # Level of Evidence 5.

articles.title: Admission TRIAGES score for unfavorable functional outcome after traumatic brain injury: association, prognostic performance, and comparison with the Glasgow coma scale.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Trauma Rating Index in Age, Glasgow Coma Scale, Respiratory rate, and Systolic blood pressure (TRIAGES) is a simple trauma score that has shown prognostic value for short-term mortality in traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its relationship with functional outcome remains insufficiently characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of adults with TBI admitted between June 2017 and May 2026. The primary exposure was the TRIAGES score calculated using age and the first GCS, respiratory rate, and systolic blood pressure values recorded at initial emergency department presentation before any in-hospital therapeutic intervention. Admission GCS was defined as the GCS value obtained at this same initial assessment. The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status at hospital discharge, defined as a discharge Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) score of 1-3. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration, Brier score, decision curve analysis, bootstrap internal validation, sensitivity analyses, and subgroup analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 753 patients, 181 (24.0%) had an unfavorable functional outcome. Each 1-point increase in TRIAGES was independently associated with higher odds of unfavorable functional status after adjustment for sex, injury mechanism, number of non-reactive pupils, and Rotterdam CT score (adjusted odds ratio 2.81, 95% confidence interval 2.29-3.45; p < 0.001). The association was approximately linear (P for non-linearity = 0.366). TRIAGES alone achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.905 compared with 0.890 for admission GCS alone (ΔAUC = 0.015, 95% CI 0.001-0.029; paired DeLong p = 0.034). Within this cohort, a Youden index-derived threshold of TRIAGES ≥3 yielded a sensitivity of 0.956 and specificity of 0.701. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.905, and the findings remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Higher TRIAGES scores at initial emergency presentation were independently associated with unfavorable functional status at hospital discharge in adults with TBI. TRIAGES showed good prognostic performance and a small within-cohort increase in discrimination relative to admission GCS alone while retaining the practical advantage of using only four routinely available variables. Prospective multicenter studies with external validation and standardized long-term functional outcomes are warranted.

articles.title: MDT-HMTL: A Multidimensional Temporal Hierarchical Multi-Task Learning Framework for Myocardial Infarction Detection and State Classification Using PPG Signals.

abstract.text: Continuous assessment of myocardial infarction (MI) using photoplethysmography (PPG) signals has potential for out-of-hospital cardiovascular monitoring, yet conventional single-channel and short-window approaches have limitations in capturing complex hemodynamic variations and dynamic disease-state transitions. To address these limitations, we propose MDT-HMTL, a Multidimensional Temporal Hierarchical Multi-Task Learning framework tailored for simultaneous MI detection and disease-state classification. By integrating multi-channel physiological representations with hierarchical temporal modeling, MDT-HMTL captures local morphological characteristics and longer-range temporal dependencies within a unified multi-task architecture. Evaluation on the MIMIC-III clinical database achieved an average area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.908 and an overall accuracy of 86.4%. Furthermore, ablation studies demonstrated the contributions of multi-dimensional representation learning and hierarchical temporal modeling to the overall performance. The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of PPG-based MI detection and longitudinal disease-state assessment, highlighting its potential for future non-invasive and wearable-compatible cardiovascular monitoring.

articles.title: Pre-Analytical Errors Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Multi-Year Retrospective Observational Study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The pre-analytical phase is the stage at which laboratory errors most frequently occur and is therefore of critical importance for patient safety. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the marked increase in workload, organizational restructuring, staff and resource redeployment, changes in patient volume and clinical workflows, and disease-related pathophysiological alterations affecting specimen characteristics created unprecedented conditions that could influence laboratory quality indicators. This study aimed to characterize changes in specimen rejection rates across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and normalization periods between 2018 and 2023, and to determine whether pandemic-related disruptions in health care delivery were associated with differences in the number, rate, and distribution of specimen rejections according to clinical unit, rejection reason, and time interval, with emphasis on the magnitude of these differences rather than statistical significance alone. The study also sought to generate evidence that could inform the development of preventive systems and strengthen laboratory preparedness for future large-scale disruptions to health care services.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study used routinely collected, aggregated laboratory information system (LIS) data from the Central Laboratory of Istanbul Atlas University Hospital for 1 January 2018 through 31 December 2023. The LIS extract was restricted to eligible specimen types, including spot and 24 h urine, serum, and whole-blood or plasma specimens collected in EDTA-, citrate-, or heparin-containing tubes; all other specimen types were excluded. Specimen rejection rates were evaluated by study period, clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason. For cross-period comparisons, the total number of specimens within each respective study period was used as the denominator for calculating rejection rates, whereas for rejection-reason-specific analyses, the number of specimen types relevant to each rejection category was used as the denominator. Negative-binomial regression with denominator-based offsets estimated adjusted rejection-rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with Bonferroni adjustment for selected pairwise comparisons. No missing or unclassifiable values were identified; no imputation was required. Reporting follows STROBE and the RECORD extension for studies using routinely collected health data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The overall rejection rate increased progressively from 0.23% in the pre-pandemic period to 0.49% during the pandemic and 0.65% in the normalization period, and monthly observed rates supported this progressive increase. In adjusted terms, the rejection rate was 2.20-fold higher during the pandemic than in the pre-pandemic period (95% CI: 1.96-2.46) and increased a further 1.42-fold in the normalization period compared with the pandemic period (95% CI: 1.27-1.59). Across clinical units, the emergency department had the highest observed rejection rate, whereas intensive care units showed the highest adjusted rejection rates during the pandemic (RR = 1.34 versus the emergency department, 95% CI: 1.00-1.80) and normalization periods. Hemolysis and clotting were the dominant rejection reasons; although clotting had the highest observed rates in the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods, hemolysis ranked highest after adjustment in all periods and separated significantly from clotting only in the normalization period (RR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.65-2.35). Time-interval effects were context-dependent rather than uniform and became informative mainly in combination with clinical unit or rejection reason: intensive care unit rejections peaked in the daytime interval during the pandemic (RR = 1.84 versus the evening interval, 95% CI: 1.06-3.19), and in the normalization period emergency department-hemolysis emerged as the leading adjusted clinical unit-rejection reason combination (RR = 1.89 versus intensive care unit-hemolysis, 95% CI: 1.19-3.00), while clotting remained centered on intensive care units and became more concentrated in the overnight and early-morning interval.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pre-analytical specimen rejection increased progressively across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and normalization periods, with adjusted effect sizes indicating a substantial and sustained deterioration rather than a transient pandemic-related disturbance, and with persistent differences in rejection patterns according to clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason. The further increase observed in the normalization period suggests that pandemic-related disruptions were associated with sustained changes in pre-analytical performance but were unlikely to be the sole explanation. Emergency department-hemolysis during the normalization period and intensive care unit-related clotting emerged as the most concrete quality-monitoring targets. Integrating rejection rates and counts with stratified monitoring by clinical unit, time interval, and rejection reason in combination may support earlier identification of emerging risks, more targeted preventive interventions, and stronger laboratory preparedness for future large-scale disruptions to health care services.

articles.title: Intra- and Inter-Operator Reliability of Internal Jugular Vein Ultrasound Image Acquisition by Ultrasound-Naive Nurses.

abstract.text: Background: Venous congestion assessment is essential in heart failure management. Inferior vena cava (IVC) ultrasonography has been widely used to determine fluid status but may not always provide satisfactory images. Hence, internal jugular vein (IJV) ultrasonography has been proposed as an alternative; however, the reliability of IJV ultrasound image acquisition by nurses without previous clinical ultrasound experience remains unclear. This study evaluated the intra- and inter-operator reliability of IJV ultrasound image acquisition by nurses without previous clinical ultrasound experience. Methods: Two nurses without prior clinical ultrasound experience acquired right IJV ultrasound images after preparatory training. Short-axis cine loops were obtained during quiet breathing and the Valsalva maneuver in healthy adults. A single investigator measured the major and minor diameters from selected still frames. Intra- and inter-operator reliability were then assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), after which agreement was evaluated by Bland-Altman analysis. Results: Both nurses successfully acquired IJV images suitable for subsequent quantitative analysis from all participants. Intra-operator reliability ranged from good to excellent, with ICC (1, 1) values of 0.765-0.967. Meanwhile, inter-operator reliability ranged from moderate to excellent, with ICC (2, 1) values of 0.629-0.916. Bland-Altman analysis revealed fixed bias in three parameters but no proportional bias. Absolute bias was <1 mm for all measurements. Conclusions: Following preparatory training, nurses without prior clinical ultrasound experience were able to acquire IJV ultrasound images with moderate-to-excellent inter-operator and good-to-excellent intra-operator relative reliability.

articles.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.

abstract.text: Motor vehicle collisions (MVCs) are among the most common mechanisms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and a meaningful proportion of affected individuals develop persistent post-concussion syndrome (PPCS) characterized by prolonged multidomain dysfunction. Conventional neuroimaging frequently fails to capture the underlying pathophysiology, leaving clinicians without objective diagnostic evidence. We describe a 57-year-old woman who sustained mTBI in a rear-end MVC in March 2023. Head computed tomography (CT) performed at the emergency department and a subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were both unremarkable. Despite normal structural neuroimaging, comprehensive multimodal functional assessment identified functional abnormalities across eight domains: vestibular function (videonystagmography (VNG)), cortical electrophysiology (quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG)), pupillary autonomics (automated infrared pupillometry), postural stability (computerized dynamic posturography (CDP)), oculomotor control (saccadometry), cardiac autonomic regulation (24-h heart rate variability (HRV)), olfaction (University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT)), and computerized concussion assessment (C3 Logix). Standardized psychological assessments confirmed moderate depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) = 14), moderate anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) = 12), clinically significant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms (PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) (PCL-5 = 38)), and substantial headache impact (Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) = 58). The patient underwent a 10-modality individualized rehabilitation program. Concussion Symptom Checklist (CSC) scores declined from 92 at initial presentation to 0 by July 2023 (17 weeks post-injury), with near-complete re-resolution to 8 by February 2024 following a transient stress-related exacerbation. When conventional neuroimaging is unremarkable, comprehensive multimodal functional testing may provide evidence consistent with mTBI pathophysiology and help guide targeted rehabilitation. This case illustrates the potential value of a systematic, multimodal approach in PPCS management, while acknowledging that definitive attribution of findings to the index injury is constrained by the single-case design and absence of a pre-injury functional baseline.
