articles.title: Beyond the Sagittal Plane: The Lateral Countermovement Jump as a Clinical Tool for Return-to-Play Decision-Making and Performance Evaluation.
articles.journal_full: International journal of sports physical therapy

abstract.text: Return-to-play (RTP) decision-making after lower-extremity injury has traditionally emphasized sagittal-plane assessments, including double and single leg vertical jump metrics, double and single-leg hop batteries, and quadriceps strength limb symmetry indices (LSI). Yet many sports place a disproportionate demand on frontal-plane, lateral force production; basketball players, for example, spend up to a third of their live game actions in a defensive shuffle or lateral cutting posture. Recent force-plate evidence supports the single-leg lateral countermovement jump (LCMJ) as a reliable, time-efficient, and low-load assessment capable of stratifying lateral movement competency in elite athletes. This clinical commentary reviews recent reliability and discriminant-validity data on the LCMJ, places the test within the broader RTP evidence base and its known limitations, and proposes a practical framework for incorporating relative lateral force testing into RTP and performance batteries used by physical therapists and sports medicine clinicians.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy as a potential treatment for MDD: a narrative review.

abstract.text: This narrative review explores the therapeutic potential of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBO2) in treating major depressive disorder (MDD). We highlight the common pathophysiological hypotheses for MDD, the strengths and limitations of current MDD treatments, and the potential for HBO2 to be a novel MDD therapeutic through anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective mechanisms. The current review discusses the monoamine, neuronal atrophy, and inflammation hypotheses of MDD pathophysiology origin, as well as how present MDD therapeutics target these MDD pathophysiological traits. While there are a multitude of existing treatments for MDD, including those pharmacological, psychotherapeutic, and neuromoduatory in nature, many treatments possess limitations. The management of difficult-to-treat depression is particularly challenging, highlighting the need for innovative, effective treatments to be developed. HBO2 is a potential novel therapy for MDD, exerting antidepressant effects through its ability to promote neurogenesis and anti-inflammatory processes in the central nervous system. Moreover, HBO2 has been indirectly correlated with an improvement in depressive symptoms in studies done in the context of treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), traumatic brain injury (TBI), post-stroke recovery, and post-coronavirus disease condition (post-COVID-19). However, there is currently a dearth of direct evidence supporting the indication of HBO2 for MDD, and clinical trials that investigate HBO2 as a primary treatment for MDD are needed. The current review provides a rationale for further exploration of the potential of HBO2 as a novel therapy for MDD.

articles.title: Burnout and Quality of Life Among Oncology Palliative Care Professionals: An Exploratory Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Oncology palliative care involves sustained engagement with suffering, loss, complex communication, and end-of-life decisions. This exploratory study compared burnout and quality of life among professionals working in oncology palliative care, intensive care, and emergency care, and secondarily with a heterogeneous reference group. Methods: A cross-sectional convenience sample included 68 healthcare professionals from two hospital units within the same Portuguese public hospital organization: oncology palliative care (N = 22), intensive care (N = 15), emergency care (N = 9), and other healthcare professionals (N = 22). Burnout and quality of life were assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey and WHOQOL-BREF, respectively. Analyses used complete cases for each multivariate outcome set. Results: No statistically significant multivariate differences were detected across the three clinical groups in burnout (Pillai's Trace = 0.187; F(6, 84) = 1.442; p = 0.208) or quality of life (Pillai's Trace = 0.146; F(10, 78) = 0.613; p = 0.798). In the secondary burnout comparison (n = 38), emotional exhaustion was higher in oncology palliative care (mean difference = 5.78; 95% CI 0.37-11.19; unadjusted p = 0.037; partial η2 = 0.115). No multivariate quality-of-life difference was detected in the secondary comparison (n = 39; p = 0.387). Conclusions: The non-significant findings do not establish equivalence between clinical settings. The nominal emotional-exhaustion difference is hypothesis-generating and requires replication. Small, unequal groups, missing data, multiple testing, and limited occupational characterization constrain precision and interpretation.

articles.title: Prehospital Point-of-Care GFAP for Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage in Acute Nontraumatic Coma.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Rapid identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with acute nontraumatic coma is critical to guiding triage and early management; however, prehospital diagnostic tools remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of prehospital whole-blood point-of-care measurement of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for detecting ICH.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This diagnostic study used data collected by a UK physician-paramedic helicopter emergency medical service between January 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. A consecutive sample of adult patients (aged ≥16 years) presenting with acute nontraumatic coma, defined as Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or less, who underwent prehospital rapid sequence induction (RSI) of anesthesia with clinical suspicion of ICH were eligible for inclusion. Patients with traumatic pathology and those without follow-up data were excluded. Patients were observed for up for 30 days from hospital admission. Data analysis was performed in June 2026.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: Prehospital whole-blood point-of-care brain biomarker (GFAP and UCH-L1) testing using the i-STAT Alinity Point-of-Care Blood Analyzer (Abbott Laboratories).

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES
abstract.text: Diagnostic accuracy of GFAP and UCH-L1 for detecting ICH, using computed tomography as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The primary study cohort comprised 65 patients who underwent prehospital brain biomarker testing (median age, 63 [IQR, 47-69] years; 55.4% male). The median (IQR) GCS score was 4 (3-6). ICH was present in 50.8% (n = 33). Thirteen (20.0%) patients underwent neurosurgery, and the 30-day survival rate was 46.2% (n = 30). GFAP demonstrated high sensitivity (97.0%; 95% CI, 84.2%-99.9%) and discriminatory ability (AUC, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.87-0.99). UCH-L1 showed lower sensitivity (78.8%; 95% CI, 61.1%-91.0%) and specificity (18.8%; 95% CI, 7.2%-36.4%), with limited discriminatory performance. A combined biomarker approach achieved 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 89.4%-100.0%) and a negative predictive value of 100.0% (95% CI, 47.8%-100.0%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this diagnostic study of adults with acute nontraumatic coma undergoing prehospital RSI, point-of-care prehospital GFAP testing was feasible and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting intracranial hemorrhage. Further prospective external validation is required to determine its association with triage, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: [Impact of an Integrated Care Model in Patients with COPD and High Risk of Readmission].

abstract.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with high morbidity and healthcare utilization, particularly due to acute exacerbations leading to Emergency Department (ED) visits and hospital admissions. Patients with multimorbidity and social vulnerability are at increased risk of readmission. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of an early, multidisciplinary, integrated care model on ED visits and hospitalizations among high-risk patients with COPD. A single-center pre-post intervention study was conducted following implementation of the Early Pulmonology Assessment/Individualised and Integrated Care Plan (EPA/IICP) protocol in February 2024. High-risk patients were identified using the LACE Index (> 9, or 5 - 9 with additional risk factors). The intervention combined medical, nursing, and social assessment with hybrid follow-up (face-to-face and remote monitoring). The primary outcomes were the number of ED visits and hospitalizations in the year before and after enrolment. Paired Student's t-tests were used for analysis. Fifty-three patients were included (mean age 67.6 years; 62% male). Baseline comorbidity and readmission risk were high (mean Charlson index 4.5; mean LACE 13.8). After one year, mean ED visits decreased from 3.09 to 0.67 (p < 0.001), and hospitalizations from 1.39 to 0.33 (p < 0.001). Remote monitoring generated early clinical interventions, with only two admissions for severe respiratory failure. Social intervention enabled most patients to maintain or regain home-based care. An early, integrated, hybrid care model was associated with significant reductions in ED visits and hospitalizations in high-risk COPD patients. This approach may represent a sustainable strategy for managing complex chronic respiratory disease.

articles.title: Federal Immigration Enforcement Deployment and Emergency Department Utilization Among Children.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Heightened immigration enforcement in the US has been associated with reduced health care utilization in immigrant communities. Pediatric emergency departments (EDs) serve as a critical safety net for children, yet the impacts of acute immigration enforcement activity in pediatric ED utilization remain incompletely characterized.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether deployment of federal law enforcement in Washington, DC, was associated with changes in pediatric ED utilization and whether these changes differed by the patients' preferred language, race, and ethnicity.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This repeated cross-sectional interrupted time series analysis compared daily pediatric ED visits from June 1 to September 30, 2025, with visits in the same calendar period in 2024 at a single pediatric ED at a freestanding children's hospital in Washington, DC. Participants included all patients younger than 26 years presenting to the pediatric ED during the study period.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Deployment of federal law enforcement personnel, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and National Guard troops, in Washington, DC, beginning August 11, 2025.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary outcome was daily pediatric ED visit counts. Interrupted time series models estimated immediate changes in ED utilization and postdeployment trends by patient-preferred language, race, and ethnicity, adjusting for age, sex, and acuity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 21 822 pediatric ED visits were included in the analysis (median age, 6.5 [IQR, 2.0-13.1] years; 11 505 visits [52.7%] by male patients). Among these visits, 6253 patients (28.7%) identified as Hispanic, 10 649 (48.8%) as non-Hispanic Black, 2200 (10.1%) as non-Hispanic White, 558 (2.6%) as non-Hispanic multiracial, 1411 (6.5%) as non-Hispanic additional race, and 652 (3.0%), unknown. Patients who preferred to speak Spanish experienced an estimated immediate change in visits following federal deployment of -10.4 visits per day, whereas patients who preferred English experienced an estimated immediate change of 5.6 visits per day (difference, -16.0 visits per day). Hispanic patients similarly experienced an estimated immediate change of -13.3 visits per day, whereas non-Hispanic patients experienced an estimated immediate change of 6.2 visits per day (difference, -19.4 visits per day). Among Hispanic patients, those preferring Spanish had greater estimated immediate changes (-12.1 visits per day) than those preferring English (-0.8 visits per day; difference, -11.3 visits per day). No significant differences were observed across non-Hispanic racial and ethnic groups. No comparable declines were observed during the same period in 2024.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this repeated cross-sectional study of pediatric ED visits before and after a federal immigration enforcement deployment, heightened immigration enforcement activity was associated with an immediate reduction in pediatric ED utilization, particularly among patients who preferred to speak Spanish. These findings suggest that immigration enforcement may have unintended consequences for children's use of emergency care.

articles.title: Postoperative morbidity among survivors of emergency war trauma surgery in a conflict setting: a descriptive cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Evidence on surgical outcomes in active conflict settings remains limited, particularly regarding postoperative morbidity and its relationship to injury severity among civilians with severe war-related injuries. This study describes the pattern of postoperative morbidity following emergency surgery for conflict-related abdominal and thoracic trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a cohort study of patients undergoing emergency war trauma surgery at a single surgical unit during the 2024 Gaza conflict. Data were collected prospectively and supplemented through retrospective review when needed. To avoid conflating early postoperative death with an absence of morbidity, postoperative morbidity was described only among patients who survived to hospital discharge.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-nine patients were included. Five patients (6%) died intraoperatively and were excluded from postoperative analysis. Of the remaining 74 patients, 20 (27%) died during the index admission and 54 (73%) survived to discharge; non-survivors had substantially higher Injury Severity Scores than survivors (median ISS 32 vs 16) and were less often haemodynamically stable on arrival (12% vs 67%). Among the 54 survivors, postoperative morbidity occurred in 46 (85%), mainly due to infectious complications (81%), particularly surgical site infection (74%). Descriptive comparison of survivors with and without morbidity showed similar injury severity between groups (median ISS 16 vs 16.5), suggesting that once patients survived long enough to be at risk of complications, morbidity was common across the injury-severity spectrum rather than concentrated among the most severely injured.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Postoperative morbidity after conflict-related emergency surgery was high among survivors and was largely driven by infectious complications. Mortality, rather than morbidity, was most closely related to injury severity. These findings support the need for consistent injury severity assessment, improved infection prevention strategies, and cautious interpretation of morbidity data in conflict cohorts where early mortality limits the population at risk of developing recorded complications.

articles.title: Small Town, Big Lessons-A Blended Supervision Placement Reflection.

abstract.text: The new blended supervision placement (BSP) presents an expanded array of training opportunities for TS2/3 ACEM registrars in regional, rural and remote locations. These newly accredited sites, previously not eligible for recognised training time, offer varied learning opportunities in both clinical and non-clinical domains. The development of this placement is aligned with the 2027 curriculum alteration in rural and remote training requirements for ACEM trainees, and reflects real workforce evolution around Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand. This opinion piece is a reflection on one TS2 trainee's recent experience at the newly BSP-accredited Macksville District Hospital on the NSW mid north coast. It reflects the value of continuity in clinical supervision across a parent and peripheral site, as well as the professional and personal rewards of practising emergency medicine in a smaller and more connected community.

articles.title: [Subclavian steal syndrome: a case report].

abstract.text: An 80-year-old female presented to the emergency department with dizziness, generalized weakness, and exertional dyspnea. Physical examination revealed a significant inter-arm systolic blood pressure discrepancy. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the chest demonstrated high-grade stenosis at the origin of the left subclavian artery, correlating with both the clinical symptoms and the hemodynamic findings. This case underscores the diagnostic utility of CTA in ensuring a prompt and precise evaluation of subclavian artery stenosis in patients presenting with inter-arm blood pressure differentials.

articles.title: Examining Moral Distress and Turnover Intention in Newly Licensed Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To examine moral distress and turnover intention among newly licensed nurses in the acute care setting.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Cross-sectional.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used purposive sampling to recruit newly licensed nurses working in the acute care setting in a multistate healthcare organisation. Participants completed a demographic survey, the Measure of Moral Distress for Healthcare Professionals and the Turnover Intention Scale-6 between May 2025 and June 2026. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, one-way analysis of variance and multiple linear regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 203 nurses, 194 were registered nurses and nine were licensed practical nurses working in Medical Surgical/Stepdown (43%), Critical Care/Emergency Department (48%) and Procedural/Surgical/Other (9%) units. Moral distress and turnover intention scores in the Medical Surgical/Stepdown departments were significantly higher than the other two groups. We found that moral distress was associated with turnover intention, controlling for department and nursing credential.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Moral distress is an important factor in turnover intention among newly licensed nurses. Organizational initiatives and early interventions that reduce moral distress may lower turnover intention and improve wellbeing. Differences in moral distress and turnover among departments and nurse credentials call for further investigations to develop department-specific interventions.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE
abstract.text: This study has global implications for nursing leaders and educators to assess moral distress as a potential indicator for turnover intention. New nurse attrition continues to challenge healthcare organisations, and interventions that support new nurses are recommended. With the growth of the nursing workforce, opportunities to assess and implement interventions for moral distress can occur within nurse residency programs. This study broadens the evidence base by including licensed practical nurses in acute care. By analysing data on moral distress and turnover intention early in nurses' careers, nurse educators and leaders are provided with a unique perspective into the transition to practice period. Healthcare organisations can implement strategies to recognise and assess moral distress to bolster efforts to support the nursing workforce and retention initiatives.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: These findings contribute to the gap in the literature on moral distress and turnover among new nurses, underline the complexities of the acute care environment and highlight the need for specialty tailored interventions. This study provides insight into initiatives that can support global nursing workforce sustainability.

abstract.label: REPORTING METHOD
abstract.text: STROBE.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: No patient or public contribution. Patients nor the public were involved in this research.

articles.title: Regional, Rural and Ready: Making the New RRR Training Requirement Count.

abstract.text: From 2027, new ACEM trainees must complete 6 months of emergency medicine training at an eligible regional, rural or remote site. The requirement aligns training more closely with where emergency physicians work and offers valuable experience in generalism and decision making with limited resources. Its success will depend on authentic placements, supportive training networks and employment arrangements that recognise the burden of relocation.

articles.title: A Mixed Methods Evaluation of a Model of Care for Domestic Violence Within the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the scope and extent of the Domestic Violence (DV) Model of Care at Campbelltown Emergency Department (ED). We detail patient population characteristics, means of identifying victim-survivors, care provided, and factors associated with social work review.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This mixed-methods evaluation utilised (1) retrospective audits of medical records of patients admitted to Campbelltown ED in 2024, who (a) responded affirmatively on the DV Routine Screening (DVRS) tool, and/or (b) were reviewed by social work relating to DV; and (2) semi-structured interviews with 19 clinicians and support workers about their understanding of and role within the model of care. Descriptive analyses quantified the scope and characteristics of the DV patient population and care provision; logistic regression identified factors associated with DVRS-identified patients seeing social work. Thematic analysis of interview data supplemented audit findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 2024, 249 ED patients responded affirmatively to the DVRS tool (DV identified prior for 52.2%), and 231 patients were reviewed by social work relating to DV. Victim-survivors were identified through DVRS tool use, explicit disclosure, referral from community partners, and clinician judgement. Transfer to the ED short stay unit facilitated safety and trauma/violence-informed care, including social work consultation for 49.8% of identified victim-survivors. Explicit disclosure or help-seeking, presenting concerns, and child safety risks were associated with seeing social work; however, presentation day/time was not.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This evaluation demonstrates that a comprehensive ED model of care, employing multiple means of identifying victim-survivors, is able to facilitate trauma/violence-informed psychosocial care alongside medical management for patients experiencing DV.

articles.title: Sports betting, online gambling, and suicidal behavior: a relationship to consider in emergency departments.
articles.journal_full: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

articles.title: Progression of emergency obstetric care for unplanned out-of-hospital births: contributions from a 13-year prospective multicenter study in France.
articles.journal_full: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe temporal trends in prehospital obstetric care for unplanned out-of-hospital births (UOHBs), assess adherence to clinical practice guidelines, and identify areas for improvement in training and health care organization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis using prospectively collected data from the French UOHB registry. A total of 3,473 births attended between October 2011 and June 2024 by 79 Emergency Medical Services centers were included. We analyzed temporal trends in maternal characteristics, modes of delivery, prehospital obstetric and neonatal care, and the main care-related time intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant increases were observed in the interval from the call to the dispatch center to the arrival of the medical team (P = .01) and in the time from delivery to placental expulsion (P < .01). The use of prophylactic oxytocin for active management of placental delivery increased (P = .01). By contrast, neonatal blood glucose measurement (P = .01) and routine nasopharyngeal suctioning (P < .01) decreased. In neonatal care, in situ temperature measurement decreased (P < .01). The use of caps, polyethylene bags, and blankets decreased, whereas skin-to-skin contact and incubator use during transport increased. The proportion of newborns who received no thermal protection measures increased (P = .045).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Periodic dissemination of clinical practice guidelines has been associated with relevant changes in prehospital practice and greater adherence to recommendations. Nevertheless, important challenges remain, including increased response times, the need to consolidate the systematic use of prophylactic oxytocin, and effective prevention of neonatal hypothermia.

articles.title: Exploring the triage accuracy of the Manchester Triage System and the Emergency Severity Index in emergency department patients with sepsis: A secondary retrospective analysis.
articles.journal_full: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To meet the requirement of the Sepsis-3 guidelines for rapid initiation of treatment, emergency department (ED) triage systems must assign patients with suspected sepsis to the highest-priority triage categories. Our aim was to explore how effectively the Manchester Triage System (MTS) and the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assign these patients to appropriate urgency categories and avoid undertriage.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A secondary analysis was conducted from a prospective, multicenter observational study (LIFE-POC), which included patients presenting with suspected organ dysfunction in 1 of 3 participant EDs (2 using MTS and 1 using ESI). The primary endpoint was a diagnosis of sepsis within 24 hours of ED presentation. Patients diagnosed with sepsis who were assigned to urgent triage categories 1, 2, or 3 were classified as accurately triaged. Ethical approval was granted by the committees of the participating centers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 388 out of 1,424 patients were diagnosed with sepsis within 24 hours of ED presentation. MTS showed a sensitivity rate of 88.2% (undertriage, 11.8%), while ESI reached 99.0% (undertriage, 1.0%). Both triage tools demonstrated low specificity: 17.5% (MTS) and 2.7% (ESI). Binary logistic regression analysis indicated that the probability of sepsis increased with higher urgency triage categories and decreased in lower urgency categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Both ESI and MTS demonstrated high sensitivity in assigning septic patients to higher urgency categories, with better performance by ESI. However, MTS showed superior discrimination between urgency levels and may therefore be more compatible with the resource limitations typically encountered in EDs.

articles.title: Impact of overnight boarding in the emergency department on in-hospital mortality and length of hospital stay among older patients.
articles.journal_full: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the association between overnight boarding in the emergency department after the decision to admit and in-hospital mortality and total episode duration among older patients admitted through the emergency department of a minimally overcrowded hospital in Boston (Massachusetts, United States).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using MIMIC-IV data from 2011 through 2019. Patients aged 65 years or older who were admitted through the emergency department and had a documented admission order were included; patients admitted to intensive care were excluded. Overnight boarding was defined as remaining in the emergency department until 8:00 AM, whereas controls were defined as patients who left the emergency department before midnight. Five sensitivity analyses were performed, with adjustment for age, sex, and comorbidity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this selected low-risk cohort, overnight boarding was not associated with in-hospital mortality or total episode duration. However, the small number of events and the potential for selection bias preclude ruling out a harmful effect.

articles.title: 24-hour limit: development of a calculator to estimate mortality attributable to delayed admission from the emergency department in patients older than 75 years.
articles.journal_full: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To develop a clinical impact calculator aimed at estimating the number of potentially preventable in-hospital deaths associated with reducing emergency department stays exceeding 24 hours in patients aged 75 years or older.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We developed a conceptual model based on hospital structural and health care delivery data and risk estimates derived from the scientific literature. Exposure was defined as waiting > 24 hours for hospital admission. Impact was estimated by calculating the attributable fraction among exposed individuals, applying different exposurereduction scenarios and performing sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The calculator enables transformation of relative risks derived from observational studies and meta-analyses into absolute estimates of potentially preventable deaths, expressed as monthly or annual periods. The estimated number of potentially preventable deaths was approximately 124 annual cases in the baseline scenario (RR, 1.3), reaching approximately 239 cases in higher-vulnerability scenarios (RR, 1.8). Although based on aggregated realworld data, these figures should be interpreted as population-level estimates derived from a model and do not constitute causal clinical validation. The model allows estimation of the impact of reducing the proportion of patients remaining in emergency departments for more than 24 hours on in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Reducing prolonged waiting times for hospital admission from emergency departments could prevent a substantial number of in-hospital deaths among older patients. The developed tool facilitates consideration of the 24-hour limit as a patient safety standard and supports implementation of organizational strategies aimed at minimizing boarding.

articles.title: Exploring the Application of Machine Learning for Daily-Life Near-Fall Detection in Older Adults.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Falls are a health concern among older adults, and near-falls may serve as an early indicator of future falls, functional decline, and the need for targeted preventive interventions. While previous research has successfully demonstrated near-fall detection using machine learning in controlled laboratory environments, it remains crucial to evaluate the application of such approaches in daily-life settings.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: This study examines the application of a pre-trained machine learning algorithm to detect gait perturbations in daily-life and to explore how these classified gait perturbations are associated with participant characteristics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data from the SeFallED study was used, which followed up on individuals aged ≥ 60 years who presented to the emergency department following a fall. Daily stepping time was recorded using a thigh-worn accelerometer over 7 days, segmented into windows, and analyzed using a laboratory-based pre-trained one-dimensional convolutional neural network to detect near-falls.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 202 participants (median age 75 years) were included in the analysis. On average, 58% of total stepping time windows were classified as gait perturbation windows. Higher age, lower cognitive and functional performance, greater concerns about falling, and higher levels of frailty were associated with a greater proportion of classified gait perturbations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The laboratory-trained algorithm classified a high number of windows as gait perturbations, likely reflecting gait irregularities including misclassifications rather than exclusively near-falls. Although these classifications still meaningfully reflect participant characteristics, further training and validation are required to enhance the algorithm's ability to accurately distinguish and objectively assess gait perturbations and near-falls in daily-life.

articles.title: Conservative Versus Higher Oxygen Targets Post-Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Optimal oxygenation following return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) remains uncertain, as both hypoxemia and hyperoxemia risk secondary injury. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing the efficacy of restrictive versus higher oxygenation targets.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis following the PRISMA 2020 protocol was carried out from database inception through June 2026. Only RCTs examining the impact of restrictive oxygenation versus higher oxygenation for adult CA patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation were included. Risks of bias and the quality of the evidence were evaluated using RoB 2 and GRADE tools. A random-effects model was used for data synthesis and presented the results in RR/MD.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eleven RCTs (12 reports) involving 4136 participants were included. Restrictive oxygenation showed no significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.88-1.06) or unfavorable neurological outcomes (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.88-1.04). Most subgroup analyses were non-significant, except for reduced mortality in the strict hypothermia subgroup (33°C-34°C), although TSA showed unstable evidence. No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. Restrictive oxygenation increased hypoxemia risk (RR 1.65) but improved ventilator-free days (MD 2.14).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There is no significant improvement in overall mortality, neurological outcome, or any other major clinical endpoint in adult CA patients with restrictive oxygen compared to higher oxygen therapy. Under current normothermia (36°C-37.5°C) protocols, the accumulated evidence trends toward futility for a restrictive approach, though the definitive information size has not yet been entirely accrued. Although restrictive levels could lead to an increased number of ventilator-free days, there will be an increased risk of hypoxemia.

articles.title: Prevalence of Professional Interpreter Use in Emergency Departments: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) increasingly serve linguistically diverse populations. Professional interpretation improves care, yet its use remains variable. Quantifying the prevalence of use and understanding disparities can inform policies and interventions. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of professional interpreter use in English-speaking EDs and compare use across patient populations and countries.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Eight databases were searched from inception to May 15, 2025. We screened full texts included in a prior scoping review to identify studies reporting the prevalence of professional interpreter use among patients requiring interpretation in English-speaking EDs. We pooled prevalence overall and stratified by population (adult vs. children) and country (United States vs. other), with 95% prediction intervals and confidence intervals (CIs). Meta-regression assessed associations between study year and prevalence. Risk of bias was evaluated using the JBI checklist for prevalence studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-two studies spanning 1997-2025 involving 65,736 participants were included. Professional interpreters were used in 29% (CI, 20%, 38%) of encounters with patients requiring interpretation. Use was higher with children (49%; CI, 41%, 58%) than adults (16%; CI, 11%, 22%), and higher in the United States (33%; CI, 24%, 43%) than other countries (14%; CI, 4%, 30%). There was no significant association between study year and interpreter use (p = 0.38).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite known benefits, professional interpreter use in EDs remains low, particularly among adults and outside the United States. Addressing this gap will require coordinated efforts from clinicians, health system leaders, and policymakers to improve access to and accountability for language-concordant care in EDs.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Point of Care Ultrasound for Pulmonary Embolism.

articles.title: Pediatric Tear Gas Poisoning in Southern Israel: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes.
articles.journal_full: The Israel Medical Association journal : IMAJ

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pepper spray and tear gas are chemical irritants causing ocular, dermal, and respiratory injury. Data specific to pediatric emergency department (PED) presentations remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and short-term outcomes of chemical irritant exposure in children presenting to a tertiary PED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 0-18 years of age presenting to a single tertiary PED between 2016 and 2024 following civilian-grade chemical irritant exposure. Cases were identified using ICD-9 codes and free-text electronic medical records search. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, treatment, and disposition were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 84 pediatric patients (median age 12.5 years, IQR 6.0-15.6; 69.0% male). Exposures occurred most commonly at home (44.0%) and school (36.9%). Ocular involvement was common. Superficial punctate keratitis was identified in 54.5% of patients who underwent fluorescein examination by ophthalmologist (21.5% of the total cohort). Respiratory and dermal symptoms were mild and self-resolving. No severe complications were documented; 96.4% were discharged home.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Civilian-grade chemical irritant exposures in children were predominantly self-limited and managed successfully with conservative ED care, supporting decontamination-based protocols while highlighting home and school settings as priorities for prevention.

articles.title: Critical Care Nurses' Encounters With Multicultural Patients and Families in Saudi Arabia: A Qualitative Study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To examine the perceptions and experiences of local and expatriate critical care nurses when interacting with multicultural patients and their families in Saudi healthcare settings.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A descriptive qualitative exploratory design was employed to gain an in-depth understanding using purposive sampling.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, conducted in English, with 18 nurses from intensive care, cardiac care, burn and emergency units. We operationally defined multicultural patients and families as those whose nationality, language, religion, or cultural background differed from that of the treating nurse (see Section 1 for the full definition). Interviews explored nurses' perceptions and encounters with multicultural patients and families. Transcribed data were analysed using thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four major themes emerged. Communication barriers, particularly language differences, were the most frequently reported and, according to participants, the most immediately consequential challenge, since language determined whether basic clinical information could be exchanged at all; cultural and religious beliefs, limited health literacy and organisational constraints shaped how well that information was received and acted upon. Nurses employed adaptive strategies, including teamwork, translation technologies and institutional support (e.g., embassies, social workers), largely in the absence of formal interpreter services. Nurses described a strong personal and professional commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion; however, most reported little or no structured training in cultural competence, relying instead on informal, experience-based learning and identified specific system-level gaps in interpreter provision and culturally adapted policy.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Critical care nurses face substantial challenges in caring for multicultural patients. Enhancing cultural competence requires tailored training, adequate resources and system-level support. These findings underscore the importance of organisational policies and infrastructure that promote culturally sensitive, patient-centred care.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Structured cultural competence training and access to system-level resources, including professional interpreters and culturally adapted policies, are essential. These measures enable nurses to communicate effectively, respect patients' cultural and religious practices, and deliver equitable, patient-centred care.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: The study highlights key communication barriers and effective strategies for culturally competent care in post-Vision 2030 Saudi healthcare settings. Findings may inform education, policy and practice and support efforts to strengthen patient-family-nurse interactions and culturally responsive care.

abstract.label: REPORTING METHOD
abstract.text: We adhered to the relevant EQUATOR Network reporting guidance using the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ); the completed COREQ checklist is provided in Table S1.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Surgeon preferences and educational gaps in the treatment of complex distal radius fractures in Latin America.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Distal radius fractures are among the most common skeletal injuries, yet their optimal treatment remains controversial. Variability in surgical decision-making has been observed among surgeons. This study aimed to identify treatment preferences among Latin American orthopaedic surgeons with different training backgrounds and levels of experience in the management of complex distal radius fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A two-part questionnaire was distributed to orthopaedic and hand surgeons across Latin America. The first section collected demographic data, and the second section presented 7 clinical scenarios involving complex distal radius fractures. Multivariate analysis using multinomial logistic regression was performed to assess the influence of age and fellowship training on treatment decision-making, with results expressed as odds ratios. P-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 617 completed questionnaires were analyzed. Most respondents were male orthopaedic surgeons with fellowship training in orthopaedic trauma or hand surgery. Most surgeons reported managing 10-25 distal radius fracture cases annually as the lead surgeon and had access to both anatomical angle-stable volar plates and fragment-specific implants. Older surgeons tended to favor more traditional techniques, whereas those with hand surgery fellowship training were more likely to adopt advanced fixation strategies and a broader range of surgical approaches.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Surgeon age and fellowship training in hand surgery were the most influential factors in treatment decision-making for complex distal radius fractures. These findings highlight an opportunity for AO Trauma Latin America to expand educational offerings focused on the treatment of complex distal radius fractures.

articles.title: Prehospital qSOFA Is Associated with 30-Day Mortality Within Emergency Department Triage Strata in Ambulance-Transported Adults with Suspected Infection: An Exploratory Three-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Prehospital quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) screens poorly for sepsis, but an already-recorded field score may still inform the receiving physician. We asked whether it is associated with 30-day mortality within each emergency department (ED) triage classification, and what it adds to the arrival score. Methods: This study focused on a retrospective cohort of 1077 adults with suspected infection transported by ambulance to one Turkish university hospital ED, 2022 to 2024 (42.1% of 2558 eligible; most exclusions arose because the hospital episode record could not be retrieved). Patients were stratified by ED-arrival qSOFA classification (2 or more), then by prehospital classification. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality from hospital and national death records. The stratified analysis was post hoc. Results: Among 685 triage-negative patients, 30-day mortality was 13.9% when the field score had been below 2 and 26.0% when it had been 2 or more (adjusted odds ratio 2.06, 95% CI 1.28 to 3.25); among 392 triage-positive patients, 40.4% and 55.2% (1.84, 1.23 to 2.76), with no evidence of heterogeneity between strata (interaction odds ratio 0.85, 0.46 to 1.58). Adding the field value to the arrival value raised the area under the curve from 0.682 to 0.713. Added to a model of age, sex, comorbidity, lactate, oxygen saturation, heart rate, and temperature, it remained associated with death (1.71, 1.24 to 2.34) but changed the area under the curve by 0.007 (p = 0.23). In 27 selection scenarios returning the 1481 excluded patients, only a reversed association among them could nullify the triage-negative association, whereas the triage-positive association was nullified in 17 scenarios, 4 of them by a positive association. Conclusions: In this highly selected single-centre cohort, the prehospital qSOFA carried prognostic information not captured by the arrival score, with small incremental discrimination beyond routine ED data. The findings support preserving prehospital physiology at handover and justify prospective validation, not a change in disposition decisions.

articles.title: Azithromycin for acute wheezing and bronchiolitis in children younger than six years: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Azithromycin is often prescribed off-label for acute wheezing and bronchiolitis in young children, despite guideline advice against routine antibiotics. We synthesised the randomised evidence and tested whether benefit depends on care setting.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We searched four databases and two registries to June 2026 for double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of azithromycin versus placebo in children younger than six years with acute wheezing or bronchiolitis. The acute episode was pooled as the ratio of means and binary outcomes as risk ratios (random-effects models).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten trials (2,071 children) were included. In emergency-department and ward patients, azithromycin had no effect on the acute episode (ratio of means 0.99, 95 % CI 0.96-1.04; I2=0 %) and did not reduce hospitalisation or recurrent wheeze. Apparent benefit was confined to intensive-care and home-treated recurrent episodes (between-subgroup p<0.0001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Azithromycin does not help children with acute wheezing or bronchiolitis where it is used; routine use is not supported.

articles.title: Effects of pregabalin added to a multimodal anesthetic protocol in cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy.

abstract.text: Advancement in anesthetic protocols is necessary to address the evolving challenges of perioperative cats' management in veterinary practice. In this study, 54 cats were enrolled and were randomly assigned to either Group P (Pregabalin, PGB) or Group C (Control). Group P received 5 mg/kg of PGB orally 90 min before hospital admission, while Group C received identical empty capsules. Sedation was assessed using a Feline Multiparametric Sedation Scale and a Simple Qualitative Scale. All cats were premedicated with methadone (0.2 mg/kg IM) and alfaxalone (1 mg/kg IM). Anesthesia was induced with propofol at 2 mg/kg and maintained with isoflurane. Physiological parameters (HR, RR, SpO2, EtCO2, Blood Pressure, and Temperature) were monitored throughout surgery. In the immediate postoperative period, the Glasgow Feline Composite Measure Pain Scale short-form and the Feline Grimace Scale were used, measured at 0, 15, 30, and 60 min after extubation. Statistical analysis included Two-way ANOVA for physiological data and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney tests for pain and sedation scores. Sedation scores increased in Group P by 2.46 (95% CI: 1.69 to 3.23; p < 0.001). Conversely, the scores of the scales used in the immediate postoperative period were significantly lower in the Group P at all evaluation times -2.15 (95% CI: -2.92 to -1.39; p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in physiological parameters. In conclusion, prehospital administration of PGB provides effective sedation and improves postoperative comfort, making it a valuable adjunct to feline anesthesia protocols.

articles.title: 5G intelligent airport platform for UAV blood transport in Shenzhen China: a retrospective observational study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Efficient and secure blood transport is critical in healthcare. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, drones) offer potential advantages in timeliness and safety, with more than 10 regions in China having implemented drone-based blood transport. However, challenges remain, including limited visual monitoring and management models constrained by specific drone types and operational conditions. Developing an open, collaborative, and intelligently managed drone transport platform is thus of significant value.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Shenzhen Blood Center utilized 5G technology to enable intelligent closed-loop management of blood distribution, route planning, and emergency dispatch and hospital reception. The system supports real-time temperature monitoring and live video surveillance during flights. By integrating open drone airports and intelligent management systems, the first "5G-enabled Intelligent Airport Platform for Drone Blood Transportation" in China was established, accommodating multiple multi-rotor drone models. Its feasibility and operational effectiveness were systematically evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: As of August 31, 2025, the platform includes two drone systems, 18 routes, and serves 15 hospitals. From January 1, 2024, to August 31, 2025, 11,784 flights transported 8,320.82 kg of blood, including 25,803 U of red blood cells, 3,383 therapeutic doses of platelets, 1,357,733 ml of plasma, and 10,314 U of cryoprecipitate. The cumulative flight time was 178,640.9 min, with an average flight duration of 15.2 min. Compared to ground transport, drones saved an average of 46.8 min (peak) and 32.3 min (off-peak). All blood products met temperature requirements, with no damage or temperature deviations recorded.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study demonstrates that a 5G-based drone platform reliably supports routine and emergency blood transport, ensuring timeliness and quality. It offers an innovative management model for blood collection and supply institutions. Future efforts will expand routes and coverage, enhance emergency supply capacity, establish a citywide drone blood transportation network and promote the low-altitude economy in healthcare.

articles.title: Vascular norepinephrine responsiveness index for early risk stratification in emergency department septic shock: a real-world cohort study from a Latin American sepsis code registry.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Septic shock is characterized by heterogeneous vascular responsiveness to norepinephrine. The vascular norepinephrine responsiveness index (VNERi), calculated as diastolic arterial pressure divided by the product of norepinephrine dose and heart rate, has been proposed as a bedside risk-stratification marker. Its performance in routine emergency department care remains uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with septic shock treated with norepinephrine in the emergency department from 2023 to 2025. The index time was the first protocolized invasive hemodynamic assessment after norepinephrine initiation. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality. Logistic regression evaluated the association between VNERi and mortality, adjusting for age, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, Charlson comorbidity index, and serum lactate. Discrimination was compared with that of the mean arterial pressure-to-norepinephrine dose ratio (MAP/NE) using paired receiver operating characteristic curves. Non-linearity was assessed using restricted cubic splines. The previously reported value of 6.7 and a cohort-specific cutoff derived using the Youden index were explored.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 238 patients, 70 experienced 28-day in-hospital mortality. Median age was 72 years, 52.9% were female, median Charlson comorbidity index was 4, and mean Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 7.4. Each 1-unit increase in VNERi was independently associated with lower odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.79-0.91). VNERi showed modestly greater discrimination than MAP/NE (AUROC, 0.737 [95% CI, 0.675-0.799] vs. 0.667 [95% CI, 0.592-0.742]; p = 0.012). The spline model fit better than the linear specification (p = 0.014). Mortality was 48.0% with VNERi <6.7 and 8.8% with VNERi ≥6.7. The cohort-specific cutoff of 7.6 provided only a marginally higher Youden index than 6.7 (0.475 vs. 0.470).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Lower VNERi was independently associated with higher 28-day in-hospital mortality and showed modestly greater discrimination than MAP/NE. Prospective multicenter validation using standardized measurement timing and external validation of candidate thresholds are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Shoulder anterior capsular (SHAC) block for analgesia in anterior shoulder dislocation: An emergency department case series.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Anterior shoulder dislocation is among the most common major joint dislocations presenting to the emergency department (ED) and is frequently managed with procedural sedation. Several analgesic and regional anesthesia strategies are available for shoulder reduction, each with distinct advantages and limitations. The Shoulder Anterior Capsular (SHAC) block is a superficial, ultrasound-guided interfascial plane technique that targets pericapsular nerve contributions to the glenohumeral joint via an anterior approach, offering a potentially motor-sparing and sedation-sparing alternative.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: We present two cases of ED anterior shoulder dislocation managed with the SHAC block at a high-volume Level 1 trauma center. In the first case, a 60-year-old male with recurrent dislocation underwent successful reduction without procedural sedation, reporting it as his least painful reduction among multiple prior experiences. In the second case, a 94-year-old female with a complex fracture-dislocation in cervical spine precautions received the SHAC block as an analgesic adjunct; although procedural sedation was ultimately required, the patient required no intravenous analgesia during a subsequent 36-h observation period. In both cases, the block was performed by an emergency medicine intern under supervision by a Pain Medicine fellowship-trained attending physician, preserving the ability to conduct post-reduction axillary nerve assessment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The SHAC block was technically feasible in two selected patients with anterior shoulder dislocation and provided variable analgesia. Further study is needed to evaluate its efficacy, safety, positioning requirements, reproducibility, and appropriate patient selection.

articles.title: Use of an Electronic Health Record Algorithm to Identify Persons With Human Immunodeficiency Virus Out Of Care in United States Emergency Departments.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) screening programs are designed primarily to identify persons with undiagnosed HIV and, therefore, systematically exclude persons with diagnosed HIV (PWHDx). PWHDx who are out of care (OOC) contribute disproportionately to HIV transmission and are a priority population within Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) initiatives. Because PWHDx OOC are not routinely identified through screening, complementary strategies are needed to support re-engagement in care. We evaluated an electronic health record algorithm (EHRa) designed to identify PWHDx presenting to the ED. We then determined HIV care status, characterized differences between patients in care (IC) and OOC, and quantified the incremental yield of EHRa-based identification beyond routine HIV screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional study across 3 EDs with universal HIV screening. Adults (≥18 years) presenting between February and July 2024 who screened HIV positive or were identified through the EHRa were included. Data from HIV screening databases and EHRa reports were analyzed using descriptive statistics and logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 88,501 adult ED visits, 798 persons with HIV were identified (0.9%): 5.1% newly diagnosed, 21.6% PWHDx OOC, and 73.3% PWHDx IC. The EHRa identified 589 PWHDx who were not captured through routine screening, including 113 (19.2%) who were OOC. Compared with IC patients, PWHDx OOC had higher AIDS prevalence (37.5% vs 18.6%) and lower viral suppression (17.6% vs 83.3%). OOC status was independently associated with cisgender female gender, housing instability, limited phone access, and being uninsured.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A simple, locally generated EHRa substantially increased identification of PWHDx in the ED, including many OOC patients who were not captured through routine screening. A simple, locally generated EHRa demonstrated substantial incremental yield for identifying PWHDx in the ED, including many OOC patients who were not captured through routine screening. EHR-based identification strategies may help identify and re-engage PWHDx OOC and support national EHE goals.

articles.title: Impact of social determinants of health on perioperative and interstage outcomes in congenital heart surgery a systematic review.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Social determinants of health (SDoH)- conditions in which patients live, grow, and age,-are increasingly recognized to influence the health of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To explore the impact of SDoH on short-term mortality and morbidity, interstage outcomes, and resource utilization, among patients following congenital heart surgery.

abstract.label: EVIDENCE REVIEW
abstract.text: A systematic review was completed according to PRISMA guidelines. Relevant studies evaluating the association of SDoH with surgical outcomes of pediatric and adult CHD patients were identified from five databases queried including PubMed, SCOPUS, CINAHL, PYSCINFO, and Cochrane between January 1999 and February 2024. Inclusion criteria incorporated prior systematic reviews and meta-analyses, secondary analyses of prospectively collected trial data, and prospective or retrospective cohort studies. Subsequent reference searches identified 39 related articles. SDoH included patient and neighborhood level metrics. Two independent reviewers screened studies for full-text review, with data extraction by an expert panel.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: Among 1,224 studies identified, 157 articles underwent full-text review and 121 were ultimately selected for data extraction. Eighty-Five articles did not address acute postoperative outcomes and were excluded. Thirty-six studies focused on acute or interstage outcomes following congenital heart surgery and served as the source information. The remainder were retrospective cohort studies using various databases. The number of study participants ranged from 98 to 174,352 (median = 6,979). Factors found to be linked with greater likelihood of in-hospital mortality included Black race, Hispanic/Latino ethnicity, Medicaid insurance, and lower neighborhood socioeconomic status. Both individual and neighborhood level determinants were associated with longer interstage periods, higher complication rates, as well as greater resource utilization and hospital readmissions. Two critical timespans for intervention to reduce inequities in care were the neonatal period and young adulthood.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: SDoH impact both acute and interstage outcomes in patients following surgery for CHD. Developing interventions to increase access to and engagement with quality care and out-of-hospital support may improve both short-term outcomes and reduce systems-level financial burden. Systematic Review Registration.

articles.title: Designing evaluation infrastructure for psychedelic harm reduction at events: a methodological framework with formative mixed-methods field application.

abstract.text: Psychedelic and other psychoactive substance use is increasing in non-clinical environments, including music festivals, concerts, and other large-scale gatherings. As psychedelic use expands beyond clinical settings, policymakers, healthcare systems, event operators, and researchers require evidence-informed frameworks for understanding and responding to psychoactive-related distress in naturalistic environments. Despite the growing presence of psychedelic harm reduction services, few studies have established reproducible methods for documenting their operation, coordination with event-health services, or role within triage and escalation pathways in naturalistic settings. This methodological paper proposes an evaluation framework for psychedelic harm reduction services and reports a formative mixed-methods field application involving the Zendo Project at two large-scale events. Nineteen pre-event surveys, five retained post-event surveys, and two matched pre/post records were obtained from medical personnel. Quantitative responses were summarized descriptively, while open-ended responses were used formatively to contextualize and refine the proposed measurement domains. The framework positions psychedelic peer support as a complementary intermediate pathway for medically stable but psychologically distressed individuals, operating alongside rather than in place of medical and public-safety services. The field application identified interpretable measurement domains concerning psychological-distress burden, preparedness, workload, safety, interprofessional coordination, escalation, and attendee disposition. Four respondents completed several principal post-event items and reported favorable perceptions of Zendo's operational role. These responses represent staff perceptions and counterfactual estimates rather than independently verified effects. Beyond evaluating a single intervention, this study offers an initial framework for measuring and comparing non-clinical psychedelic support models and for informing future research, policy development, and event-health infrastructure as psychedelic use continues to expand beyond clinical settings. Additionally, by translating field-based psychedelic support into measurable operational, public health, and economic outcomes, the proposed methodology offers a foundation for the future evaluation, comparison, and development of products, services, and care infrastructures designed to support altered-state experiences in non-clinical environments.

articles.title: Healthcare providers' confidence, satisfaction, and perceived preparedness following a multicomponent simulation-based cardiopulmonary resuscitation training program in Gaza.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: High-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) requires not only technical competence but also confidence, effective teamwork, and psychological readiness among healthcare providers. Evidence regarding the impact of simulation-based CPR training on healthcare providers' confidence, satisfaction, and perceived preparedness remains limited in conflict-affected and resource-constrained settings.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess healthcare providers' self-confidence, satisfaction, and perceived preparedness following an intensive, multicomponent simulation-based CPR training program implemented among physicians and nurses working in governmental critical care facilities in Gaza.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a single-group evaluation of an intensive, 8-h multicomponent simulation-based CPR training program delivered to 100 healthcare providers (50 physicians, 50 nurses) working in emergency rooms, intensive care units, and coronary care units at Al-Shifa Medical Complex, Gaza, between August and December 2022, aligned with the 2020 American Heart Association Guidelines. Participants were recruited using purposive, non-probability sampling of all eligible clinical staff in these units. Self-reported confidence in CPR-related competencies was assessed before and after the intervention using identical questionnaire items; satisfaction and perceived preparedness were assessed only after the intervention. Outcomes were measured on a structured, five-point Likert-scale questionnaire (Cronbach's α = 0.87), content-validated by an expert panel and refined through a pilot study, analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 26.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Participants reported very high satisfaction across all training domains, with instructor feedback usefulness rated highest (4.75 ± 0.39). Self-reported confidence increased markedly from pre- to post-training across all assessed domains: confidence in performing CPR rose from 2.91 ± 0.82 to 4.63 ± 0.51, airway management confidence from 2.85 ± 0.79 to 4.58 ± 0.54, and CPR team leadership confidence from 2.73 ± 0.88 to 4.49 ± 0.57. Most participants (92%) preferred simulation-based training over traditional lecture-based methods, and post-training perceived preparedness for real cardiac arrest situations was high (rapid response ability, 4.71 ± 0.40).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Multicomponent simulation-based CPR training was associated with marked improvement in healthcare providers' self-reported confidence, and was accompanied by high levels of post-training satisfaction and perceived emergency preparedness in a conflict-affected healthcare environment. Integrating structured simulation-based education into continuing professional development programs may strengthen emergency response capacity and workforce readiness in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Utility of Point-of-care Ultrasound in Clinical Care: A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has emerged as an essential bedside diagnostic tool in modern clinical practice. By enabling real-time visualization of anatomical structures and physiological processes, POCUS allows clinicians to rapidly evaluate patients and integrate imaging findings directly into clinical decision-making. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding the clinical utility of POCUS across both critical and noncritical care settings. Key applications include the use of structured ultrasound protocols during cardiac arrest, such as the US-CAB framework, and lung ultrasound approaches like the bedside lung ultrasound in emergency protocol for evaluating acute respiratory failure. In addition, growing evidence supports the use of POCUS in common emergency department presentations, including acute flank pain, nontraumatic abdominal pain, and undifferentiated chest pain or dyspnea. Across these clinical scenarios, POCUS has been shown to facilitate rapid diagnosis, reduce reliance on radiation-based imaging, and improve operational efficiency by shortening emergency department length of stay and expediting clinical decision-making. Despite its clinical advantages, the effective implementation of POCUS requires appropriate operator training and standardized protocols to ensure diagnostic reliability. Ongoing advances in portable ultrasound technology and image-analysis tools may further enhance the accessibility and clinical integration of POCUS in diverse healthcare environments. Overall, POCUS represents a valuable extension of bedside clinical assessment and continues to play an expanding role in modern patient-centered care.

articles.title: Point-of-care Ultrasound: Past, Present, and Future.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (PoCUS) has fundamentally transformed clinical practice from comprehensive, organ-based imaging into a rapid, goal-directed bedside tool. The development of standardized protocols - such as focused assessment with sonography for trauma, rapid ultrasound for shock and hypotension, and bedside lung ultrasound in emergency - along with real-time procedural guidance, has established PoCUS as an essential competency in critical care and emergency medicine. Currently, technological advancements have miniaturized ultrasound devices, dismantling geographical barriers and facilitating decentralized healthcare models. In the emergency department (ED), the early integration of PoCUS significantly reduces the ED length of stay and optimizes resource utilization, whereas its application continues to expand into general inpatient and community care. Looking forward, the democratization of medical education and the convergence of wireless technology with artificial intelligence will further minimize operator dependence. As its diagnostic value is firmly established, future research must pivot toward quantifying patient-centered outcomes, such as mortality and hospital readmission rates, solidifying PoCUS as an indispensable pillar of modern medicine.

articles.title: Prehospital Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma with 5G-enabled Real-time Telesupervision for the Early Detection of Intra-abdominal Hemorrhage and Trauma Team Activation: A Case Report and Feasibility Insight.

abstract.text: Prehospital ultrasound, particularly the Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (EFAST), has emerged as a valuable tool in the early identification of life-threatening conditions, including hemoperitoneum and pneumothorax. Current evidence supports the role of prehospital ultrasound in improving diagnostic accuracy, facilitating triage decisions, and enhancing communication with receiving trauma centers. However, its application in detecting intra-abdominal hemorrhage and expediting trauma team activation (TTA) remains underutilized in many emergency medical systems. This case highlights the critical importance of prehospital TTA in a patient with hemorrhagic shock secondary to blunt abdominal trauma. Rapid identification of hemoperitoneum via EFAST and immediate transmission of ultrasound findings enabled the timely mobilization of the trauma surgeon, interventional radiologist, and operating suite. Such integrated communication can significantly improve outcomes in patients with devastating hemorrhage by minimizing the time to definitive intervention.

articles.title: Admission point-of-care D-dimer for identifying haemostatic envenomation after snakebite: A prospective observational study.

abstract.text: Haemostatic envenomation (HE) - comprising venom-induced coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, and systemic bleeding - is the principal determinant of snakebite morbidity in South Asia. Conventional coagulation tests lack sensitivity for early haemostatic activation; D-dimer has been proposed as a rapid triage biomarker, but data from Indian emergency settings are lacking. We conducted a prospective diagnostic accuracy study (JMMC&RI, Thrissur, Kerala; March-December 2022; n = 96 consecutive snakebite patients). The primary aim was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of admission point of care D-dimer for identifying HE. Secondary aims were to compare its performance with standard coagulation tests and to evaluate it against the broader composite outcome - clinically significant envenomation (CSE). HE was defined as modified Lee-White clotting time (MLW) ≥15 min, failed 20-min whole-blood clotting test (20WBCT), INR ≥1.4, fibrinogen <100 mg/dL, platelet count <100 × 109/L, or systemic haemotoxic bleeding. Comparators were MLW/20WBCT, prothrombin time, INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, and platelet count. Thirty-three patients (34.4%) met HE criteria. At the Youden-optimal threshold of 620 ng/mL, D-dimer achieved sensitivity 87.9% (95% CI: 72.7-95.2%), specificity 79.0% (67.4-87.3%), PPV 69.0% (54.0-80.9%), NPV 92.5% (82.1-97.0%), LR+ 4.19, LR- 0.153, and accuracy 82.1% (73.2-88.5%). AUC was 0.874 (0.791-0.957) - highest among all comparators: MLW 0.763, WBCT 0.652, aPTT 0.544, fibrinogen 0.728, platelet count 0.681, INR 0.646, and PT 0.615. D-dimer ≥620 ng/mL was the strongest independent predictor of HE (OR 22.04; 95% CI: 6.13-79.25; p < 0.001). Three of four patients with delayed coagulopathy had D-dimer ≥620 ng/mL at admission. Against the broader clinically significant envenomation (CSE) endpoint (n = 52, 54.2%), AUC was 0.885 (0.816-0.954) at 139 ng/mL (sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 81.8%). Admission D-dimer demonstrated higher discriminatory performance for HE than all standard coagulation comparators. Its NPV of 92.5% supports potential utility as a rapid rule-out biomarker. These findings are exploratory and require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Dental Advanced Life Support (DALS) in Korea: development, current practice, and future perspectives.
articles.journal_full: Journal of dental anesthesia and pain medicine

articles.title: Medical Encounters During the 2026 AETF European Taekwon-Do Championships: A Five-Day Retrospective Descriptive Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Injury surveillance is essential in combat sports, but recorded medical encounters may depend on assessment thresholds, competition regulations, and ringside medical organization. This study characterized medical encounters requiring assessment by the competition medical team during a five-day European Taekwon-do competition according to their number, operational severity, anatomical location, and impact on continued participation. Methods: A retrospective descriptive analysis was conducted based on 242 recorded medical encounters collected over five consecutive days of competition. The individual medical encounter served as the unit of analysis. Data were collected using a hybrid paper- and digital-based reporting system. Variables included competition day, location, medical-encounter category, operational severity classification, ability to continue competition, hospital referral, ambulance transport, and clinical description. Results: A total of 242 medical encounters were recorded: 58 on Day 1, 75 on Day 2, 18 on Day 3, 30 on Day 4, and 61 on Day 5. Most recorded medical encounters were classified as minor (239/242; 98.8%), while three were classified as moderate (1.2%). The most frequently recorded medical-encounter categories were head (83/242; 34.3%), abdomen (34/242; 14%), knee (21/242; 8.7%), and ankle (17/242; 7%). Most medical encounters were associated with continued participation (230/242; 95%). Hospital referral occurred in two cases, including one ambulance transfer. The number of recorded medical encounters decreased markedly after Day 2, coinciding with a change in the operational threshold for medical assessment of very minor problems. Conclusions: The number and characteristics of recorded medical encounters varied across the competition, with the observed patterns also reflecting competition procedures and reporting practices. The hybrid paper- and digital-based system provided a pragmatic approach to competition medical surveillance, while standardized definitions, consistent assessment procedures, and reliable digital infrastructure are needed. Future studies should incorporate athlete-exposure and bout-level data to enable valid exposure-adjusted injury incidence comparisons.

articles.title: Insomnia Severity and Its Demographic and Health-Related Correlates Among Paramedic Students in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.text: Background: Sleep disturbances among healthcare students can negatively affect academic performance and future clinical decision-making. However, limited evidence exists on insomnia among Emergency Medical Services (EMS) students, a group exposed to unique academic and operational stressors. This study assessed insomnia severity and its demographic and health-related correlates among paramedic students in Saudi Arabia. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 238 EMS students in Saudi Arabia. Insomnia severity was assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Descriptive statistics summarized insomnia levels, and bivariate tests and multiple linear regression were used to examine group differences and predictors in SPSS. Results: The mean ISI score was 11.8 ± 5.3, indicating subthreshold insomnia among paramedic students.
