Recognizing this reversible yet potentially fatal condition is crucial, as prompt initiation of antithyroid therapy and vasodilators can rapidly alleviate ischaemia and reduce the risk of recurrence. The favourable outcome in this patient illustrates how early identification of the underlying cause can guide swift and effective management.

articles.title: Massive Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding in an Adolescent Patient: A Case Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding in pediatric patients arises from diverse etiologies that vary across age groups. Although it is an uncommon cause of life-threatening hemorrhagic shock, prompt recognition and management are essential. Owing to the infrequency of hemorrhagic shock from GI bleeding in pediatrics, emergency physicians may lack familiarity with its diagnosis and management. Furthermore, multiple etiologies may coexist and may not be detected during the initial esophagogastroduodenoscopy, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure.

abstract.label: CASE REPORT
abstract.text: A 17-year-old boy with a history of plaque psoriasis was transported by ambulance to the pediatric emergency department of an urban level one trauma center, presenting with copious hematemesis and hemodynamic instability. Initial resuscitation in the emergency department included blood transfusion, followed by admission to the pediatric intensive care unit. The first endoscopic evaluation by pediatric gastroenterology identified duodenal erosion; however, the patient experienced further large-volume bleeding out of proportion to these findings. A subsequent endoscopy revealed a Dieulafoy lesion, which was treated successfully. The patient was ultimately discharged home and has remained stable during long-term follow-up. WHY SHOULD AN EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN BE AWARE OF THIS?: Although severe GI bleeding in pediatric patients is uncommon, emergency physicians must quickly identify hemorrhagic shock across all age groups and be familiar with the broad differential diagnoses that vary by age. Initial management must prioritize airway protection and hemodynamic stabilization as a bridge to definitive intervention. Clinicians should recognize the limitations of endoscopic gastroduodenoscopy and consider the potential for concurrent sources of bleeding that may necessitate additional intervention. © 2025 Elsevier Inc. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, artificial intelligence training, and similar technologies.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Video-Oculography for Acute Vertigo and Dizziness.

abstract.text: In this article, we review studies that bring video-oculography (VOG) to the emergency department and inpatient settings, with an emphasis on acute vestibular syndrome. We find that most current studies are research-based, rather than pilot clinical programs. Many focus on the use of VOG to differentiate central disorders (eg, ischemic stroke) from peripheral (eg, inner ear) mimics. We critically appraise the classes of eye movements studied by each, and then provide an update on recent work in leveraging artificial intelligence, telemedicine, and the use of consumer devices and smartphones for VOG-applications, to expand reach and improve vestibular diagnosis.

articles.title: Emergency Televestibular Diagnosis: Case Studies from Around the Globe.

abstract.text: This article reviews established televestibular models from United States, Germany, and Australia. These services share core elements such as standardized history, targeted vestibular examinations, and remote expert interpretation. By extending neuro-otology expertise across multiple hospitals, they enhance equity and scalability while reducing unnecessary imaging, admissions, and missed strokes. Differences include operator training, technology requirements, and the professional background of the neuro-otology expert. Implementation challenges include sustaining workforce training, information technology (IT) integration, workflow adaptation, and funding gaps. This review provides practical insights into the workflows and resources required for emergency department televestibular models and highlights their potential to deliver meaningful system-level benefits.

articles.title: Early serial changes in FIB-4 after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and short-term clinical outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index combines age, aminotransferase levels, and platelet count. Although developed for chronic liver fibrosis, its components may reflect acute hepatic and systemic injury after cardiac arrest. The primary aim of this study was to characterize early changes in FIB-4 from admission to an approximately 72-hour repeat assessment after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Secondarily, we evaluated the association of FIB-4 values with 28-day mortality and whether repeat measurement provided additional prognostic information.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to the intensive care unit after sustained return of spontaneous circulation between May 1, 2023, and May 1, 2026. After a record-level eligibility audit, 188 patients were included; 28-day vital status was available for 182. FIB-4 was calculated from the first laboratory set obtained at intensive care unit admission and from the complete laboratory set closest to 72 h after the admission laboratory sample within a 48-96-hour window. The primary analysis assessed paired change in FIB-4. Secondary analyses examined the association of admission FIB-4 with 28-day mortality and, using a 72-hour landmark approach, the association of repeat FIB-4 with subsequent mortality through day 28 and its incremental contribution beyond the admission value.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A valid repeat FIB-4 measurement was available in 122 patients. In paired analysis, median FIB-4 decreased from 5.21 at admission to 3.16 at approximately 72 h (p < 0.001). Of the 182 patients with known 28-day vital status, 82 died (45.1%). Admission FIB-4 was higher in patients who died than in survivors (6.84 [3.25-10.75] vs. 4.14 [2.32-8.16]; p = 0.019). Each doubling of admission FIB-4 was associated with higher odds of mortality in the unadjusted analysis (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.02-1.55; p = 0.029); however, in the OHCA-specific complete-case model, the adjusted association was not statistically significant (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.91-1.46; p = 0.227), and adding FIB-4 to the clinical model increased the AUC only from 0.647 to 0.648 (difference, 0.001). In the 72-hour landmark cohort, 56 patients had an available pre-landmark repeat measurement and known 28-day vital status; 29 died after the landmark. Repeat FIB-4 showed weak discrimination for subsequent mortality (AUC, 0.585), and the OR per doubling was 1.23 (95% CI, 0.86-1.76; p = 0.255). Adding repeat FIB-4 to the admission value increased the AUC from 0.575 to 0.581 (difference, 0.006; 95% CI, - 0.053 to 0.205; likelihood-ratio p = 0.294).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients with available paired measurements, FIB-4 decreased from admission to the approximately 72-hour repeat assessment; however, the magnitude of change showed little discriminatory ability for subsequent mortality in the landmark cohort. Higher admission FIB-4 was associated with mortality in the unadjusted analysis, but this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for major OHCA-specific prognostic factors, and FIB-4 provided essentially no incremental discrimination when added to the clinical model. The incremental prognostic contribution of repeat measurement remained uncertain because of the limited landmark sample and imprecise estimates. FIB-4 should be regarded as a research marker of the acute systemic and hepatic response after cardiac arrest rather than as a stand-alone clinical prediction tool.

articles.title: Rural Health and Atypical Stroke: Technology-Based Posterior Circulation Stroke Diagnosis.

abstract.text: Diagnostic errors cause an estimated 900,000 deaths and disabilities annually in the United States, and stroke is the leading cause of diagnostic error-related harm in US emergency departments. Posterior circulation strokes (PCS's) are frequently misdiagnosed due to atypical presentations such as dizziness. Key contributors to rural-urban care gaps in PCS diagnosis are highlighted for rural care (eg, challenges in bedside diagnosis and limited access to neurologists). Emerging technologies (eg, telestroke, video-oculography-based teledizzy programs, mobile stroke units, and smartphone tools) can improve diagnostic access, timeliness and accuracy for patients living in rural communities.

articles.title: [Tsutsugamushi disease with left heart failure as the main manifestation complicated by multiple organ dysfunction: a case report and literature review].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Wei Zhong Bing Ji Jiu Yi Xue
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue

abstract.text: Tsutsugamushi disease (TD) is a zoonotic and naturally focal infectious disease caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi (Ot), transmitted between humans and rodents through the bite of chigger mites. On August 17, 2025, a patient with TD complicated by acute left sided heart failure and multiple organ dysfunction was admitted to Wuhan Jinyintan Hospital. The patient presented to the emergency department with a 10 day history of fever, palpitations, dyspnea, and cough, and had a history of outdoor exposure. Physical examination revealed a temperature of 39.2 centigrade, a heart rate of 79 beats/min (showing relative bradycardia), an eschar of 0.5 cm×0.6 cm at the intersection of the right mid axillary line and the umbilical horizontal line, and a truncal rash. Laboratory findings showed an eosinophil count of 0, troponin T 1.31 μg/L, N terminal pro B type natriuretic peptide 2 912.60 ng/L, and elevated procalcitonin. Electrocardiography revealed prolonged Q T and Q Tc intervals, and chest CT demonstrated bilateral interstitial pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusion. Next generation sequencing of blood detected Ot nucleic acid fragments, and serum Ot immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody was positive, confirming the diagnosis of TD complicated by myocarditis, acute left sided heart failure, and multiple organ dysfunction. The patient was treated with doxycycline combined with rifampicin for anti infection, along with symptomatic and supportive care, as well as local interventions including thoracentesis drainage and bronchoalveolar lavage. Subsequently, the patient's body temperature normalized, cardiac function improved, pulmonary edema and pleural effusion resolved, and myocardial enzymes returned to normal levels; the patient was discharged with clinical cure. This case indicates that TD can affect the cardiovascular system, presenting as acute left sided heart failure and myocarditis. For patients with fever, relative bradycardia, and multiple organ dysfunction, TD should be considered in the differential diagnosis, and early recognition of the eschar together with prompt initiation of etiological therapy are crucial for improving prognosis.

articles.title: Q-LEASE: Lifecycle-bound zero-trust authorization for HPC-to-QPU job handoffs.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Zero-Trust access control for cloud APIs is well established, but hybrid High-Performance Computing (HPC)-to-Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) workflows have a lifecycle existing mechanisms were not built for: a job queues for minutes to days, is dispatched, executes, and only then releases results, while identity, policy, and hardware calibration state can change throughout. Existing token, proof-of-possession, and workload-identity mechanisms do not separate permission to queue from permission to execute, nor bind authorization to current hardware state.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We designed and implemented Q-LEASE, a two-capability protocol separating a Queue Admission Ticket from a single-use Execution Capability bound to a circuit hash, backend identity, and calibration epoch, re-evaluated by a real Open Policy Agent (OPA) engine immediately before dispatch. The prototype uses real Ed25519/PASETO tokens, DPoP-style proof-of-possession, SPIFFE-shaped workload identity, and a phase-aware revocation state machine, deployed as six containerised services on a Kubernetes ( kind) cluster with Kueue-driven queueing. We compared Q-LEASE against four representative baselines across 16 attack/failure scenarios (2400 attack trials, 500 clean trials), and verified core safety properties with TLA+/TLC and token-flow security with the Tamarin prover.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Q-LEASE blocked 90.0% of unauthorized-execution attempts (95% confidence interval (CI) 87.0-92.4%), versus 12.5-37.9% for the four baselines. The remaining gap came from queue/execution separation and circuit/backend/calibration-epoch binding, which no baseline implements. Both TLA+ safety properties held, and all five Tamarin lemmas were proved automatically. Q-LEASE's mean policy-decision latency was 44.3 ms, approximately 34.4 ms higher than the baselines, with no measurable increase in end-to-end workflow completion time relative to a real, contention-driven queue wait, while running against a real Kueue-admitted workload on a real cluster.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Separating queue admission from execution authorization, and binding it to hardware state re-checked immediately before dispatch, closes a gap that composing existing OAuth-family mechanisms does not, at a latency cost small relative to realistic QPU queue waits.

articles.title: Palliative, end-of-life care for the burn-injured patient.
articles.journal_full: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

abstract.text: This review seeks to describe end-of-life trajectories in burns patients, and a holistic approach to care which encompasses the patient, the family and the health care professionals who care for them. It includes relevant considerations in determining the indications for end-of-life care rather than active treatment aimed at cure. Care for the dying burns patient is described in emergency department, intensive care and ward settings. Inclusive communication to ensure appropriate and consensus-based decision-making which is supported by the treating team, patient and family is paramount in developing a shared understanding of the aims of required interventions. Checklists and guidelines support these aims, and examples are provided, along with details of practical challenges in care delivery. The importance of an established pathway to offer organ donation to burns patients with unsurvivable injuries is highlighted, and outcomes from our institution are reported.

articles.title: Burn injury management by Dutch physician-staffed HEMS: Findings from the HEMS-BURNS cohort and National Trauma Registry.
articles.journal_full: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Dutch Physician staffed Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (P-HEMS) are regularly dispatched to provide care to patients with burns on scene. It is unclear if and which patients with burns benefit from P-HEMS care. This study aimed to investigate P-HEMS dispatch and cancellation rates, intervention rates, and patient outcomes in burn care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a descriptive retrospective cohort study. Databases of the Rotterdam P-HEMS and the Dutch National Trauma Registry (NTR) were consulted for burn cases between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2023. Data on cancellation, patient characteristics, burn severity and type, prehospital treatment, transportation, treatment times, and mortality were collected and analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Rotterdam P-HEMS was dispatched 976 times for suspected burn injuries, with 455 (46.6%) dispatches being cancelled, mainly due to minor injuries (n = 288; 63.3%). Of 521 non-cancelled dispatches, most involved adults (n = 345; 66.2%) and flame burns (n = 248; 59.6%), while pediatric patients mostly had scald burns (n = 123; 81.5%). P-HEMS specific interventions were performed in 33.6% of non-cancelled dispatches, with a significantly lower rate in children than in adults (14.2% vs 43.5%; p < 0.001) and a significantly lower rate for scald burns than for flame burns (14.6% vs 45.6%; p < 0.001). Of 879 patients with burns with HEMS involvement recorded in the NTR, median Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 9 (P25-P75 1-25), median hospital length of stay (HLOS) was 5 days (P25-P75 2-21 days), ICU admission occurred in 465 of 879 cases (52.9%), and in-hospital mortality was 13.7% (n = 120).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study found that 46.6% of P-HEMS dispatches for patients with burns were cancelled, often due to minor injuries. P-HEMS-specific interventions were performed in 33.6% of non-cancelled dispatches. These findings suggest a need to optimize dispatch criteria to reduce overtriage and improve efficiency of P-HEMS dispatch for burn care.

articles.title: Calf Injuries: Anatomy, Pathology, and Treatment.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons

abstract.text: Calf injuries are common in athletes and typically result in missed time from sport and activities of daily living. The three individual triceps surae muscles can be injured, with differing described mechanisms. Gastrocnemius or plantaris strains tend to occur during sudden explosive movement of the ankle from a dorsiflexed to a plantarflexed position with the knee in extension. Soleus strains typically occur from repetitive dorsiflexion of the ankle with the knee flexed. Imaging modalities such as magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasonography can be helpful in determining the location and grade of injury, which can aid in treatment and return to play timelines. Classically, these injuries have been graded as grade I, II, or III, with grade I having <10% muscle fiber disruption, grade II having >10 to 50% muscle fiber disruption, and grade III having 50 to 100% muscle fiber disruption. The mainstay of treatment for most calf strains is nonsurgical, with surgical management being rare but reported in the literature for isolated grade III ruptures of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Return to sport and activities requires a graduated physical therapy program focused on restoring tissue length without excessive strain. Recent limited evidence has shown promising results with quicker return to activities and decreased pain with platelet-rich plasma injections.

articles.title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on breast cancer care in Romania: a cohort analysis from the Oncological Institute of Bucharest.

abstract.text: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic profoundly disrupted healthcare systems worldwide, raising concerns regarding delays in cancer diagnosis and treatment. How these disruptions affected breast cancer care during and after the pandemic remains incompletely understood, particularly in Eastern European oncology centers. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of newly diagnosed breast cancer cases treated at the Oncological Institute of Bucharest (IOB), comparing a pandemic cohort (n = 73) with a post-pandemic cohort (n = 99) with respect to age at diagnosis, tumor laterality, location, stage, grade, receptor subtype, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status, and intervals across the diagnostic and treatment pathways. We measured the intervals between: General Practitioner (GP) referral and the patient's first presentation to the surgery unit; imaging diagnosis (ultrasound, mammogram, or MRI) and the date of biopsy or surgery; biopsy result and initiation of neoadjuvant treatment; the end of neoadjuvant treatment and surgery; surgery and adjuvant treatment; and consecutive chemotherapy sessions. Between the two cohorts, the median age was similar (56 [47-67] vs. 59 [50-68] years). Similarities were also found in tumor laterality and quadrant location. In the post-pandemic cohort, 31.3% of patients were diagnosed with advanced-stage disease, compared with 20.5% in the pandemic cohort, although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Our study showed that chemotherapy delivery was more efficient post-pandemic, with shorter intervals between treatment sessions (18 [17-19] vs. 21 [21-22] days). Referral-to-presentation times were also shorter post-pandemic (3 [1-8] vs. 6 [2-10] days). In contrast, during the post-pandemic year, the interval between the end of neoadjuvant therapy and surgery remained prolonged. During the COVID-19 pandemic, breast cancer care at a major Romanian oncology center was preserved through adapted clinical pathways. We also found that delays in surgical treatment occurred in the post-pandemic period, and a higher percentage of advanced-stage cases were diagnosed. Our findings suggest that pre-hospital delays and residual system constraints, rather than deficiencies in oncology care, contributed to stage migration in the post-pandemic group.

articles.title: "It's Scary, but I Handle It": A Qualitative Study on Severe Hypoglycemia Experiences and Reasons for Declining to Participate in a Community Paramedicine Trial to Prevent Hypoglycemia Among People With Diabetes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Severe (level 3) hypoglycemia is a life-threatening complication of diabetes associated with substantial risk of recurrence and long-term morbidity. This study examined how adults with diabetes interpreted severe hypoglycemic events and why they declined participation in a community paramedicine program (Diabetes Rescue, Engagement, and Management [Diabetes-REM]) designed to prevent recurrence.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted semistructured qualitative interviews with adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who experienced severe hypoglycemia requiring emergency medical services and declined enrollment in Diabetes-REM. Interviews explored hypoglycemia management experiences and reasons for nonparticipation and were explored using thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixteen adults (44% female; mean age 60 years, range 25-83) participated. Four interrelated themes emerged. First, participants normalized glucose variability as a baseline condition of diabetes and interpreted severe events as situational and correctable when a cause was identifiable, or as inevitable when it was not, rather than as evidence of increased risk. Second, participants relied on prevention systems encompassing habitual routines, caregiver involvement, and glucose-monitoring technologies. Third, severe episodes were frightening and disruptive but typically prompted adjustments to personal management over pursuit of additional clinical support. Finally, reasons for declining Diabetes-REM included time constraints (56%), perceived lack of benefit (25%), and privacy concerns or discomfort with home visits (25%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among adults who declined a community paramedicine hypoglycemia prevention intervention, severe events were absorbed into existing self-management frameworks rather than viewed as signals of increased risk. Programs targeting hypoglycemia recurrence should account for patients' risk perceptions and existing management systems, positioning support as complementary rather than corrective.

articles.title: Online clinical readiness course enhanced knowledge and perceived confidence of trainees during the COVID-19 pandemic.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education globally. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the International Emergency Medicine Education Project's online COVID-19 Clinical Readiness Course in enhancing participants' knowledge and perceived confidence in managing COVID-19.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a prospective, mixed-methods study. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-course assessments and surveys, while qualitative feedback was gathered via open-ended responses at the end of the course. Non-parametric tests were used for statistical comparisons, and thematic analysis of qualitative data was performed using customized large language model tools with human review and triangulation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 703 participants from 72 countries enrolled, 644 (91.6%) completed the knowledge assessments, and 510 (72.5%) completed the exit surveys. The majority (77.2%) were medical trainees, and 51.4% were from low- and lower-middle-income countries. The median score increased from 60 to 92 (p < 0.001) post-course. Perceived confidence in managing key clinical scenarios, including hypoxia, early symptoms, airway problems, sepsis, and cardiac arrest, also increased significantly (p < 0.001). Participants reported that the course met their expectations, with a median (IQR) score of 9 (8-10). Qualitative feedback revealed high satisfaction and highlighted areas for improvement.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The online Clinical Readiness Course significantly improved knowledge and perceived confidence in COVID-19 management among medical trainees worldwide. Scalable online education may help address training gaps during public health emergencies and support global medical education.

articles.title: Evaluation of Effective Factors in the Prognosis of Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Transferred by Emergency Medical Services and Self-Referred Patients in Tehran.
articles.journal_full: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Little is known about the current scenario of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) under primary angioplasty; Transferred by emergency medical services and self-referred patients in Iran.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study population consisted of AMI patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who were consecutively admitted with Emergency Medical Services (EMS) or directly in the first six months of 2021 in 2 PCI-capable selected hospitals in Tehran. We analyzed the pattern of transfer by emergency medical services and compared in-hospital treatments and outcomes between transferred patients and self-referred patients in Tehran. Statistical comparisons were performed using chi‑square, t‑tests, or Mann-Whitney U tests, and multivariable logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with in‑hospital mortality, with significance set at P<0.05.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In-hospital mortality was higher in the self-referred than in patients transferred by EMS (9.8% versus 5.2%) (P=0.014). The average door-to-balloon (DTB) time in the self-referred patients was significantly higher (60.26±59.0 minutes vs 49.30±48.82 minutes) (P=0.020). Results show that the average DTB time of patients who died in the hospital was higher than that of patients who were alive in the self-referred patients. The average time from pain onset to Balloon (OTB) in the self-referred patients and those transferred by EMS was 348.74±316.07 minutes and 226.26±183.15 minutes, respectively (P<0.001). Multivariable logistic regression models the chance of in-hospital mortality in patients who self-referred is 2.17 times that of patients who were transferred by EMS, which is statistically significant (P=0.008).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our results indicated that there are significant differences in treatment delay and use of early revascularization, such as time of first medical contact (FMC) to the device, time of pain onset to Balloon (OTB), and DTB time between transferred-by-EMS patients and self-referred patients.

articles.title: Mortality Outcomes Following Pediatric Emergency Department Visits: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal_full: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments with high readiness to admit children may reduce mortality rates, but comprehensive and comparative evidence is limited. This study is the first systematic review and meta-analysis conducted to determine the effect of pediatric emergency department readiness on in-hospital mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A search for relevant articles was conducted up to 17 December 2025 in the international databases PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Relevant keywords were used for the search. Current study question: In children presenting to emergency departments (Population), how is the level of emergency readiness for pediatric care (Exposure) associated with mortality (Outcome)? This section was created using the PICO approach. Data analyses were conducted using the meta-analysis packages in STATA/MP.v17 (College Station, Texas, USA).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The overall in-hospital mortality rate was estimated to be about 2%. Meta-analysis showed that care at highest-readiness EDs (Quartile 4 wPRS) was associated with a significant reduction in mortality (OR=0.617; 95% CI, 0.491-0.744).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Increasing the level of emergency department pediatric readiness can be associated with a reduction in in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the importance of policy to improve standards of pediatric emergency readiness in all hospitals.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Pain Assessment Tools in Prehospital Emergency Care: Evidence from Observational Studies.
articles.journal_full: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In the prehospital setting, pain assessment and documentation are often insufficient due to time constraints and high workload. Although validated tools such as the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), and Verbal Rating Scale (VRS) exist for rapid pain assessment, their use in emergency medical services (EMS) remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases was performed for observational studies conducted in prehospital emergency settings, including both trauma and mixed patient populations reporting pain assessment practices.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 1,834 identified articles, 8 studies in which pain intensity was measured using standard instruments such as NRS, VAS, or VRS were eligible for inclusion. The results showed that the documentation and assessment of pain in the prehospital setting were performed in only 22.5% to 46.7% of patients, indicating a generally low frequency of pain evaluation before hospital admission. Across the included observational studies, EMS-related pain management interventions were reported to be associated with reductions in pain intensity; however, due to methodological heterogeneity and the absence of quantitative synthesis, the magnitude of these changes could not be reliably estimated.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pain recording and assessment in the prehospital setting are below recommended standards, and only a limited proportion of patients are systematically monitored. This deficiency can lead to inadequate decision-making in pain management. Strengthening the training of EMS personnel for recording pain is essential to improve the quality of care.

articles.title: Epidemiological Insights into Xenobiotic-Induced Seizures: A Correlational Descriptive Study from a Poisoning Referral Center in Northwestern Iran.
articles.journal_full: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Seizure is a common complication of poisoning caused by toxins and various drugs. Epidemiological insights into xenobiotic-induced seizures enable emergency physicians to anticipate seizure risk during toxic exposures, optimize triage decisions, and tailor strategies. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiological characteristics and essential factors related to xenobiotic-induced seizures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 122 patients who developed seizures following poisoning with drugs, alcohol, opioids, pesticides, or stimulants between July 2021 and June 2022. Sociodemographic profiles and details of the poisoning/ toxic agents were collected through bedside interviews. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics with SPSS version 21.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The majority of patients were men (110, 90.2%), with a mean age of 30.5 ± 11.99 years; 61 (50%) were married, and 95 (77.9%) resided in urban areas. Suicidal poisoning was the most frequent cause (62 cases, 50.8%), followed by poisoning related to substance abuse (33 cases, 27%). Opioids particularly tramadol (75 cases, 61.5%) were the leading cause of xenobiotic-induced seizures. All patients experienced generalized tonic-clonic seizures, with 87 (71.3%) having a single episode. Significant gender and occupation-based differences were observed: suicidal poisoning was more common among women, whereas substance abuse predominated among men. Education level was also found to influence the type of poisoning agent.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Xenobiotic-induced seizures are predominantly associated with opioid poisoning, are prevalent among young males with suicidal tendencies and substance abuse. These findings highlight the need for targeted preventive strategies, early identification of at-risk individuals, and improved management protocols for poisoning-related seizures.

articles.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy in Hospital Emergency Departments: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal_full: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments face challenges of overcrowding and human error. This systematic review evaluates the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving triage and diagnostic accuracy in emergency settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review was conducted by searching PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar until September 2025. Inclusion criteria comprised original studies reporting at least one quantitative performance metric. Study quality was assessed using NOS and QUADAS-2. Data were synthesized narratively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: AI models outperformed traditional triage systems (AUC often >0.90). In clinical interpretation of AUC, its limitations in imbalanced datasets should be considered, and metrics such as PPV, NPV, and AUPRC should also be reported. For instance, despite an acceptable AUC, ChatGPT 4.0 led to significant over-triage due to low specificity (18.2%). However, risks of algorithmic bias and challenges of integrating AI with real-world clinical workflows remain major implementation barriers. User resistance and the need for continuous ethical oversight were also identified.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: AI holds potential to improve emergency triage, but current evidence is largely based on retrospective single-center studies. Clinical implementation should be gradual, starting in high-risk domains (e.g., sepsis screening), and supported by continuous ethical oversight.

articles.title: Dynamics of Ultrasound Findings in Acute Cholecystitis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Abdominal ultrasound is the first-line imaging modality for diagnosing acute cholecystitis. While sonographic criteria for acute cholecystitis are well established, their temporal dynamics and correlation with disease severity remain poorly understood. This study aimed to explore the time course of ultrasound findings in acute cholecystitis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Between November 2017 and October 2018, patients admitted with acute cholecystitis fulfilling the Tokyo Guidelines were prospectively enrolled. All patients received standard care and underwent an initial abdominal ultrasound at admission. Daily follow-up scans were planned until cholecystectomy or discharge. Patients with at least two ultrasound exams were included in the final analysis. Parameters assessed included gallbladder wall thickness and volume, as well as mural and pericholecystic edema. All exams followed a standardized protocol and were performed by certified ultrasound specialists.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 120 patients were enrolled. Of these, 88 underwent at least one ultrasound examination, and 37 received two or more scans and were included in the final analysis. Gallbladder wall edema was present in all but one case and remained stable over time. Mean gallbladder wall thickness and volume showed minimal changes, with a slight reduction in volume during the 1st days. Substantial intraindividual variability in gallbladder volume and wall thickness was observed, independent of disease severity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Sonographic criteria for acute cholecystitis remain stable over time, suggesting that the timing of ultrasound does not affect diagnostic accuracy. However, substantial individual variability limits their use for risk scoring or severity grading, highlighting the need for complementary diagnostic approaches.

articles.title: Anticipating a new pandemic; what to expect for musculoskeletal extremity injuries at the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The rapid, extensive spread of COVID-19 had a profound impact on our healthcare system. The imposed restrictions by the governments impacted the incidence of musculoskeletal injuries. Comparative data on number of patients, types of injuries, underlying trauma mechanisms, and proportion of operative treatment in musculoskeletal extremity injuries can be of value to healthcare facilities when preparing for potential future pandemics, providing valuable insights into various crucial aspects of healthcare management, encompassing ED-management, operation room planning, surgical and orthopedic floor management, and out-patient clinic management.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Count data for this retrospective study was gathered in a large urban teaching hospital and level 2 trauma center in the Netherlands during calendar weeks 11-18 in the pre-pandemic years 2018/2019 and pandemic year 2020 for adults and children. Types of injury were classified into eight distinct anatomic regions: shoulder/upper arm, elbow, lower arm/wrist, hand/finger, knee, lower leg, ankle, and foot.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the years 2018, 2019, and 2020, a total of 1651, 1877, and 950 patients presented to the ED with musculoskeletal extremity injuries. In comparison to the pre-pandemic years 2018 and 2019 there was a decline of 701 patients (43 % reduction) and 927 patients (49 % reduction). The reduction was greater among children than adults. The decline in sports-related injuries is partially offset by injuries caused by other trauma mechanisms. A significant difference (P = 0.005) was observed for operative treatment in the region of "hand/finger" (7 % vs 13 %).

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The pandemic resulted in a significant decrease of patients visiting the ED with musculoskeletal extremity injuries. The overall surgical operation rate remains comparable to pre-pandemic years, leading to a considerable reduction in the absolute number of patients requiring surgical treatment. This information can be valuable for hospitals in reallocating healthcare staff to provide essential care for patients in a future pandemic with governmental restrictions.

articles.title: Advancement in Use of Point-of-care Ultrasound in Pediatric Emergency Medicine in Israel: A Survey Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) adoption has increased at different rates in different regions. We measured the effect of POCUS training activities on self-confidence and on barriers limiting use among pediatric emergency physicians in Israel from 2019 to 2024.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We surveyed physicians who were certified as of August 2024. Statistical analysis used SPSS20.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 2019, 48% used POCUS daily and 30% several times weekly, versus 72% and 21% in 2024 (P = 0.01). On a Likert scale of 1-5, there was less agreement with statements that lack of training opportunities and lack of self-confidence in POCUS ability were impediments to use (4 vs. 2 and 4 vs. 3 respectively, P < 0.001), and that ultrasound machine availability was an impediment to use (2 vs. 1, P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Didactic videoconferences, in-person training courses, and obligatory POCUS experience and knowledge for pediatric emergency medicine board certification have increased POCUS development in Israel.

articles.title: Role of 'Community Grief Counsellors' in Enhancing Eye Donations.
articles.journal_full: Nepalese journal of ophthalmology : a biannual peer-reviewed academic journal of the Nepal Ophthalmic Society : NEPJOPH

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Corneal blindness remains a major public health concern, with a persistent shortage of donor corneas despite awareness initiatives. Ambulance drivers and freezer box service providers, due to their close interaction with bereaved families, may influence eye donation decisions; however, their knowledge, attitude, and practices toward eye donation remain underexplored.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To understand the Knowledge, Attitude and Practice (KAP) towards eye donation among ambulance workers and freezer box service providers.

abstract.label: METHODOLOGY
abstract.text: A validated questionnaire containing 19 questions on knowledge, six on attitude and seven on practice patterns was administered to the study population and their responses were analysed.

abstract.label: RESULT
abstract.text: Mean age of the participants was 37.57 years. Among all, 69% of the study population had received at least secondary school education. The study participants had partial knowledge (mean score: 15), fair attitude (mean score: 5.8) and poor practise (mean score: 2.7) pattern towards eye donation. Using Dunn's pairwise comparison test, it was observed that the attitude scores of freezer box workers were significantly lesser in comparison to ambulance drivers (p = 0.001) and owners (p = 0.017).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The study brought to light that active awareness campaigns are required in this cohort and there is considerable potential to improve eye donation if they partner with local eye banks.

articles.title: Distribution and Hospital Information System Acknowledgment Timeliness of Critical Value Reports in a Large Tertiary Hospital: A Retrospective Descriptive Study.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To describe the distribution of critical value reports, departmental patterns, and HIS-recorded acknowledgment timeliness in a large tertiary hospital in 2023 and to identify targets for process optimization.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Critical value reporting is a key healthcare quality and safety process, but whole-hospital evidence on item distribution, departmental variation, and HIS acknowledgment timeliness across high-load settings remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, descriptive, observational study analyzed all consecutive laboratory-related critical value records from the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University in 2023. Records with complete timestamps were included. Variables included test item, department, visit type, specimen collection time, result dispatch time, clinical recipient, and HIS acknowledgment time. HIS acknowledgment time was defined as the interval between result dispatch/reporting and the first documented clinical acknowledgment/response in the HIS. A timely HIS acknowledgment was defined as documented acknowledgment within 15 min; a delayed HIS acknowledgment was defined as documented HIS acknowledgment requiring more than 60 min. Data were analyzed descriptively using median with interquartile range and frequency with percentage.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 53,639 critical value records were analyzed. The highest proportions were for WBC count (21.46%), microbial culture (14.10%), PLT count (12.97%), and cTnI (12.86%). The top departments were the hematology ward (22.13%), ICU (20.65%), and emergency department (17.46%). The overall median HIS acknowledgment time was 35 s (IQR 20-96 s), and the overall timely acknowledgment rate was 94.57%. The highest untimely acknowledgment rates were observed in the emergency department (9.53%), ICU (6.98%), and hematology outpatient clinic (6.39%). The highest delayed acknowledgment rates were observed in the hematology outpatient clinic (2.51%), emergency department (2.15%), and ICU (1.01%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION(S)
abstract.text: HIS-recorded critical value acknowledgment was generally timely, but untimely and delayed acknowledgment clustered in specific high-load departments. These findings can inform process optimization. Because clinical interventions and patient outcomes were not evaluated, no conclusions about patient safety outcomes can be drawn.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT
abstract.text: Nurse managers should ensure clear accountability for critical value acknowledgment, implement unit-level escalation protocols, monitor item- and department-level timeliness dashboards, support mobile alert access, and conduct regular audits and training, particularly in the emergency department, ICU, and hematology outpatient clinic.

articles.title: Rural Cardiovascular Health in Missouri: Needs, Care Gaps, and Resources for a More Connected System.

abstract.text: Missouri's rural health needs are inseparable from cardiovascular health. Nearly one-quarter of Missourians live in nonmetro areas, where rural hospitals, clinics, community health centers, emergency medical services agencies, public health departments, and community organizations anchor care. Yet heart disease is the leading cause of death in Missouri; the 20 counties with the highest heart disease death rates are rural; and recent data show higher rural heart disease and stroke mortality than urban Missouri. Cardiovascular risk is shaped by clinical care, primary care access, transportation, insurance, broadband, food security, medication affordability, and specialty referral networks. Missouri has building blocks: critical access hospitals, rural clinics, federally qualified health centers, the Misouri Time Critical Diagnosis System for STelevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and stroke, heart disease and stroke prevention program, workforce recruitment programs, and rural health transformation initiatives. This article proposes a rural cardiovascular agenda centered on prevention, urgent treatment, recovery, and community-level coordination.

articles.title: Dimensionality of Moral Distress Among Emergency Nurses in a Non-Western Context: A Two-Stage Psychometric Validation.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To evaluate the dimensional structure of moral distress in a non-Western emergency nursing context, cross-validate it in an independent subsample, and establish concurrent criterion-related validity against burnout and turnover intention.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Moral distress predicts burnout and turnover in emergency nursing but is usually analyzed as a single aggregate score, treating structurally distinct ethical conflicts as interchangeable.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Two-stage split-half psychometric study across six university-affiliated emergency departments in western Iran, reported per COSMIN and STROBE. Of 620 eligible nurses, 568 consented (91.6%) and were randomly allocated to exploratory (n = 298) and confirmatory (n = 242) subsamples after listwise deletion (pooled N = 540). Participants completed the culturally adapted 38-item Moral Distress Scale, the Maslach Burnout Inventory, and a turnover intention measure. Both subscales were analyzed by principal axis factoring with parallel analysis; the intensity model was tested by confirmatory factor analysis, compared against a unidimensional alternative, and examined for configural invariance. Hierarchical regression quantified incremental variance in the outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Exploratory analysis yielded congruent five-factor solutions across both subscales (mean Tucker's φ = 0.988 and Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin = 0.955 and 0.943): communication and autonomy conflicts, unprofessional and futile care, systemic and economic constraints, working with incompetent colleagues, and conflicts with family wishes. All 38 items loaded on their expected factor (0.777-0.899) with no cross-loading above 0.111. Confirmatory fit was excellent (χ2[655] = 731.00; comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.991; root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.022; and standardized root mean square residual = 0.034) and held separately in educational and noneducational hospitals. Reliability (α = 0.925-0.963) and convergent validity (average variance extracted = 0.689-0.774) were supported. The dimensions added 49.4%, 40.5%, and 46.6% of variance in emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and turnover intention (all p < 0.001), with communication and autonomy conflicts the strongest correlate throughout (β = 0.274-0.341). A unidimensional model fitted poorly (CFI = 0.415 and RMSEA = 0.176).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Moral distress was better represented as multidimensional than unidimensional. Constrained professional voice was the dimension most strongly associated with workforce vulnerability, identifying it as a priority for organizational attention. Associations are concurrent, invariance was established only at the configural level, and cross-national replication is required.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT
abstract.text: Nurse managers should move beyond aggregate moral distress scores and identify the specific ethical conflict domains that place emergency nurses at greatest risk. Management strategies should prioritize strengthening nurses' professional voice, improving interdisciplinary communication, supporting ethical decision-making, and addressing organizational constraints that limit autonomy. Targeted interventions in these areas may help reduce burnout, improve retention, and create ethically supportive emergency care environments.

articles.title: A daily scrum at the gastrointestinal oncology ward shortens the length of stay, a tertiary center experience.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Multidisciplinary meetings among medical and paramedical staff can limit the length of stay (LOS) of oncology patients during repeated hospitalizations. We applied the scrum methodology to streamline our discharge planning. This framework originated in IT development to address operational challenges and to allow for rapid adaptation. We aimed to assess whether a daily scrum can impact LOS and the readmission rate.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We implemented a daily multidisciplinary meeting, called scrum at the 26 bed- Gastro-intestinal (GI) oncology ward of our tertiary center from October 2022 to July 2023. This daily multidisciplinary debriefing determines the exact medical and paramedical criteria for discharge. We compared outcomes during the intervention to a four-year pre-intervention baseline. We applied a linear model to evaluate whether the scrum reduced the LOS while correcting for case mix.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included a total of 664 GI oncology patients over a 10-month period. The adjusted mean LOS was 4.09 days. After correcting for case mix, LOS decreased significantly during the daily scrum period compared to the four-year pre-scrum baseline (-9.96%, p=0.011). Unplanned readmissions within 30 days from discharge did not increase.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Implementing a daily scrum significantly reduced the length of stay at our oncology ward. The scrum framework provides an effective strategy to optimize bed capacity. It minimizes unnecessary hospital days and reduces the risk of suboptimal patient care.

articles.title: Characterization of Vibration and Sound Exposure during Neonatal Transport: A Scoping Review of Methods and Findings.

abstract.text: Neonatal transport plays a vital role in ensuring that newborns who require specialized medical care can safely access appropriate services. Standard, regionalized transport protocols and equipment are required to improve access, timeliness, and consistency to the level of care provided. A key concern in neonatal transport is the potential exposure of newborns to elevated sound and whole-body vibration from the variety of transport incubators, medical equipment, and the vehicle platforms used in practice. Although international research groups are actively pursuing strategies to mitigate harmful sound and whole-body vibration, characterizing the transport environment remains a critical prerequisite for identifying resonance-driven amplification and informing targeted mitigation. This scoping review explores the methods and findings of vibration and sound characterization studies in neonatal transport. A total of 33 articles were included in this review, 28 of which evaluated vibration and 16 measured sound. The exposure levels of the different modes of transport and positions within the vehicles were compared. With the exception of a single study, sound measurements exceeded recommended limits for transport incubators, and vibration levels commonly surpassed "uncomfortable" thresholds for adults. Current whole-body vibration standards apply only to healthy adults, which results in ambiguity in their application to newborns and emphasizes a critical gap in defining safe exposure limits for neonates. Defining the risks, magnitude, and acceptable limits of these environmental stressors is essential to ensuring safer transport for vulnerable newborns.

articles.title: Beyond E-FAST: Using POCUS to Suggest the Bullet's Injury Path of a Thoracoabdominal Gunshot - Case Report.

abstract.text: Transmediastinal traumatic injuries challenge trauma surgeons due to their potential to involve thoracic and abdominal cavities, requiring rapid assessment for timely interventions. This case report describes a 27-year-old male with a thoracoabdominal gunshot wound, emphasizing the potential role of ultrasound in emergency settings. The patient presented with diminished left-sided breath sounds and stable hemodynamics. Physical examination revealed an entry wound at the sixth intercostal space. With portable X-ray unavailable, ultrasound detected left hemothorax, pneumothorax, and pneumopericardium. The sonographic findings suggested the bullet's trajectory and helped further management. CT confirmed findings, with esophagoscopy and thoracoscopy identifying minor esophageal and pericardial injuries. Discharged three days post-injury, the patient highlights ultrasound's utility in resource-limited settings despite lower sensitivity compared to CT.
